knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-Window Reference Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-memory nonmonotone Armijo reference based on recent objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given iterates \(x_k\), objective values \(f_k=f(x_k)\), and nonnegative memory lengths \(m_k\), define the maximum-window reference
\[
R_k=\max_{0\leq j\leq m_k} f_{k-j},
\qquad 0\leq m_k\leq \min\{m_{k-1}+1,M\},
\]
where \(M\geq0\) is fixed and unavailable negative-index values are excluded. For a descent direction \(p_k\) and \(c\in(0,1)\), a step \(\alpha_k>0\) is accepted when
\[
f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\leq R_k+c\alpha_k\nabla f(x_k)^\top p_k.
\]
When \(M=0\), this family reduces to monotone Armijo acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reference is the largest recent objective value, allowing controlled increases while retaining an Armijo decrease relative to a finite window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\leq R_k+c\alpha_k\nabla f(x_k)^\top p_k\).

notation.meaning: Maximum objective value in the active memory window.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The maximum-window construction is plausible and belongs in this leaf, but it has no cited source. In addition, the recurrence refers to m_{k-1} without separately initializing m_0 or restricting the recurrence to k greater than or equal to 1.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable. At iteration \(k\), let \(d_k\neq0\) satisfy \(\nabla f(x_k)^Td_k<0\), and let trial steps be drawn from \(\{\tau\sigma^h:h\in\mathbb N_0\}\), where \(\tau>0\) and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic nonmonotone Armijo backtracking with a finite memory window.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(M\in\mathbb N_0\), \(c\in(0,1)\), and integers \(m(k)\) satisfying
\[
m(0)=0,\qquad 0\le m(k)\le\min\{m(k-1)+1,M\}.
\]
Define the maximum-window reference
\[
R_k^{\max}=\max_{0\le j\le m(k)}f(x_{k-j}).
\]
The maximum-window backtracking step is \(\alpha_k=\tau\sigma^{h_k}\), where \(h_k\) is the least \(h\in\mathbb N_0\) for which
\[
f(x_k+\tau\sigma^h d_k)\le R_k^{\max}+c\tau\sigma^h\nabla f(x_k)^Td_k.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximum-window reference is the largest objective value among the current iterate and at most a fixed number of recent iterates. Maximum-window backtracking tests geometrically decreasing positive steps and accepts the first one that gives sufficient decrease relative to that maximum. The memory length may grow by at most one per iteration until it reaches its fixed cap. When the cap is zero, the reference is the current objective value and the rule is ordinary monotone Armijo backtracking.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_k^{\max}=\max_{0\le j\le m(k)}f(x_{k-j})\) and \(h_k=\min\{h\in\mathbb N_0:f(x_k+\tau\sigma^h d_k)\le R_k^{\max}+c\tau\sigma^h\nabla f(x_k)^Td_k\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The reference can be written \(R_k^{\max}=\max\{f(x_i):\max(0,k-m(k))\le i\le k\}\).
special_cases_latex: \(M=0\) yields monotone Armijo backtracking.
\(m(k)=\min\{k,M\}\) uses the full available window of width at most \(M+1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: \(R_k^{\max}\ge f(x_k)\), so the acceptable set contains the corresponding monotone Armijo acceptable set.
Every accepted point obeys \(f(x_{k+1})<R_k^{\max}\) because the directional derivative is negative.
boundary_notes: The running maximum need not decrease at every iteration.
This definition does not cover unbounded memory or weighted-average references.

notation.meaning: maximum number of preceding objective values retained

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted-Average Reference Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonmonotone Armijo references formed by recursively weighted objective averages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_k=f(x_k)\), initialize \(Q_0=1\) and \(R_0=f_0\), and choose weights \(\eta_k\in[0,1]\). Define
\[
Q_{k+1}=\eta_kQ_k+1,
\qquad
R_{k+1}=\frac{\eta_kQ_kR_k+f_{k+1}}{Q_{k+1}}.
\]
For a descent direction \(p_k\) and \(c\in(0,1)\), accept \(\alpha_k>0\) when
\[
f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\leq R_k+c\alpha_k\nabla f(x_k)^\top p_k.
\]
Thus \(R_k\) is a convexly weighted average of observed objective values; choosing \(\eta_k=0\) resets the reference to the latest value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recursive weighted average supplies the nonmonotone reference against which an Armijo-type decrease is required.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable at \(x_k\) and \(\nabla f(x_k)^\top p_k<0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\leq R_k+c\alpha_k\nabla f(x_k)^\top p_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recursive weighted-average reference is mathematically coherent and the definition kind fits the leaf, but the precise indexing and weight convention require an authoritative source with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(g_k^Td_k<0\). Let \(\eta_k\in[0,1]\) be prescribed weights.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic nonmonotone Armijo acceptance using the recursive Zhang–Hager-type weighted reference; exact external support was not located in the supplied local sources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(Q_0=1\) and \(C_0=f(x_0)\). For \(k\ge0\), accept \(\alpha_k>0\) when
\[
f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\le C_k+c\alpha_k g_k^Td_k,
\qquad c\in(0,1),
\]
set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and update
\[
Q_{k+1}=\eta_kQ_k+1,\qquad
C_{k+1}=\frac{\eta_kQ_kC_k+f(x_{k+1})}{Q_{k+1}}.
\]
The resulting \(C_k\) is a normalized weighted average of accepted objective values and constitutes the family’s reference value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted-average reference family maintains a positive normalizing weight and a reference that averages the newly accepted objective value with the previous reference. The line search applies an Armijo-type sufficient-decrease inequality relative to the current average. The parameter between zero and one controls how much historical information is retained. Zero memory makes the next reference equal the latest accepted objective value; positive memory permits the reference to differ from the current objective and therefore permits nonmonotone accepted values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k\text{ is accepted}\iff f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\le C_k+c\alpha_kg_k^Td_k\), with \(Q_{k+1}=\eta_kQ_k+1\) and \(C_{k+1}=(\eta_kQ_kC_k+f(x_{k+1}))/Q_{k+1}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(w_k=\eta_kQ_k/(\eta_kQ_k+1)\), the update is \(C_{k+1}=w_kC_k+(1-w_k)f(x_{k+1})\), where \(w_k\in[0,1)\).
special_cases_latex: A constant \(\eta_k=\eta\in(0,1)\) yields geometrically fading historical weights.
immediate_consequences_latex: \(Q_k>0\) for every \(k\).
\(C_{k+1}\) lies between \(C_k\) and \(f(x_{k+1})\).
boundary_notes: The recursion does not coincide with a finite maximum-window reference.
A precise inspectable source supporting the complete recursion was not available among the supplied locator hints.

knowledge_statements.title: Relationships Among Acceptance Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implications and distinctions among common differentiable line-search acceptance predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi'(0)<0\), \(\alpha>0\), and \(0<c_1<c_2<1\). Strong Wolfe acceptance implies standard Wolfe acceptance because
\[
|\phi'(\alpha)|\leq c_2|\phi'(0)|\ \Longrightarrow\ \phi'(\alpha)\geq c_2\phi'(0).
\]
Goldstein acceptance with \(c\in(0,\tfrac12)\),
\[
\phi(0)+(1-c)\alpha\phi'(0)\leq\phi(\alpha)\leq\phi(0)+c\alpha\phi'(0),
\]
implies Armijo acceptance with parameter \(c\). A nonmonotone Armijo rule using any reference \(R\geq\phi(0)\) weakens the corresponding monotone Armijo upper bound. Exact minimization, Goldstein, and Wolfe acceptance are otherwise not mutually equivalent without additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong Wolfe implies Wolfe, Goldstein implies Armijo with the same decrease parameter, and elevated nonmonotone references relax monotone Armijo; the families are not generally equivalent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{strong Wolfe}\Rightarrow\text{Wolfe}\), \(\text{Goldstein}(c)\Rightarrow\text{Armijo}(c)\), and \(R\geq\phi(0)\Rightarrow\text{nonmonotone Armijo is no stronger than monotone Armijo}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Set-theoretic compatibility of standard line-search acceptance predicates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi(\alpha)=f(x+\alpha p)\) for \(\alpha>0\), with \(\phi'(0)<0\). Fix \(0<c_1<c_2<1\), \(0<c<1/2\), and a reference \(R\ge\phi(0)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relations among acceptance predicates at one smooth line-search iteration; algorithmic procedures for finding a member of an acceptance set are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
A_{c_1}=\{\alpha:\phi(\alpha)\le\phi(0)+c_1\alpha\phi'(0)\},
\]
\[
G_c=\{\alpha:\phi(0)+(1-c)\alpha\phi'(0)\le\phi(\alpha)\le\phi(0)+c\alpha\phi'(0)\},
\]
\[
W_{c_1,c_2}=\{\alpha\in A_{c_1}:\phi'(\alpha)\ge c_2\phi'(0)\},
\]
\[
SW_{c_1,c_2}=\{\alpha\in A_{c_1}:|\phi'(\alpha)|\le c_2|\phi'(0)|\},
\quad
A_{R,c_1}=\{\alpha:\phi(\alpha)\le R+c_1\alpha\phi'(0)\}.
\]
Then \(SW_{c_1,c_2}\subseteq W_{c_1,c_2}\subseteq A_{c_1}\) and \(A_{c_1}\subseteq A_{R,c_1}\). Also \(G_c\subseteq A_c\). Exact acceptance is the separate set \(E=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha>0}\phi(\alpha)\); no unconditional inclusion between \(E\) and the inexact sets is part of this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard acceptance families are related by inclusion of their acceptable-step sets. Strong Wolfe implies ordinary Wolfe, and ordinary Wolfe includes Armijo sufficient decrease as one of its conditions. A nonmonotone Armijo test with a reference no smaller than the current objective admits every step admitted by the corresponding monotone Armijo test. Goldstein acceptance implies its upper sufficient-decrease inequality. Exact line-search acceptance is instead defined by minimization of the entire one-dimensional objective and is not automatically identified with any inexact predicate.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\in C^1((0,\infty))\) and the right derivative \(\phi'(0)\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(SW_{c_1,c_2}\subseteq W_{c_1,c_2}\subseteq A_{c_1}\subseteq A_{R,c_1}\) and \(G_c\subseteq A_c\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inclusions mean that satisfying a stronger predicate guarantees satisfaction of every predicate to its right, for the same parameter values and line function.
special_cases_latex: If \(\alpha\in SW_{c_1,c_2}\), then the curvature slope is bounded on both its negative and positive sides.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every strong-Wolfe step has sufficient decrease.
A maximum-window nonmonotone test is a relaxation of monotone Armijo at the same iteration.
boundary_notes: Goldstein and Wolfe sets need not contain one another under arbitrary parameter choices.
An exact minimizer can be excluded by the Goldstein lower inequality.
The relationships compare predicates, not computational cost or convergence guarantees.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(p_k\) be a search direction. Define the line function \(\phi_k(\alpha)=f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\) on a domain \(D_k\subseteq(0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic one-dimensional procedures used inside finite-dimensional line-search methods; both exact minimization and inexact acceptance are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A step-selection algorithm family is a collection of procedures \(\mathscr S\) such that each \(S\in\mathscr S\), given \(\phi_k\), an admissible set \(\mathcal C_k\subseteq D_k\), initial state \(s_0\), and permitted value or derivative oracles, generates trial steps
\[
\alpha_i=T_i(s_i)\in D_k,
\]
updates \(s_{i+1}=U_i(s_i,\alpha_i,\phi_k(\alpha_i),\phi_k'(\alpha_i))\) using only available oracle data, and terminates either with \(\alpha_k=\alpha_i\in\mathcal C_k\) or with a declared failure status. For exact search, \(\mathcal C_k=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in D_k}\phi_k(\alpha)\); for inexact search, \(\mathcal C_k\) is specified by inequalities such as Armijo, Goldstein, Wolfe, or strong Wolfe.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A step-selection algorithm is an oracle-driven one-dimensional procedure attached to a current point and search direction. It generates trial step lengths, evaluates the line function and possibly its derivative, updates its internal state, and stops when a trial belongs to a prescribed acceptance set. Exact procedures use the set of one-dimensional minimizers as their target; inexact procedures use sufficient-decrease and curvature predicates. Bracketing, backtracking, interpolation, and safeguarding describe different state-update mechanisms within this common family.
assumptions_latex: Each update uses only oracle information already obtained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S(\phi_k,\mathcal C_k,s_0)\in\mathcal C_k\cup\{\mathrm{failure}\}\), with every successful output equal to an evaluated or certified acceptable step.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The procedure is a state machine whose terminal successful states are labeled by elements of \(\mathcal C_k\).
special_cases_latex: Backtracking uses a decreasing trial sequence.
Bracket-zoom search first establishes an interval and then refines it.
Exact line search takes \(\mathcal C_k=\operatorname*{argmin}\phi_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: An acceptance family specifies \(\mathcal C_k\), whereas a step-selection algorithm specifies how to locate an element of it.
Different algorithms can implement the same acceptance predicate.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert finite termination without additional regularity and update conditions.
Selection of the multidimensional direction \(p_k\) is outside this object.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(p_k\neq0\), and define \(\phi_k(\alpha)=f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\) on a nonempty step domain \(D_k\subseteq[0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic exact line search on a specified ray or interval; global and explicitly declared local variants are distinguished.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An exact line-search method returns a step
\[
\alpha_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in D_k}\phi_k(\alpha)
=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in D_k}f(x_k+\alpha p_k),
\]
provided this set is nonempty, and sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). If the method is explicitly designated a local exact search, it instead returns a local minimizer of \(\phi_k\) in \(D_k\); that variant must not be conflated with global minimization on the entire ray. Exactness refers to the defining optimization problem, not to a finite-precision numerical tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact line search chooses a step that minimizes the objective restricted to the current search line over a stated step domain. The domain may be the nonnegative ray or a bounded interval. If several global minimizers exist, any of them is an exact step unless a tie-breaking rule is supplied. A method that returns merely a stationary point or a tolerance-based approximation is not globally exact without additional conditions. The next multidimensional iterate is obtained by moving from the current point by the selected scalar multiple of the direction.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in D_k}\phi_k(\alpha)\neq\varnothing\) for a globally exact output.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in D_k}f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\phi_k(\alpha_k)=\inf_{\alpha\in D_k}\phi_k(\alpha)\), with the infimum attained.
If \(D_k\) is convex and \(\phi_k\) is differentiable and convex, an interior step is exact precisely when \(\phi_k'(\alpha_k)=0\).
special_cases_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^TQx-b^Tx\) with \(Q\succ0\) and \(D_k=(0,\infty)\), an interior exact step is \(\alpha_k=-\nabla f(x_k)^Tp_k/(p_k^TQp_k)\).
Derivative-free and derivative-based procedures differ in how they locate the same minimizer set.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(0\in D_k\), then \(f(x_{k+1})\le f(x_k)\).
For an interior differentiable minimizer, \(\nabla f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)^Tp_k=0\).
boundary_notes: Approximate minimization to a numerical tolerance is an inexact implementation unless the tolerance is part of a separately defined acceptance set.
A first positive stationary point need not be the global minimizer on a nonconvex line.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a current point \(x\) and search direction \(\Delta x\), an exact line search selects \[t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\geq0}f(x+s\Delta x).\] It is applicable only when this ray-restricted problem has a minimizer; it is practically attractive when solving the scalar problem is inexpensive relative to computing \(\Delta x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact line search chooses a nonnegative step that minimizes the objective along the ray from the current point in the search direction. The choice requires an attained ray minimum and is attractive when the scalar minimization is cheap relative to direction computation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\geq0}f(x+s\Delta x)

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Free Exact Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bracket-reduction search for a minimizer of the one-dimensional objective without derivative evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a continuous line function \(\phi\), a bracket \([a_0,b_0]\) containing a minimizer, and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). At iteration \(j\), choose two interior points \(u_j<v_j\), evaluate \(\phi(u_j)\) and \(\phi(v_j)\), and discard the exterior subinterval inconsistent with the smaller value: retain \([a_j,v_j]\) if \(\phi(u_j)\leq\phi(v_j)\), otherwise retain \([u_j,b_j]\). Golden-section placement may reuse one evaluation and gives a fixed contraction factor. Stop when \(b_j-a_j\leq\varepsilon\), and output a point \(\widehat\alpha\in[a_j,b_j]\) minimizing the sampled values. No derivative evaluation is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated function comparisons shrink a bracket containing a line minimizer; termination returns an accuracy-controlled approximation without derivatives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\alpha\in[a_j,b_j]\) with \(b_j-a_j\leq\varepsilon\), using only evaluations of \(\phi\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(D=[a,b]\subset\mathbb{R}\) be compact and let \(\phi:D\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous with a nonempty minimizer set \(X_*\). The permitted oracle returns only values \(\phi(\alpha)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Idealized derivative-free exact search on a bounded one-dimensional interval; finite-tolerance golden-section and Fibonacci searches are approximations to this object.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A derivative-free exact search is a value-oracle procedure producing nested nonempty compact intervals
\[
I_0=D\supseteq I_1\supseteq I_2\supseteq\cdots,
\qquad X_*\cap I_i\neq\varnothing,
\]
using only previously queried pairs \((\alpha_j,\phi(\alpha_j))\), such that \(\operatorname{diam}(I_i)\to0\). Its exact output is the unique point
\[
\alpha_*\in\bigcap_{i=0}^{\infty}I_i,
\]
which consequently belongs to \(X_*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in D}\phi(\alpha)\). No derivative value or derivative sign may enter the interval updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A derivative-free exact search uses only evaluations of the one-dimensional objective. It maintains nested intervals that continue to contain a minimizer and whose lengths tend to zero. In the idealized infinite-precision limit, the intervals identify one exact minimizer. Golden-section and Fibonacci searches instantiate the value-only interval-reduction mechanism, although practical finite termination normally returns only an interval or approximate minimizer. The definition requires an assumption such as unimodality or convexity that makes value comparisons sufficient to preserve a minimizing point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigcap_{i\ge0}I_i=\{\alpha_*\}\) with \(\alpha_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in D}\phi(\alpha)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The midpoint sequence \(m_i=(\inf I_i+\sup I_i)/2\) converges to the exact selected minimizer \(\alpha_*\).
special_cases_latex: Golden-section search uses a fixed interval-reduction ratio.
Fibonacci search uses ratios determined by Fibonacci numbers for a prescribed finite evaluation budget.
immediate_consequences_latex: A finite stopping rule \(\operatorname{diam}(I_i)\le\varepsilon\) certifies localization rather than literal exactness.
Derivative availability is neither assumed nor used.
boundary_notes: Without unimodality, convexity, or another minimizer-preserving structure, ordinary value comparisons need not justify discarding a subinterval.
This definition is idealized; floating-point implementations generally return approximate minimizers.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Based Exact Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded derivative-root search for a minimizer of a continuously differentiable convex line objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a continuously differentiable convex line function \(\phi:[a_0,b_0]\to\mathbb{R}\), a derivative bracket \([a_0,b_0]\) satisfying \(\phi'(a_0)<0\leq\phi'(b_0)\), and a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). At iteration \(j\), select a safeguarded interpolation, secant, or bisection trial \(t_j\in(a_j,b_j)\). If \(\phi'(t_j)<0\), set \(a_{j+1}=t_j\) and \(b_{j+1}=b_j\); otherwise set \(a_{j+1}=a_j\) and \(b_{j+1}=t_j\). Stop when \(|\phi'(t_j)|\leq\varepsilon\) or \(b_j-a_j\leq\varepsilon\). In the first case output \(t_j\); in the second case output any chosen point \(\widehat\alpha\in[a_j,b_j]\), such as the sampled point having the smallest objective value. The maintained bracket contains a global minimizer of \(\phi\) on \([a_0,b_0]\), and the interval-width termination criterion places \(\widehat\alpha\) within \(\varepsilon\) of some such minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuously differentiable convex line objective, a safeguarded derivative-root search preserves a bracket containing a global line minimizer and returns either a point with small derivative or a point within the requested bracket-width accuracy of a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns either \(t_j\) with \(|\phi'(t_j)|\leq\varepsilon\), or \(\widehat\alpha\) lying in a minimizer-containing interval of width at most \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Current derivative sign-change bracket containing a global minimizer.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(D=[a,b]\) or \(D=[0,\infty)\), let \(\phi(\alpha)=f(x+\alpha p)\), and suppose \(\phi\) is continuously differentiable on the interior of \(D\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth one-dimensional exact search using derivative information; convexity is imposed when stationarity is used as a sufficient global certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A derivative-based exact search is a procedure permitted to query \(\phi\) and \(\phi'\) whose successful output satisfies
\[
\alpha_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in D}\phi(\alpha).
\]
For differentiable convex \(\phi\), this requirement is equivalently certified by
\[
0\in\partial(\phi+\iota_D)(\alpha_*),
\]
namely \(\phi'(\alpha_*)=0\) for \(\alpha_*\in\operatorname{int}D\), \(\phi'(a)\ge0\) at a finite left endpoint, or \(\phi'(b)\le0\) at a finite right endpoint. A derivative-based search may bracket a change in derivative sign and refine that bracket until it identifies the certified minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A derivative-based exact search locates a global minimizer of the line function while being allowed to evaluate its derivative. For a differentiable convex line function, an interior zero of the derivative is exactly a global minimizer; one-sided derivative signs provide the corresponding endpoint certificates. Thus derivative-root bracketing can replace purely value-based interval reduction. For a nonconvex line function, a zero derivative is only a stationary point and does not by itself establish exact global minimization.
assumptions_latex: The exact output is required to minimize \(\phi\) globally on \(D\).
For the stationarity equivalence, \(D\) is convex and \(\phi\) is convex on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in D}\phi(\alpha)\); under convexity this is equivalent to \(0\in\partial(\phi+\iota_D)(\alpha_*)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an interior minimizer of differentiable convex \(\phi\), exactness is equivalent to \(\phi'(\alpha_*)=0\).
For \(\phi(\alpha)=f(x+\alpha p)\), \(\phi'(\alpha)=\nabla f(x+\alpha p)^Tp\).
special_cases_latex: For a strictly convex quadratic line function, the unique root of \(\phi'\) is the unique exact step.
Newton, secant, and derivative-bisection iterations may serve as locating mechanisms when appropriately safeguarded.
immediate_consequences_latex: At an interior exact differentiable step, the new gradient is orthogonal to the search direction.
Strict convexity makes the exact step unique.
boundary_notes: For nonconvex \(\phi\), derivative stationarity is necessary at an interior minimizer but not sufficient for global exactness.
A small derivative residual defines an inexact numerical criterion, not literal exactness.

notation.meaning: directional derivative along the search line
indicator function of the step domain
convex subdifferential used for the constrained certificate

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(p_k\) satisfy \(g_k^Tp_k<0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic sufficient-decrease backtracking; a bounded variable contraction factor is allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(\bar\alpha_k>0\), \(c\in(0,1)\), and constants \(0<\rho_{\mathrm{lo}}\le\rho_{\mathrm{hi}}<1\). Set \(\alpha^{(0)}=\bar\alpha_k\). While
\[
f(x_k+\alpha^{(i)}p_k)>f(x_k)+c\alpha^{(i)}g_k^Tp_k,
\]
choose \(\rho_i\in[\rho_{\mathrm{lo}},\rho_{\mathrm{hi}}]\) and set
\[
\alpha^{(i+1)}=\rho_i\alpha^{(i)}.
\]
If \(i_k\) is the first index satisfying the sufficient-decrease inequality, return \(\alpha_k=\alpha^{(i_k)}\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtracking begins with a positive trial step and repeatedly contracts it until the Armijo sufficient-decrease inequality holds. Each contraction factor is bounded strictly between zero and one, preventing both vanishingly aggressive and arbitrarily weak contractions. The accepted step is the first successful trial. Fixed-ratio geometric backtracking and safeguarded interpolation are two choices for producing the contraction factors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k=\alpha^{(i_k)}\), where \(i_k=\min\{i:f(x_k+\alpha^{(i)}p_k)\le f(x_k)+c\alpha^{(i)}g_k^Tp_k\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(\phi_k(\alpha)=f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\), the stopping test is \(\phi_k(\alpha)\le\phi_k(0)+c\alpha\phi_k'(0)\).
special_cases_latex: \(\rho_i\equiv\rho\in(0,1)\) gives geometric backtracking.
Safeguarded interpolation chooses variable \(\rho_i\) within fixed bounds.
For Newton and quasi-Newton methods, \(\bar\alpha_k=1\) is customary.
immediate_consequences_latex: The accepted step satisfies monotone decrease because \(c\alpha_kg_k^Tp_k<0\).
If the initial trial is rejected, the immediately preceding trial \(\alpha_k/\rho_{i_k-1}\) violates Armijo.
boundary_notes: Armijo backtracking does not by itself impose a Wolfe curvature condition.
Finite termination relies on differentiability and strict descent.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficient decrease as the sole backtracking acceptance test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States both the failure boundary for an isolated sufficient-decrease test and the acceptance principle enabled by suitable backtracking; it does not assert finite termination or convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sufficient-decrease condition alone does not ensure reasonable progress along a given search direction when candidate step lengths are not selected appropriately. With candidate step lengths generated by a suitable backtracking procedure, sufficient decrease alone may be used to terminate the line search, without the additional condition (3.6b).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sufficient decrease alone need not ensure reasonable progress along a search direction. When trial steps are selected by a suitable backtracking procedure, however, sufficient decrease alone can serve as the line-search termination test, without the additional condition (3.6b).
assumptions_latex: p_k\text{ is the given search direction}
\text{candidate step lengths are generated by a suitable backtracking procedure}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{the sufficient-decrease condition may be used as the sole line-search termination test}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative-curvature direction and curvilinear line-search construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A partial second-order method construction, not a complete algorithm or an unconditional convergence guarantee. The extract does not specify the combination coefficients, search curve, or acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an iterate \(x_k\), a direction of negative curvature is a vector \(p_-\) satisfying \(p_-^{T}\nabla^{2}f(x_k)p_-<0\). When such a direction exists, a line-search method may combine \(p_-\) with the steepest-descent direction \(-\nabla f(x_k)\) and perform a curvilinear backtracking search along the resulting path. The negative-curvature component is introduced to help prevent convergence to a nonminimizing stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-curvature direction has a negative Hessian quadratic form. When one exists, certain line-search Newton methods combine it with the negative gradient and commonly use curvilinear backtracking. The purpose is to help the iteration avoid nonminimizing stationary points, but the extract does not give a complete algorithm or prove unconditional avoidance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{A search construction may combine }p_-\text{ with }-\nabla f(x_k)\text{ and use curvilinear backtracking to exploit the detected negative curvature.}\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Simple Objective Reduction Is Insufficient for GRG Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The extract calls its sufficient-decrease inequality a Wolfe condition, but the displayed condition contains no curvature inequality; the statement therefore records exactly the displayed sufficient-decrease requirement without adding one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the GRG direction $\bar d_k=-\widetilde g_k$, the acceptance test $f(x_{k+1})<f(x_k)$ alone does not guarantee that the iterates converge to a KKT point. One stronger acceptance rule is, for some fixed $\beta\in(0,1)$, $$\widetilde f((x_k)_N+\alpha_k\bar d_k)\le \widetilde f((x_k)_N)+\beta\alpha_k\bar d_k^T\widetilde g_k,$$ equivalently $$f(x_{k+1})\le f(x_k)-\beta\alpha_k\|\widetilde g_k\|_2^2.$$ Thus a trial point is rejected when $f(x_B,x_N)>f(x_k)-\beta\alpha\|\widetilde g_k\|_2^2$. An alternative is to choose initial trial steps satisfying $$\frac{\alpha_k^{(0)}}{\|\widetilde g_k\|}\to0,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{\alpha_k^{(0)}}{\|\widetilde g_k\|}=+\infty.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict objective decrease by itself does not ensure convergence of GRG iterates to a KKT point. The extract proposes either a reduced-gradient sufficient-decrease test or normalized initial steps that vanish but have a divergent sum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x_{k+1})<f(x_k)\text{ alone is insufficient; impose the displayed sufficient-decrease condition or the displayed normalized diminishing-step conditions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected-Gradient Search Path and Acceptance Conditions on a Polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the Euclidean projected-gradient path for linear equality and inequality constraints, together with a two-level sufficient-decrease line-search condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a_i^Tx=b_i\ (i\in E),\ a_i^Tx\ge b_i\ (i\in I)\}
e\varnothing\), let \(f\) be differentiable, and define the Euclidean projection \(P(x)=\arg\min_{z\in X}\|z-x\|_2\). From a feasible \(x_k\), define \(x_k(\alpha)=P[x_k-\alpha
abla f(x_k)]\). Select \(\alpha_k>0\) so that \(f(x_k(\alpha_k))\le f(x_k)+\mu_1(x_k(\alpha_k)-x_k)^T
abla f(x_k)\), and require either \(\alpha_k\ge\gamma_1\) or \(\alpha_k\ge\gamma_2 ar\alpha_k>0\), where \( ar\alpha_k\) satisfies \(f(x_k( ar\alpha_k))>f(x_k)+\mu_2(x_k( ar\alpha_k)-x_k)^T
abla f(x_k)\). Here \(\gamma_1,\gamma_2>0\) and \(\mu_1,\mu_2\in(0,1)\). For the equality-constrained null-space method, if \(Z^TZ=I\), then \(-ZZ^T
abla f(x_k)\) is the orthogonal projected-gradient direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty polyhedron, project the ordinary gradient ray onto the feasible set and search along the resulting piecewise-linear path. The accepted step satisfies sufficient decrease and either a fixed positive lower bound or a lower bound relative to a trial step that fails a second decrease test. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected-gradient line search that expands the initial trial relative to the preceding accepted step and quarters it until sufficient decrease holds. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_k(\alpha)=P[x_k-\alpha\nabla f(x_k)]\) for the Euclidean projection \(P\) onto the nonempty linearly constrained feasible set \(X\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unit-Step Acceptance and Quadratic Newton-Decrement Recurrence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded local convergence result for backtracking Newton iterations on a self-concordant objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let f be self-concordant, let 0<\alpha<1/2, and define \eta=(1-2\alpha)/4. If \lambda(x)<1 and
\[
x^+=x-\nabla^2f(x)^{-1}\nabla f(x),
\]
then
\[
\lambda(x^+)\le\frac{\lambda(x)^2}{(1-\lambda(x))^2}.
\]
If \lambda(x)\le(1-2\alpha)/2, the unit Newton step lies in \operatorname{dom}f and satisfies the Armijo sufficient-decrease condition. In particular, if \lambda(x)\le\eta, backtracking accepts t=1 and
\[
\lambda(x^+)\le2\lambda(x)^2,
\]
so the Newton decrement converges quadratically in this phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For self-concordant Newton iteration, λ(x)<1 implies λ(x+)≤λ(x)^2/(1−λ(x))^2. With Armijo parameter 0<α<1/2, a unit step lies in the domain and satisfies sufficient decrease when λ(x)≤(1−2α)/2. Below η=(1−2α)/4, backtracking accepts the unit step and λ(x+)≤2λ(x)^2, yielding quadratic local convergence.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is self-concordant and }\nabla^2f(x)\text{ is invertible}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda(x)<1\Rightarrow\lambda(x^+)\le\frac{\lambda(x)^2}{(1-\lambda(x))^2};\quad \lambda(x)\le\eta\Rightarrow t=1\text{ is accepted and }\lambda(x^+)\le2\lambda(x)^2.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Backtracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo backtracking with a fixed geometric contraction factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given differentiable \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), a point \(x\), a descent direction \(p\), an initial step \(\bar\alpha>0\), and parameters \(c,\rho\in(0,1)\), initialize \(j=0\) and \(\alpha_j=\bar\alpha\). While
\[
f(x+\alpha_jp)>f(x)+c\alpha_j\nabla f(x)^\top p,
\]
set \(\alpha_{j+1}=\rho\alpha_j\) and increment \(j\). Stop at the first accepted trial and output \(\alpha=\alpha_j\). If \(\nabla f\) is continuous near \(x\) and \(p\) is a descent direction, the loop terminates after finitely many reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from an initial step, multiply by a fixed factor until the Armijo sufficient-decrease inequality holds.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable near \(x\) and \(\nabla f(x)^\top p<0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha=\bar\alpha\rho^j\) is the first trial satisfying \(f(x+\alpha p)\leq f(x)+c\alpha\nabla f(x)^\top p\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in C^1(\mathbb{R}^n)\), \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(g_k^Tp_k<0\). Fix \(\bar\alpha_k>0\), \(\rho\in(0,1)\), and \(c\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The fixed-contraction specialization of smooth Armijo backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the geometric trial grid
\[
\Gamma_k=\{\bar\alpha_k\rho^j:j\in\mathbb N_0\}.
\]
The geometric backtracking exponent and step are
\[
j_k=\min\{j\in\mathbb N_0:f(x_k+\bar\alpha_k\rho^jp_k)\le f(x_k)+c\bar\alpha_k\rho^jg_k^Tp_k\},
\qquad
\alpha_k=\bar\alpha_k\rho^{j_k}.
\]
Thus trials are evaluated in the order \(\bar\alpha_k,\bar\alpha_k\rho,\bar\alpha_k\rho^2,\ldots\), and the first Armijo-admissible member is returned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric backtracking is the fixed-ratio member of the backtracking family. Starting from a positive initial step, it tests the geometric sequence obtained by repeatedly multiplying by one constant between zero and one. The selected step is the first grid member satisfying Armijo sufficient decrease. Its defining feature is the fixed trial grid; replacing the constant ratio by interpolation-generated ratios produces a different backtracking variant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k=\bar\alpha_k\rho^{j_k}\), where \(j_k\) is the least nonnegative integer satisfying the Armijo inequality.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\alpha_k=\max\{\alpha\in\Gamma_k:f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\le f(x_k)+c\alpha g_k^Tp_k\}\), when the grid is ordered from largest to smallest.
special_cases_latex: \(j_k=0\) means the initial trial is accepted.
\(\bar\alpha_k=1\) gives the common unit-step-first variant.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(j_k>0\), then \(\alpha_k/\rho\) fails the Armijo inequality.
The accepted step belongs to the discrete grid \(\Gamma_k\).
boundary_notes: A changing contraction factor is backtracking but not geometric backtracking in this fixed-ratio sense.
The definition does not include interpolation between grid points.

knowledge_statements.title: Interpolation-Enhanced Backtracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo backtracking whose rejected trials generate safeguarded interpolated replacements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(\phi(0)\), \(\phi'(0)<0\), an initial trial \(\alpha_0>0\), \(c\in(0,1)\), and safeguards \(0<\tau_-<\tau_+<1\), evaluate \(\phi(\alpha_j)\). If \(\phi(\alpha_j)\leq\phi(0)+c\alpha_j\phi'(0)\), stop and output \(\alpha_j\). Otherwise construct a quadratic or cubic interpolant using available values and derivatives, and let \(\widehat\alpha_j\) be its predicted minimizer. Set
\[
\alpha_{j+1}=\min\{\tau_+\alpha_j,\max\{\tau_-\alpha_j,\widehat\alpha_j\}\}.
\]
Repeat until acceptance or a prescribed evaluation or minimum-step limit is reached; on reaching a limit, report line-search failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rejected Armijo trials are replaced by safeguarded quadratic or cubic interpolation estimates, with explicit failure limits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output either satisfies \(\phi(\alpha_j)\leq\phi(0)+c\alpha_j\phi'(0)\) or explicitly reports a stopping-limit failure.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi(\alpha)=f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\), where \(\phi'(0)<0\). Fix \(c_1\in(0,1)\) and safeguards \(0<\rho_{\mathrm{lo}}<\rho_{\mathrm{hi}}<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth Armijo backtracking whose rejected evaluations define quadratic or cubic interpolation models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a rejected trial \(\alpha_i>0\), form an interpolation model \(q_i\) satisfying selected available conditions among
\[
q_i(0)=\phi(0),\quad q_i'(0)=\phi'(0),\quad q_i(\alpha_j)=\phi(\alpha_j)
\]
for recent rejected trials \(\alpha_j\). Let \(\widehat\alpha_{i+1}\) be a minimizer of \(q_i\) over positive steps. The safeguarded next trial is
\[
\alpha_{i+1}=\Pi_{[\rho_{\mathrm{lo}}\alpha_i,\rho_{\mathrm{hi}}\alpha_i]}(\widehat\alpha_{i+1}),
\]
where \(\Pi\) denotes interval projection. Trials continue until
\[
\phi(\alpha_i)\le\phi(0)+c_1\alpha_i\phi'(0),
\]
and the first successful trial is returned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interpolation-enhanced backtracking replaces a fixed contraction by a trial predicted from a local polynomial model of the line function. The model uses the origin value and slope together with one or more rejected function values; a quadratic model is available after the first rejection and a cubic model after two suitable rejected values. Safeguards force every new trial to be a controlled fraction of its predecessor. Acceptance remains the Armijo condition, so interpolation changes trial selection rather than the acceptance family.
assumptions_latex: Each interpolation model satisfies its stated value and derivative conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_{i+1}\in[\rho_{\mathrm{lo}}\alpha_i,\rho_{\mathrm{hi}}\alpha_i]\), and termination occurs at the first \(\alpha_i\) satisfying Armijo sufficient decrease.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The projection safeguard is equivalent to clipping the model minimizer below by \(\rho_{\mathrm{lo}}\alpha_i\) and above by \(\rho_{\mathrm{hi}}\alpha_i\).
special_cases_latex: Using \(\phi(0)\), \(\phi'(0)\), and \(\phi(\alpha_0)\) yields the quadratic model and trial in equations (3.57)–(3.58) of the cited source.
Using the origin data and two rejected function values yields a cubic model.
Resetting an unsafe interpolated trial to \(\alpha_i/2\) is a particular safeguard.
immediate_consequences_latex: The trial sequence decreases at every rejection.
Safeguarding prevents a model minimizer from lying too close to either zero or the rejected step.
boundary_notes: The interpolation model need not globally approximate the line function.
Derivative-based cubic interpolation at two nonzero points belongs to the wider trial-interpolation family.

children.title: Bracketed Inexact Searches
children.top_down_role: Search organizations that establish an interval of uncertainty and refine it until an acceptance criterion is met.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi:[0,\alpha_{\max}]\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable with \(\phi'(0)<0\), and let \(\mathcal C\subset(0,\alpha_{\max}]\) be a specified inexact acceptance set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic searches organized into a bracketing phase followed by interval refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A bracketed inexact search consists of two phases. The bracketing phase evaluates trials until it either finds \(\alpha\in\mathcal C\) or constructs endpoints \(a,b\) such that
\[
0\le\min\{a,b\}<\max\{a,b\}\le\alpha_{\max},
\qquad \mathcal C\cap(\min\{a,b\},\max\{a,b\})\neq\varnothing.
\]
The refinement phase maintains this nonempty-intersection invariant, selects safeguarded trials strictly between the endpoints, and replaces an endpoint after each unsuccessful trial. It terminates only when an evaluated trial belongs to \(\mathcal C\). For strong-Wolfe zoom, the maintained bracket additionally satisfies a sufficient-decrease endpoint invariant and an oriented derivative-sign condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bracketed inexact search first finds an interval known to contain acceptable steps and then refines that interval. Each refinement trial is chosen inside the bracket, commonly by bisection or safeguarded interpolation. If the trial is not acceptable, one endpoint is replaced while preserving the fact that the interval contains at least one acceptable step. The method targets an acceptance set such as Goldstein or strong Wolfe rather than the exact minimizer set.
assumptions_latex: The bracketing phase establishes \(\mathcal C\cap(a,b)\neq\varnothing\) after ordering the endpoints.
Every refinement update preserves that invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful output \(\alpha_*\) is an evaluated point satisfying \(\alpha_*\in\mathcal C\); before success, the maintained bracket continues to intersect \(\mathcal C\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The interval is an interval of uncertainty for an acceptable step, rather than necessarily for a minimizer.
special_cases_latex: Goldstein bracketing targets the two-sided Goldstein inequalities.
Wolfe bracket-zoom targets Wolfe or strong-Wolfe inequalities.
Bisection and safeguarded polynomial interpolation are alternative refinement selectors.
immediate_consequences_latex: The acceptance predicate and the interval-update mechanism are logically distinct.
The bracket endpoints need not themselves be acceptable.
boundary_notes: A bracket around a minimizer is stronger than the inexact acceptable-step invariant required here.
Backtracking without a maintained two-sided interval is not a bracketed search in this sense.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an initial uncertainty interval [a_1,b_1] and \delta>0, initialize \lambda_1=a_1+0.382(b_1-a_1) and \mu_1=a_1+0.618(b_1-a_1). If \phi(\lambda_k)\leq\phi(\mu_k), stop with \lambda_k when \mu_k-a_k\leq\delta; otherwise set a_{k+1}=a_k, b_{k+1}=\mu_k, \mu_{k+1}=\lambda_k, reuse \phi(\mu_{k+1})=\phi(\lambda_k), and set \lambda_{k+1}=a_{k+1}+0.382(b_{k+1}-a_{k+1}). Evaluate only the newly introduced observation and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start with observations at 0.382 and 0.618 of the initial interval. Compare their function values, discard the excluded side, reuse the surviving observation and its value, and evaluate one new golden-ratio observation. Stop when the retained side has length at most the prescribed tolerance, returning the indicated surviving observation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize $\alpha_0\in[0,\infty)$, $h_0>0$, $t>1$, $k=0$, and $\phi_k=\phi(\alpha_k)$. Set $\alpha_{k+1}=\alpha_k+h_k$ and evaluate $\phi_{k+1}$. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\phi:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ and let $\alpha^*\in[0,\infty)$ satisfy $\phi(\alpha^*)=\min_{\alpha\ge 0}\phi(\alpha)$. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fibonacci section method: finite-horizon contraction and limiting ratio
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact interval-length bound and limiting Fibonacci ratio. The extract's observation-optimality claim is not formalized because it does not define the admissible comparison class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let F_0=F_1=1 and F_{j+1}=F_j+F_{j-1}. For a horizon n and k=1,\ldots,n-1, place
\[
\lambda_k=a_k+\frac{F_{n-k-1}}{F_{n-k+1}}(b_k-a_k),\qquad
\mu_k=a_k+\frac{F_{n-k}}{F_{n-k+1}}(b_k-a_k).
\]
Under the stated unimodal comparison updates, the uncertainty-interval length satisfies
\[
b_{k+1}-a_{k+1}=\frac{F_{n-k}}{F_{n-k+1}}(b_k-a_k),
\qquad
b_n-a_n=\frac{b_1-a_1}{F_n}.
\]
Consequently, F_n\geq (b_1-a_1)/\delta implies b_n-a_n\leq\delta. Moreover,
\[
\lim_{j\to\infty}\frac{F_{j-1}}{F_j}=\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}=\tau,
\]
so the large-index Fibonacci contraction factors approach the golden-section factor \tau.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fibonacci search positions its observations using ratios of Fibonacci numbers. With the stated unimodal interval updates, the final interval length after the prescribed horizon is the initial length divided by F_n. Thus choosing F_n at least as large as the initial length divided by the tolerance ensures the requested final interval length. Ratios of consecutive Fibonacci numbers approach the golden-section constant, so the corresponding large-index contraction factors approach the golden-section factor.
assumptions_latex: \text{The interval updates use the stated two-case unimodal comparison rule for }k=1,\ldots,n-1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b_n-a_n=\frac{b_1-a_1}{F_n}\leq\delta\ \text{if }F_n\geq\frac{b_1-a_1}{\delta},\qquad \lim_{j\to\infty}\frac{F_{j-1}}{F_j}=\tau.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generic smooth descent iteration and stopping test
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded representation of an unconstrained smooth descent iteration. Satisfying a fixed positive gradient tolerance at one iterate does not by itself imply that gradients tend to zero or that the iterates converge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given $x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n$, a generic descent method generates $x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k d_k$, where $d_k$ is a descent direction and $\alpha_k$ is selected so that $f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)<f(x_k)$. An approximate-stationarity stopping test is $\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\leq\delta$ for a prescribed $\delta>0$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a point in Euclidean space, a generic descent method chooses a descent direction and a step length giving strict objective decrease, then updates the iterate. It may stop when the gradient norm is at most a prescribed positive tolerance, but that finite-tolerance test alone establishes no convergence result.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is differentiable at the iterates}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k,\qquad \|\nabla f(x_k)\|\leq\delta\ \text{is a stopping condition, not a convergence guarantee}

knowledge_statements.title: Goldstein Search Algorithms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bracketed search for a step satisfying the two-sided Goldstein decrease bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi'(0)<0\), choose \(c\in(0,\tfrac12)\), and initialize \(a=0\), \(b=+\infty\), and \(\alpha>0\). If
\[
\phi(\alpha)>\phi(0)+c\alpha\phi'(0),
\]
set \(b=\alpha\). If
\[
\phi(\alpha)<\phi(0)+(1-c)\alpha\phi'(0),
\]
set \(a=\alpha\). Otherwise output \(\alpha\). After an endpoint update, choose the next trial inside \((a,b)\) when \(b<+\infty\), commonly by bisection or safeguarded interpolation; when \(b=+\infty\), choose a larger trial. Stop upon acceptance or a prescribed numerical-failure limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The search brackets steps that decrease too little or too much and refines until both Goldstein inequalities hold.
assumptions_latex: Trial selection remains strictly inside every finite bracket
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi(0)+(1-c)\alpha\phi'(0)\leq\phi(\alpha)\leq\phi(0)+c\alpha\phi'(0)\), or a numerical-failure limit is reported.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bracketed search for a Goldstein-admissible step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi(\alpha)=f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\), with \(\phi'(0)<0\), and fix \(c\in(0,1/2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic inexact line search targeting the two-sided Goldstein condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the Goldstein acceptable set
\[
\mathcal G_c=\{\alpha>0:\phi(0)+(1-c)\alpha\phi'(0)\le\phi(\alpha)\le\phi(0)+c\alpha\phi'(0)\}.
\]
A Goldstein search algorithm generates positive trials and returns only an \(\alpha_k\in\mathcal G_c\). A bracketed member maintains lower and upper trial bounds and classifies a trial as too long when
\[
\phi(\alpha)>\phi(0)+c\alpha\phi'(0),
\]
and as too short when
\[
\phi(\alpha)<\phi(0)+(1-c)\alpha\phi'(0).
\]
It then refines the resulting interval by a safeguarded selection rule until neither failure occurs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Goldstein search seeks a step whose objective value lies between two lines based on the initial value and directional derivative. The upper line enforces sufficient decrease, while the lower line rules out steps that are excessively short. A trial above the upper bound is classified as too long; one below the lower bound is classified as too short. Bracketing or another safeguarded update uses these classifications to choose further trials, and a successful algorithm returns only a step satisfying both inequalities.
assumptions_latex: Every successful termination test checks both Goldstein inequalities.
For a bracketed implementation, updates preserve the existence of an admissible step in the interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k\in\mathcal G_c\), equivalently \(\phi(0)+(1-c)\alpha_k\phi'(0)\le\phi(\alpha_k)\le\phi(0)+c\alpha_k\phi'(0)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The upper inequality is the Armijo condition with parameter \(c\); the lower inequality supplies a lower control on useful step length.
special_cases_latex: Bisection may select the next point of an established bracket.
Safeguarded interpolation may replace bisection without changing the Goldstein terminal predicate.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every Goldstein-accepted step satisfies Armijo sufficient decrease with parameter \(c\).
The two-sided test can exclude an exact line minimizer.
boundary_notes: Goldstein acceptance does not require evaluating \(\phi'(\alpha)\).
The family is distinct from Wolfe search, whose lower-step control is expressed by a curvature inequality.

notation.meaning: Goldstein parameter restricted below one half

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi:[0,\alpha_{\max}]\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, with \(\phi'(0)<0\). Fix \(0<c_1<c_2<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The standard two-phase search for a strong-Wolfe step using expanding trials followed by interval zoom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A Wolfe bracket-zoom algorithm first generates increasing trials \(0=\alpha_0<\alpha_1<\cdots\le\alpha_{\max}\). It accepts \(\alpha_i\) if
\[
\phi(\alpha_i)\le\phi(0)+c_1\alpha_i\phi'(0),
\qquad
|\phi'(\alpha_i)|\le-c_2\phi'(0).
\]
Otherwise it invokes \(\operatorname{zoom}(\alpha_{\mathrm{lo}},\alpha_{\mathrm{hi}})\) when sufficient decrease fails, when \(\phi(\alpha_i)\ge\phi(\alpha_{i-1})\), or when \(\phi'(\alpha_i)\ge0\). Zoom maintains a bracket containing strong-Wolfe steps, chooses a safeguarded interior trial, and updates an endpoint until a strong-Wolfe trial is accepted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Wolfe bracket-zoom family has two phases. The first expands positive trial steps and either accepts a strong-Wolfe step or detects an interval that brackets acceptable steps. The zoom phase repeatedly chooses a safeguarded point inside that interval, checks sufficient decrease and curvature, and replaces an endpoint while preserving the bracket invariants. The procedure stops only at an evaluated step satisfying both strong-Wolfe inequalities.
assumptions_latex: The line function is bounded below along the searched ray when existence is required.
Expansion reaches \(\alpha_{\max}\) in finitely many expansion trials.
Zoom trial points are safeguarded away from ineffective endpoint choices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful output \(\alpha_*\) satisfies \(\phi(\alpha_*)\le\phi(0)+c_1\alpha_*\phi'(0)\) and \(|\phi'(\alpha_*)|\le-c_2\phi'(0)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The curvature test is \(|\phi'(\alpha_*)|\le c_2|\phi'(0)|\).
special_cases_latex: Ordinary Wolfe search replaces the absolute-value curvature bound by \(\phi'(\alpha_*)\ge c_2\phi'(0)\).
Zoom trials may be chosen by bisection, quadratic interpolation, or cubic interpolation.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every successful output satisfies Armijo sufficient decrease.
The bracket phase may finish directly without calling zoom if an expansion trial is already acceptable.
boundary_notes: The arguments supplied to zoom may be oppositely ordered; their roles, rather than numerical order, determine the invariants.
Unsafeguarded interpolation is not required by this family.

notation.meaning: zoom endpoint with the best qualifying sufficient-decrease value

knowledge_statements.title: Wolfe Bracketing Phase
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expansion phase that accepts a Wolfe step or produces an interval for zoom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\phi'(0)<0\), choose \(0<c_1<c_2<1\), set \(\alpha_0=0\), and generate increasing trials \(\alpha_i\). At trial \(i\geq1\), invoke zoom on \([\alpha_{i-1},\alpha_i]\) if
\[
\phi(\alpha_i)>\phi(0)+c_1\alpha_i\phi'(0)
\]
or, for \(i>1\), \(\phi(\alpha_i)\geq\phi(\alpha_{i-1})\). Accept \(\alpha_i\) if \(|\phi'(\alpha_i)|\leq c_2|\phi'(0)|\). If \(\phi'(\alpha_i)\geq0\), invoke zoom on \([\alpha_i,\alpha_{i-1}]\). Otherwise enlarge the trial subject to a maximum step. Report failure if evaluation, finiteness, or iteration limits prevent acceptance or bracketing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing trials either satisfy strong Wolfe or identify endpoints enclosing a region to be refined by zoom.
assumptions_latex: Trials increase subject to a finite maximum-step safeguard
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The phase returns a strong-Wolfe step, an ordered pair of zoom endpoints, or an explicit safeguarded failure.

knowledge_statements.title: Wolfe Zoom Phase
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded interval refinement following Wolfe bracketing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input endpoints \(\alpha_{\mathrm{lo}},\alpha_{\mathrm{hi}}\) supplied by Wolfe bracketing, with \(0<c_1<c_2<1\). Choose a safeguarded interpolated trial \(\alpha_j\) strictly inside their interval. If
\[
\phi(\alpha_j)>\phi(0)+c_1\alpha_j\phi'(0)
\quad\text{or}\quad
\phi(\alpha_j)\geq\phi(\alpha_{\mathrm{lo}}),
\]
replace \(\alpha_{\mathrm{hi}}\) by \(\alpha_j\). Otherwise, accept when \(|\phi'(\alpha_j)|\leq c_2|\phi'(0)|\); if not, reverse the high endpoint when \(\phi'(\alpha_j)(\alpha_{\mathrm{hi}}-\alpha_{\mathrm{lo}})\geq0\), then replace \(\alpha_{\mathrm{lo}}\) by \(\alpha_j\). Repeat until acceptance; report failure if interval, evaluation, or iteration safeguards are exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zoom safeguards interpolation within a Wolfe bracket, updates endpoints by decrease and derivative tests, and stops at a strong-Wolfe step.
assumptions_latex: The endpoints satisfy the bracketing-phase zoom invariant
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The phase returns \(\alpha_j\) satisfying the strong Wolfe conditions or an explicit safeguarded failure.

knowledge_statements.title: Safeguarded Wolfe Trial Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior safeguarding for interpolation-based trials during a bracketed Wolfe search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a Wolfe-search bracket with endpoints \(a<b\), choose a safeguard parameter \(\tau\in(0,1/2)\) and form an interpolation candidate \(\widehat\alpha\) from available values of \(\phi\) and \(\phi'\). Define \(I_\tau=[a+\tau(b-a),\,b-\tau(b-a)]\). If \(\widehat\alpha\) is finite and its interpolation model is well-defined, take \[\alpha_{\mathrm{trial}}=\operatorname{proj}_{I_\tau}(\widehat\alpha).\] Otherwise take \(\alpha_{\mathrm{trial}}=(a+b)/2\). Evaluate \(\phi(\alpha_{\mathrm{trial}})\), and, when required, \(\phi'(\alpha_{\mathrm{trial}})\); return the trial to the Wolfe bracket-update rule. Stop when a trial satisfies the prescribed Wolfe conditions or a declared evaluation or interval-width limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project each valid interpolated Wolfe trial into a strict bracket interior; use the midpoint when interpolation is invalid, then evaluate and update the bracket.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable at every trial requiring a slope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_{\mathrm{trial}}\in[a+\tau(b-a),\,b-\tau(b-a)]\), so every accepted trial remains strictly inside the current bracket.

knowledge_statements.title: Wolfe Search Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure mechanisms for finite bracket-zoom searches seeking weak or strong Wolfe steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<c_1<c_2<1\). Wolfe-search guarantees require a descent slope, sufficient regularity, existence of an acceptable step, and unlimited exact progress. These boundaries are genuine: for \(\phi(\alpha)=-\alpha\), the strong-curvature inequality \(|\phi'(\alpha)|\le c_2|\phi'(0)|\) becomes \(1\le c_2\), so no strong Wolfe step exists. If \(\phi'(0)\ge0\), the usual descent-based existence argument does not apply. A finite implementation may also terminate without a Wolfe step when evaluations fail, its budget is exhausted, or floating-point rounding makes the bracket endpoints or safeguarded trial indistinguishable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Wolfe search can fail without descent, regularity, or an acceptable step, and can terminate computationally through evaluation limits, invalid values, or bracket stagnation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A bracket-zoom procedure cannot guarantee finite successful termination when any stated existence or computational-progress requirement is removed.

knowledge_statements.title: Moré–Thuente Safeguarded Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong-Wolfe line search using staged bracketing and safeguarded interpolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a differentiable ray function \(\phi\), constants \(0<c_1<c_2<1\), a trial \(\alpha_1>0\), and stopping limits, with \(\phi'(0)<0\). Set \(\psi(\alpha)=\phi(\alpha)-\phi(0)-c_1\alpha\phi'(0)\). In stage one, update an interval of uncertainty using values and slopes of \(\psi\) until a trial has sufficient decrease and nonnegative modified slope, or already satisfies the strong Wolfe conditions. Thereafter update the interval using \(\phi\) and \(\phi'\). At every iteration choose a safeguarded cubic, quadratic, or secant trial strictly inside the admissible interval. Return \(\alpha\) when \(\phi(\alpha)\le\phi(0)+c_1\alpha\phi'(0)\) and \(|\phi'(\alpha)|\le c_2|\phi'(0)|\); otherwise report the applicable stopping limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Moré–Thuente search brackets uncertainty in two stages and uses safeguarded interpolation until it finds a strong-Wolfe step or reaches a stopping limit.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable on the explored interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On successful termination, the returned \(\alpha>0\) satisfies both sufficient decrease and the strong Wolfe curvature condition.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi:[0,\alpha_{\max}]\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable with \(\phi'(0)<0\), and fix \(0<c_1<c_2<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Named safeguarded derivative-based line search targeting sufficient decrease and strong curvature; the inspected sources support its target conditions and safeguarded bracketing character at a secondary-source level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A Moré–Thuente safeguarded search maintains trial steps and an interval of uncertainty, selects new trials by safeguarded quadratic or cubic interpolation, and returns only a step \(\alpha_*\in(0,\alpha_{\max}]\) satisfying
\[
\phi(\alpha_*)\le\phi(0)+c_1\alpha_*\phi'(0),
\qquad
|\phi'(\alpha_*)|\le c_2|\phi'(0)|.
\]
Every interpolated trial is restricted to the current admissible interval and bounded away from choices that fail to reduce the interval effectively. Endpoint updates preserve the algorithm’s bracket or interval-of-uncertainty invariants until acceptance or a declared numerical or bound-related failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Moré–Thuente-type search is a safeguarded derivative-based line search for a strong-Wolfe step. It maintains an interval of uncertainty, uses function and derivative data to form quadratic or cubic trial estimates, clips those estimates to safe interior locations, and updates the interval after unsuccessful evaluations. Successful termination requires both sufficient decrease and a small directional derivative relative to the initial slope. Failure statuses must be distinguished from successful acceptance.
assumptions_latex: Function and derivative values are available at trial points.
Interpolation is safeguarded within the maintained interval.
Successful termination checks both stated inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_*\) is reported as successful only if \(\phi(\alpha_*)\le\phi(0)+c_1\alpha_*\phi'(0)\) and \(|\phi'(\alpha_*)|\le c_2|\phi'(0)|\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The curvature condition is \(|\phi'(\alpha_*)|\le-c_2\phi'(0)\) because \(\phi'(0)<0\).
special_cases_latex: A loose search commonly uses a small \(c_1\) and a comparatively large \(c_2\).
Bisection may replace an unsafe interpolation proposal while retaining the bracket.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every successfully returned step satisfies monotone sufficient decrease.
The accepted derivative may be negative, zero, or positive, but its magnitude is controlled.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial interpolation rule for line-search trials
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(I=[a,b]\subsetef{unused}\mathbb{R}\) be replaced here by a genuine interval \(I=[a,b]\subset\mathbb{R}\), and let \(\phi:I\to\mathbb{R}\) be a line function. Suppose values and, when available, derivatives have been evaluated at distinct nodes \(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r\in I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic or cubic model construction for proposing a line-search trial; acceptance is determined separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A trial-step interpolation rule selects a polynomial \(q\) of prescribed degree satisfying available Hermite conditions
\[
q(\alpha_i)=\phi(\alpha_i)\quad(i\in V),
\qquad
q'(\alpha_i)=\phi'(\alpha_i)\quad(i\in D),
\]
with enough independent conditions to determine \(q\). It forms the raw proposal
\[
\widehat\alpha\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in I}q(\alpha)
\]
and returns the safeguarded trial
\[
\alpha_{\mathrm{trial}}=\Pi_{I_{\mathrm{safe}}}(\widehat\alpha),
\qquad I_{\mathrm{safe}}\subseteq I,
\]
where \(I_{\mathrm{safe}}\) excludes unsafe neighborhoods of relevant endpoints. The proposed point is a trial only and must subsequently satisfy the governing line-search acceptance predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trial-step interpolation fits a low-degree polynomial to previously evaluated line-function data and proposes a minimizer of that polynomial. Function-only data with the initial slope can define quadratic or cubic models; function and derivative data at two points define a cubic Hermite model. A safeguard clips or replaces a proposal that lies too near an endpoint or outside the permitted interval. Interpolation chooses where to evaluate next but does not itself accept the step.
assumptions_latex: The interpolation nodes are distinct whenever required for uniqueness.
The supplied value and derivative data determine the chosen polynomial model.
The raw model minimizer exists on the permitted interval.
A nonempty safeguard interval \(I_{\mathrm{safe}}\subseteq I\) is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_{\mathrm{trial}}=\Pi_{I_{\mathrm{safe}}}(\widehat\alpha)\), where \(\widehat\alpha\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in I}q(\alpha)\) and \(q\) satisfies the selected interpolation conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Quadratic interpolation at the origin and one nonzero trial uses \(q(0)=\phi(0)\), \(q'(0)=\phi'(0)\), and \(q(\alpha_0)=\phi(\alpha_0)\).
Cubic Hermite interpolation at two nodes uses their two values and two derivatives.
special_cases_latex: The quadratic proposal based on \(0\) and \(\alpha_0\) is \(\widehat\alpha=-\phi'(0)\alpha_0^2/[2(\phi(\alpha_0)-\phi(0)-\alpha_0\phi'(0))]\) when the denominator defines a minimizing quadratic.
Bisection can be used when an interpolation proposal is unsafe or ill-conditioned.
immediate_consequences_latex: A safeguarded proposal remains inside the permitted trial interval.
Changing the acceptance predicate does not change the formal interpolation conditions.
boundary_notes: The polynomial is a local model and need not majorize or globally approximate \(\phi\).
Degenerate or nonminimizing interpolants require a fallback rule.
The malformed auxiliary token in the ambient interval declaration is explicitly superseded by \(I=[a,b]\subset\mathbb{R}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-slope quadratic interpolation for estimating a stationary trial step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a\ne0\), and suppose \(\phi(0)\), \(g_0=\phi'(0)\), and \(\phi(a)\) are known. The unique quadratic \(q(\alpha)=\phi(0)+g_0\alpha+c\alpha^2\) interpolating \(q(a)=\phi(a)\) has \[c=\frac{\phi(a)-\phi(0)-g_0a}{a^2}.\] If \(c>0\), its unique minimizer is \[\alpha_q=-\frac{g_0}{2c}=-\frac{g_0a^2}{2\bigl(\phi(a)-\phi(0)-g_0a\bigr)}.\] If \(c\le0\), the model has no unique unconstrained minimizer and the trial must be replaced or safeguarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fit a quadratic to two function values and the initial slope; use its stationary point only when the fitted curvature is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(c>0\), \(\alpha_q\) is the unique global minimizer of the interpolating quadratic \(q\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi:I\to\mathbb R\) be a univariate line-search function on an interval \(I\subseteq\mathbb R\) containing distinct points \(0\) and \(\alpha_0\). Assume that \(\phi(0)\), \(\phi'(0)\), and \(\phi(\alpha_0)\) are available.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic line searches using one function value, one directional derivative at the base point, and one additional function value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The quadratic interpolant is the unique polynomial \(q\in\mathbb P_2\) satisfying \(q(0)=\phi(0)\), \(q'(0)=\phi'(0)\), and \(q(\alpha_0)=\phi(\alpha_0)\). Explicitly, \[q(\alpha)=\phi(0)+\phi'(0)\alpha+\frac{\phi(\alpha_0)-\phi(0)-\alpha_0\phi'(0)}{\alpha_0^2}\alpha^2.\] If \(\phi(\alpha_0)-\phi(0)-\alpha_0\phi'(0)>0\), its unconstrained minimizer is \[\alpha_q=-\frac{\phi'(0)\alpha_0^2}{2\bigl(\phi(\alpha_0)-\phi(0)-\alpha_0\phi'(0)\bigr)}.\] A quadratic-interpolation trial step on a permitted interval \(J\subseteq I\) is any minimizer of \(q\) over \(J\); when \(\alpha_q\in J\), it equals \(\alpha_q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic interpolation constructs the unique degree-at-most-two polynomial matching the line-search value and derivative at the base point and the value at one nonzero trial step. When its quadratic coefficient is positive, the displayed stationary point is the model minimizer; otherwise a constrained trial is selected by minimizing the polynomial over the permitted interval.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is differentiable at \(0\), and the three interpolation data are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[q(0)=\phi(0),\qquad q'(0)=\phi'(0),\qquad q(\alpha_0)=\phi(\alpha_0),\] with \(q\) and, when the quadratic coefficient is positive, \(\alpha_q\) given by the displayed formulas.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(q(\alpha)=a\alpha^2+b\alpha+c\), the interpolation conditions are equivalent to \(c=\phi(0)\), \(b=\phi'(0)\), and \(a=[\phi(\alpha_0)-\phi(0)-\alpha_0\phi'(0)]/\alpha_0^2\).
special_cases_latex: For a strictly convex quadratic objective restricted to a line, the interpolant equals the exact restriction and its interior minimizer is the exact line minimizer.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(\phi'(0)<0\) and the fitted coefficient is positive, then \(\alpha_q>0\).
The construction requires no derivative evaluation at \(\alpha_0\).
boundary_notes: A nonpositive fitted quadratic coefficient does not define an unconstrained finite minimizer; an endpoint or safeguarded fallback must then be specified separately.
Quadratic interpolation alone is not an acceptance condition and does not guarantee Armijo, Goldstein, or Wolfe acceptability.

notation.meaning: Real polynomials of degree at most two.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Three-Point Quadratic Interpolation with Bracket Updating
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bracketed one-dimensional quadratic-interpolation procedure using three function values and a prescribed quadratic trial-point formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\varepsilon>0\), an initial three-point bracket \(\{\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3\}\) containing \(\alpha^*\), and the values \(\phi(\alpha_i)\), compute a quadratic-interpolation trial point \(\bar\alpha\). If \((\bar\alpha-\alpha_1)(\bar\alpha-\alpha_3)\ge 0\), replace the bracket using \(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3,\bar\alpha\) and repeat. Otherwise, stop when \(|\bar\alpha-\alpha_2|<\varepsilon\); if this test fails, update the bracket and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from a three-point bracket containing the target minimizer and compute the objective at its points. Repeatedly form the quadratic-interpolation trial point. A trial outside the interval determined by the first and third bracket points triggers a bracket update. A trial inside that interval is accepted when its distance from the middle point is below the tolerance; otherwise the bracket is updated and the process repeats.
assumptions_latex: \bar\alpha\text{ is produced by the prescribed three-point quadratic-interpolation formula}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |\bar\alpha-\alpha_2|<\varepsilon\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{termination};\quad\text{otherwise the bracket is updated and interpolation is repeated.}

Then the sequence \(\{\alpha_k\}\) generated by the specified three-point quadratic-interpolation formula has convergence order \(1.32\).

knowledge_statements.title: Cubic Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-point Hermite cubic interpolation and its real stationary trial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For distinct \(a,b\), let \(f_a=\phi(a)\), \(f_b=\phi(b)\), \(g_a=\phi'(a)\), and \(g_b=\phi'(b)\). The cubic Hermite interpolant matches these four data. Define \[d_1=g_a+g_b-3\frac{f_a-f_b}{a-b},\qquad d_2=\operatorname{sign}(b-a)\sqrt{d_1^2-g_ag_b}.\] When the radicand is nonnegative and \(g_b-g_a+2d_2\ne0\), a stationary point of the interpolant is \[\alpha_c=b-(b-a)\frac{g_b+d_2-d_1}{g_b-g_a+2d_2}.\] It is selected as a minimizing trial only if it is real, lies in the admissible interval, and has positive model second derivative there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cubic matching values and slopes at two points yields a closed-form stationary trial, accepted only when real, admissible, and locally minimizing.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is differentiable at distinct points \(a\) and \(b\).
The displayed square root and denominator define a finite real number.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed \(\alpha_c\) is a stationary point of the two-point cubic Hermite interpolant.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cubic interpolation from two rejected trial values
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi:I\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable at \(0\), and let \(\alpha_0,\alpha_1\in I\setminus\{0\}\) be distinct trial steps. Suppose \(\phi(0)\), \(\phi'(0)\), \(\phi(\alpha_0)\), and \(\phi(\alpha_1)\) are known.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Function-value-oriented smooth backtracking in which the derivative is known only at the base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The cubic interpolant is the unique polynomial \(c\in\mathbb P_3\) satisfying \[c(0)=\phi(0),\quad c'(0)=\phi'(0),\quad c(\alpha_0)=\phi(\alpha_0),\quad c(\alpha_1)=\phi(\alpha_1).\] It has the form \(c(\alpha)=a\alpha^3+b\alpha^2+\phi'(0)\alpha+\phi(0)\), where \[\begin{pmatrix}a\\b\end{pmatrix}=\frac{1}{\alpha_0^2\alpha_1^2(\alpha_1-\alpha_0)}\begin{pmatrix}\alpha_0^2&-\alpha_1^2\\-\alpha_0^3&\alpha_1^3\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}\phi(\alpha_1)-\phi(0)-\alpha_1\phi'(0)\\\phi(\alpha_0)-\phi(0)-\alpha_0\phi'(0)\end{pmatrix}.\] A cubic-interpolation trial step on \(J\subseteq I\) is a minimizer of \(c\) over \(J\); an interior candidate is a root of \(3a\alpha^2+2b\alpha+\phi'(0)=0\) having positive second derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cubic interpolation constructs the unique degree-at-most-three polynomial matching the base value and derivative and two distinct nonzero trial values. The next trial is a constrained minimizer of this polynomial; an interior candidate must be a stationary point at which the polynomial has positive curvature.
assumptions_latex: All four interpolation data are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a unique \(c\in\mathbb P_3\) satisfying the four interpolation conditions, with coefficients \(a,b\) given by the displayed linear formula.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The coefficient pair \((a,b)\) is equivalently the unique solution of \(a\alpha_i^3+b\alpha_i^2=\phi(\alpha_i)-\phi(0)-\alpha_i\phi'(0)\) for \(i=0,1\).
special_cases_latex: If \(a=0\), the fitted model degenerates to the corresponding quadratic interpolant.
In backtracking, \(\alpha_0\) and \(\alpha_1\) may be the two most recent rejected trial steps.
immediate_consequences_latex: Only one directional derivative, \(\phi'(0)\), is required.
Minimizing over a compact safeguard interval \(J\) always yields at least one model trial.
boundary_notes: The formula does not select between multiple stationary points without a minimum and interval test.
An interpolated minimizer must normally be safeguarded before use; model minimization does not itself establish line-search acceptability.

notation.meaning: Real polynomials of degree at most three.
Permitted interval for the next trial step.
