knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Related Stationarity Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity consequence of Zoutendijk summability under uniform angle control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume the Zoutendijk series satisfies \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\cos^2	heta_k\lVert
abla f(x_k)Vert^2<\infty\). If the directions are uniformly gradient-related in angle, namely there exists \(\delta>0\) such that \(\cos	heta_k\ge\delta\) for every \(k\), then \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert
abla f(x_k)Vert^2<\infty,\qquad \lim_{k	o\infty}\lVert
abla f(x_k)Vert=0.\] Hence every accumulation point at which \(
abla f\) is continuous is first-order stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zoutendijk summability plus a uniform angle bound forces gradient norms to zero and makes every accumulation point stationary.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla f\) is continuous at any accumulation point considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert\to0\), and every accumulation point \(x_*\) satisfies \(\nabla f(x_*)=0\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and let nonzero \(p_k\) satisfy \(g_k^Tp_k<0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth line-search sequences for which Zoutendijk summability is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The directions are uniformly gradient-related in the angle sense if \(\exists\delta>0\) such that \(-g_k^Tp_k\geq\delta\|g_k\|\|p_k\|\) for every nonstationary iterate. The associated full stationarity consequence is \(\|g_k\|\to0\). A weaker subsequential gradient-related condition requires an infinite index set \(K\) and \(\delta>0\) with \(\cos\theta_k\geq\delta\) for \(k\in K\); paired with Zoutendijk summability, it yields \(\liminf_k\|g_k\|=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly gradient-related directions make a fixed positive angle with the negative gradient and, with Zoutendijk summability, force the entire gradient sequence to zero. If the angle bound holds only on an infinite subsequence, the canonical conclusion is the weaker statement that gradient norms have zero lower limit.
assumptions_latex: For the full conclusion, \(\cos\theta_k\geq\delta>0\) for all nonstationary indices.
For the subsequential conclusion, the same bound holds on an infinite index set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform angle-relatedness implies \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\|g_k\|=0\); infinite-subsequence angle-relatedness implies \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|g_k\|=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Uniform gradient-relatedness is \(\inf_k[-g_k^Tp_k/(\|g_k\|\|p_k\|)]>0\).
special_cases_latex: Steepest descent is uniformly gradient-related with \(\delta=1\).
Positive-definite Newton-like directions with uniformly bounded matrix condition numbers have a uniform angle bound.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every accumulation point at which the gradient is continuous is stationary when the full gradient-norm conclusion holds.
boundary_notes: First-order stationarity does not distinguish local minima from saddles or maxima.
A mere descent condition without a uniform angle bound is insufficient for the full conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Zoutendijk Framework Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Angle degeneration prevents summability alone from implying stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Zoutendijk summability does not by itself imply vanishing gradients. In \(\mathbb{R}^2\), set \(g_k=(1,0)\) and \(p_k=(-1,2^k)\). Then \(g_k^{\mathsf T}p_k=-1<0\), so every \(p_k\) is a descent direction for gradient \(g_k\), while \[\cos^2\theta_k=\frac{1}{1+4^k},\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\cos^2\theta_k\lVert g_k\rVert^2<\infty.\] Nevertheless, \(\lVert g_k\rVert=1\) for all \(k\). Therefore an angle condition or another gradient-relatedness hypothesis is essential for deriving stationarity from the Zoutendijk series alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If descent directions become nearly orthogonal to the negative gradient, the Zoutendijk series may converge while gradient norms remain bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k\cos^2\theta_k\lVert g_k\rVert^2<\infty\) but \(\lVert g_k\rVert\not\to0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity boundary of the Zoutendijk framework
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) for a smooth objective \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary object distinguishing the hypotheses and conclusions of the classical finite-dimensional smooth Zoutendijk result from nearby theories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The classical Zoutendijk validity regime is the class of tuples \((f,x_0,\{p_k\},\{\alpha_k\})\) for which: \(f\) is bounded below; \(f\in C^1\) on an open neighborhood of \(\mathcal L=\{x:f(x)\leq f(x_0)\}\); \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz there; \(g_k^Tp_k<0\); and each \(\alpha_k\) obeys a Wolfe-type rule that implies angle-weighted decrease. Its canonical conclusion boundary is first-order: \(\sum_k\cos^2\theta_k\|g_k\|^2<\infty\), not convergence of iterates or convergence to minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classical framework applies to lower-bounded, continuously differentiable finite-dimensional objectives with a Lipschitz gradient near the initial level set, descent directions, and suitable Wolfe-type steps. Its guaranteed endpoint is angle-weighted gradient summability and derived first-order stationarity, not convergence of the iterates to a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The objective and iteration satisfy every condition defining the stated validity regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The framework guarantees only the angle-weighted summability conclusion unless additional direction, compactness, or second-order hypotheses are supplied.
special_cases_latex: Goldstein and strong Wolfe acceptance lie within the nearby supported family because they yield analogous Zoutendijk conditions.
immediate_consequences_latex: Claims about convergence to a local minimum require information beyond this regime, such as negative-curvature handling or convexity.
boundary_notes: Nonsmooth objectives require a different stationarity measure and are excluded.
Stochastic or noisy function and gradient evaluations are excluded from the classical deterministic statement.
If \(\nabla f\) is not Lipschitz on the relevant neighborhood, the classical decrease estimate is unavailable.
If directions approach orthogonality with \(-g_k\), the framework may yield no full gradient convergence.

notation.meaning: Initial level set defining the relevant smoothness region.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order global convergence in smooth unconstrained optimization; global refers to initialization, not convergence to a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A global convergence route is a set of verifiable step and direction conditions implying one of the stationarity predicates \(G_{\mathrm{full}}:\|g_k\|\to0\), \(G_{\mathrm{sub}}:\liminf_k\|g_k\|=0\), or \(G_{\mathrm{acc}}:\nabla f(\bar x)=0\) for every accumulation point \(\bar x\). Canonical routes include exact line minimization with gradient-related directions, Armijo backtracking with controlled directions, and Wolfe-type acceptance combined with Zoutendijk angle control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A line-search global convergence route is a specified combination of step acceptance and search-direction quality that guarantees full-sequence, subsequential, or accumulation-point first-order stationarity from arbitrary admissible starting points. Exact, Armijo-backtracking, and Wolfe-based analyses are distinct canonical routes.
assumptions_latex: The objective has the smoothness and lower-boundedness required by the selected route.
Every generated direction and step satisfies that route's quantitative conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected route implies at least one of \(G_{\mathrm{full}}\), \(G_{\mathrm{sub}}\), or \(G_{\mathrm{acc}}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For bounded iterate sequences and continuous \(\nabla f\), \(G_{\mathrm{full}}\) implies \(G_{\mathrm{acc}}\).
special_cases_latex: Uniformly angle-related directions plus Wolfe steps give \(G_{\mathrm{full}}\).
An infinite subsequence of uniformly good angles can give \(G_{\mathrm{sub}}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition makes the strength of a global convergence statement explicit rather than treating all stationarity conclusions as identical.
boundary_notes: None of the three predicates alone asserts convergence to a global minimizer.
Iterate convergence requires additional assumptions such as isolated stationary points, convexity, or an appropriate error-bound property.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Line-Search Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global first-order convergence of steepest descent with exact ray minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable with globally \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient for some \(L>0\), and suppose \(f\) is bounded below on the initial level set \(\mathcal L=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}\). For each \(k\in\mathbb{N}_0\), define \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), choose an exact ray minimizer \(\alpha_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\ge0}f(x_k-\alpha g_k)\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_kg_k\). Then \[f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge\frac{1}{2L}\lVert g_k\rVert^2,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert g_k\rVert^2<\infty,\] and consequently \(\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a lower-bounded objective with a globally Lipschitz gradient, steepest descent with an existing exact minimizer on every search ray produces square-summable gradient norms converging to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuously differentiable and \(\nabla f\) is globally \(L\)-Lipschitz for some \(L>0\).
\(f\) is bounded below on \(\mathcal L=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}\).
For every \(k\in\mathbb{N}_0\), the set \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\ge0}f(x_k-\alpha\nabla f(x_k))\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert^2<\infty\) and \(\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert\to0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The step \(\alpha_k\) is exact if \(\alpha_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\geq0}f(x_k+\alpha d_k)\); a commonly used stationary exact variant takes \(\alpha_k=\min\{\alpha>0:\nabla f(x_k+\alpha d_k)^Td_k=0\}\). The iteration has exact-line-search global stationarity convergence if its exact steps and direction assumptions imply that every accumulation point is stationary, or, under a uniform angle condition and suitable curvature bounds, that \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact line search minimizes the objective over the nonnegative search ray; a standard variant selects the first positive stationary point on that ray. Exact-line-search convergence means that, with the stated direction and regularity conditions, accumulation points are stationary or the complete gradient sequence tends to zero.
assumptions_latex: Each ray subproblem has the selected exact solution.
The objective and direction sequence satisfy the compactness, boundedness, and smoothness conditions required for the chosen stationarity conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact-line-search global stationarity is \(\nabla f(\bar x)=0\) for every accumulation point \(\bar x\), or the stronger \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to0\) under uniform direction quality.
equivalent_formulations_latex: At an interior differentiable ray minimizer, \(\nabla f(x_{k+1})^Td_k=0\).
special_cases_latex: For a strongly convex quadratic and conjugate directions, exact line search recovers the classical finite-dimensional conjugate-gradient structure.
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact minimization gives \(f(x_{k+1})\leq f(x_k)\).
Consecutive gradients are orthogonal to the preceding direction whenever the selected minimizer is interior.
boundary_notes: Exact line search concerns minimization on a ray, not global minimization in \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
Exact ray minimization may be computationally impractical and need not produce iterate convergence without additional assumptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Armijo–Backtracking Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global first-order convergence of steepest descent with fixed-start backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable with globally \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient for some \(L>0\), and suppose \(f\) is bounded below on the initial level set \(\mathcal L=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}\). For each \(k\in\mathbb{N}_0\), set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_kg_k\), where \(\alpha_k\) is obtained by backtracking from a fixed \(\bar\alpha>0\) with factor \(\rho\in(0,1)\) until \[f(x_k-\alpha_kg_k)\le f(x_k)-c_1\alpha_k\lVert g_k\rVert^2\] holds for a fixed \(c_1\in(0,1)\). Then \[\alpha_k\ge \rho\min\!\left\{\bar\alpha,\frac{2(1-c_1)}{L}\right\}>0,\] and consequently \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert g_k\rVert^2<\infty,\qquad \lVert g_k\rVert\to0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a lower-bounded objective with a globally Lipschitz gradient, steepest descent using fixed-start Armijo backtracking has uniformly positive accepted steps and gradient norms converging to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuously differentiable and \(\nabla f\) is globally \(L\)-Lipschitz for some \(L>0\).
\(f\) is bounded below on \(\mathcal L=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert^2<\infty\) and \(\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert\to0\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(g_k^Tp_k<0\). Fix \(\bar\alpha>0\), \(c\in(0,1)\), and \(\rho\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic smooth unconstrained descent with geometric backtracking and quantitative direction quality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Armijo-backtracking step is \(\alpha_k=\bar\alpha\rho^{m_k}\), where \(m_k\) is the least nonnegative integer satisfying \(f(x_k+\bar\alpha\rho^{m_k}p_k)\leq f(x_k)+c\bar\alpha\rho^{m_k}g_k^Tp_k\). The iteration has Armijo-backtracking global stationarity convergence when, under its stated smoothness and gradient-related direction assumptions, either a stationary iterate occurs or \(\|g_k\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Armijo backtracking chooses the first geometrically reduced trial step that achieves sufficient decrease. Its canonical convergence route combines finite acceptance with directions that remain quantitatively related to the negative gradient, yielding either finite arrival at stationarity or convergence of gradient norms to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^1\) and its gradient has the regularity required on the relevant level set.
The directions satisfy a uniform angle condition, and any required norm-scaling bounds are uniform.
The objective values are bounded below along the generated sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each \(k\), \(m_k<\infty\); under the global-route assumptions, either \(g_k=0\) for some \(k\) or \(\|g_k\|\to0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The accepted step is the largest member of \(\{\bar\alpha\rho^m:m\in\mathbb N_0\}\) satisfying the Armijo inequality.
special_cases_latex: For steepest descent, \(p_k=-g_k\), the angle condition is automatic.
A variable contraction factor is admissible when it remains in a fixed interval \([\rho_{\mathrm{lo}},\rho_{\mathrm{hi}}]\subset(0,1)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The accepted step is not arbitrarily smaller than the preceding rejected geometric trial.
boundary_notes: Armijo decrease alone, without controlled trial generation and direction quality, does not imply global stationarity.
The definition is monotone and does not cover reference-value nonmonotone searches.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Curvature-Vanishing Convergence of Second-Order Armijo Backtracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic first- and second-order model decrease for bounded descent-pair sequences accepted by the second-order Armijo rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be twice continuously differentiable on an open set $\mathcal D$, and suppose that $L(x_0)=\{x\in\mathcal D:f(x)\leq f(x_0)\}$ is compact. Let $g_k=\nabla f(x_k)$ and $G_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)$. Suppose $\{\|s_k\|\}$ and $\{\|d_k\|\}$ are bounded, and for fixed $\rho,\gamma\in(0,1)$ the iterates satisfy $x_{k+1}=x_k+\gamma^{2i_k}s_k+\gamma^{i_k}d_k$ together with $f(x_{k+1})\leq f(x_k)+\rho\gamma^{2i_k}[g_k^Ts_k+\tfrac12d_k^TG_kd_k]$. Then $g_k^Ts_k\to0$ and $d_k^TG_kd_k\to0$ as $k\to\infty$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice continuously differentiable objective with a compact initial level set, if both direction sequences are bounded and every iterate is accepted by the second-order Armijo curve rule, then the first-order descent product and the negative-curvature quadratic product both converge to zero.
assumptions_latex: $f\in C^2(\mathcal D)$ for an open $\mathcal D\subset\mathbb R^n$.
$x_0\in\mathcal D$ and $L(x_0)=\{x\in\mathcal D:f(x)\leq f(x_0)\}$ is compact.
$x_{k+1}=x_k+\gamma^{2i_k}s_k+\gamma^{i_k}d_k$ and the second-order Armijo inequality holds at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lim_{k\to\infty}g_k^Ts_k=0,\qquad \lim_{k\to\infty}d_k^TG_kd_k=0.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} is twice continuously differentiable on an open set D; L=\{x\mid f(x)\leq f(x_0)\} is a compact subset of D; the Goldfarb second-order Armijo algorithm uses an admissible sequence of descent pairs \{(s_k,d_k)\} satisfying -s_k^Tg_k\geq c_1\|s_k\|^2 and s_k^TG_ks_k\leq c_2\|s_k\|^2 for 0<c_1,c_2<\infty; and f has only finitely many stationary points in L. Then x_k\to x^* for some x^* satisfying g(x^*)=0 and G(x^*)\succeq0. Moreover, if G_k\neq0 for infinitely many k, then G(x^*) has at least one zero eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the preceding Goldfarb convergence assumptions and finiteness of the stationary points in the level set, the entire iterate sequence converges to a point with zero gradient and positive-semidefinite limiting curvature. If G_k is nonzero for infinitely many iterations, the limiting matrix also has a zero eigenvalue.
assumptions_latex: L=\{x\mid f(x)\leq f(x_0)\}\text{ is a compact subset of }D
\{(s_k,d_k)\}\text{ is an admissible sequence of descent pairs used by the second-order Armijo algorithm}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\to x^*,\qquad g(x^*)=0,\qquad G(x^*)\succeq0;\qquad \bigl(G_k\neq0\text{ for infinitely many }k\bigr)\Rightarrow 0\in\operatorname{spec}(G(x^*))

knowledge_statements.title: Nonmonotone Line-Search Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-memory nonmonotone Armijo globalization with uniformly gradient-related directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable and bounded below on the initial level set, with Lipschitz gradient there. Set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and suppose \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\le-c\lVert g_k\rVert^2\) and \(\lVert d_k\rVert\le C\lVert g_k\rVert\) for constants \(c,C>0\). For fixed \(M\ge1\) and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), choose \(\alpha_k\) by geometric backtracking until
\[
f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\le \max_{0\le j\le\min\{k,M-1\}}f(x_{k-j})+\sigma\alpha_k g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k.
\]
Then every backtracking search terminates, and the iterates \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\) satisfy \(\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-memory nonmonotone Armijo search with uniformly gradient-related directions is well defined and drives the gradient norm to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable, bounded below on the relevant level set, and has Lipschitz gradient there.
\(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\le-c\lVert g_k\rVert^2\) and \(\lVert d_k\rVert\le C\lVert g_k\rVert\).
Backtracking uses fixed finite memory and a fixed geometric contraction factor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert\to0\).

notation.meaning: Number of objective values retained by the nonmonotone reference maximum.

The finite-memory nonmonotone reference rule and the strong conclusion that the full gradient sequence converges to zero require an authoritative theorem-level source locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-memory nonmonotone backtracking with gradient-related directions on a compact initial level set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(0\leq m(k)\leq\min\{m(k-1)+1,M\}\), set \(R_k=\max_{0\leq j\leq m(k)}f(x_{k-j})\), and let \(\alpha_k=\tau\sigma^{h_k}\), where \(h_k\) is the least \(h\in\mathbb N_0\) satisfying \(f(x_k+\tau\sigma^hd_k)\leq R_k+\gamma\tau\sigma^h\nabla f(x_k)^Td_k\). The route is convergent when compactness of the initial level set and constants \(c_1,c_2>0\) with \(g_k^Td_k\leq-c_1\|g_k\|^2\) and \(\|d_k\|\leq c_2\|g_k\|\) ensure that every accumulation point is stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-memory nonmonotone line search compares a trial value with the maximum of a bounded window of recent objective values plus an Armijo slope term. With compactness and uniformly gradient-related, norm-controlled directions, every accumulation point of the generated sequence is stationary.
assumptions_latex: The backtracking exponent is the first one satisfying the finite-memory inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\in\Omega\) for all \(k\), and every accumulation point \(\bar x\) satisfies \(\nabla f(\bar x)=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(M=0\), \(R_k=f(x_k)\) and the rule reduces to monotone Armijo backtracking.
special_cases_latex: A fixed full window \(m(k)=\min\{k,M\}\) satisfies the memory recursion.
immediate_consequences_latex: Individual objective increases are permitted while the finite-memory reference values control long-term progress.
boundary_notes: Unbounded memory is not covered by this finite-memory statement.
The conclusion concerns accumulation points and does not assert convergence of the whole iterate sequence.

children.title: Global-to-Local Transition
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between global acceptance and the eventual behavior of fast local direction methods.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) converge to a stationary point \(x^*\), and suppose a globalization line search tests \(\alpha=1\) before damped alternatives.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth Newton or quasi-Newton line-search methods near a nondegenerate local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A line-search method has a global-to-local transition at \(x^*\) if its globally valid acceptance mechanism produces the sequence from remote starting points, while there exists \(k_0\) such that \(\alpha_k=1\) for every \(k\geq k_0\), so the asymptotic iteration is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\). For Wolfe globalization with \(c_1\leq1/2\), a canonical compatibility condition is \(\|\nabla f(x_k)+\nabla^2f(x_k)p_k\|/\|p_k\|\to0\) near a stationary \(x^*\) with positive-definite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global-to-local transition occurs when a globally safeguarded line-search method eventually accepts every full trial step, after which its behavior coincides with the underlying undamped local method. For Wolfe-globalized Newton-like methods, asymptotic satisfaction of the Newton equation is the canonical compatibility condition.
assumptions_latex: The line search tests and accepts \(\alpha=1\) whenever it satisfies the Wolfe conditions, with \(c_1\leq1/2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists k_0\ \forall k\geq k_0:\alpha_k=1\); if the full steps are then taken, the convergence is superlinear under the cited conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For quasi-Newton directions \(p_k=-B_k^{-1}g_k\), the compatibility condition is the Dennis–Moré directional approximation condition.
special_cases_latex: Exact Newton directions satisfy the residual condition with zero numerator.
Suitable quasi-Newton directions satisfy it asymptotically without requiring full matrix convergence.
immediate_consequences_latex: The globalization ceases to damp the local model once the local regime is reached.
boundary_notes: Convergence to a stationary point is an assumption of this local transition statement, not a conclusion of it.
If the search never tests the unit step first, admissibility need not imply actual unit-step selection.

notation.meaning: Index after which all accepted steps are full steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Eventual Unit-Step Acceptance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Newton transition under an Armijo sufficient-decrease test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be twice continuously differentiable near \(x_*\), with \(\nabla f(x_*)=0\) and \(\nabla^2f(x_*)\) positive definite. Assume the Hessian is Lipschitz near \(x_*\), \(x_k\to x_*\), and \(d_k=-\nabla^2f(x_k)^{-1}\nabla f(x_k)\). If backtracking tests
\[
f(x_k+\alpha d_k)\le f(x_k)+\sigma\alpha\nabla f(x_k)^{\mathsf T}d_k,
\qquad 0<\sigma<\tfrac12,
\]
starting from \(\alpha=1\), then there exists \(K\) such that \(\alpha_k=1\) for every \(k\ge K\). Consequently, the globalization no longer damps the local Newton iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a nondegenerate minimizer, Armijo backtracking with parameter below one half eventually accepts every full Newton step.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla^2f\) is locally Lipschitz and \(d_k\) is the exact Newton direction.
Armijo backtracking starts with \(\alpha=1\) and uses \(0<\sigma<1/2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\alpha_k=1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Damping Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed damping prevents Newton's characteristic superlinear local rate even on a quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be positive definite and \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx\). The Newton direction is \(d(x)=-x\). If a globalization mechanism persistently selects a fixed \(\bar\alpha\in(0,1)\), then
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k+\bar\alpha d(x_k)=(1-\bar\alpha)x_k.
\]
Thus \(\lVert x_{k+1}\rVert=(1-\bar\alpha)\lVert x_k\rVert\): convergence is exactly linear unless an iterate is already zero. Hence eventual removal of nonvanishing damping is necessary for the full-step Newton quadratic rate in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed step smaller than one makes Newton's method only linearly convergent, even for a positive-definite quadratic.
assumptions_latex: Every Newton step is multiplied by the same \(\bar\alpha\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=(1-\bar\alpha)x_k\), so the convergence factor is \(1-\bar\alpha\) and the rate is linear.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent-damping barrier to the local regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) be a line-search Newton-like iteration whose undamped local method corresponds to \(\alpha_k=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic diagnostic for failure of a globalization method to become inactive near a candidate solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The iteration exhibits persistent damping if there exist \(\varepsilon>0\) and infinitely many indices \(k\) such that \(\alpha_k\leq1-\varepsilon\); equivalently, \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\alpha_k<1\). This is a global-to-local barrier because eventual unit-step acceptance fails. A stronger uniform barrier holds when \(\sup_{k\geq k_0}\alpha_k\leq1-\varepsilon\) for some \(k_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistent damping means that accepted steps remain bounded away from one along an infinite subsequence. It blocks eventual unit-step acceptance and therefore prevents direct transfer of a local full-step convergence theorem. Uniform persistent damping means that every sufficiently late step is bounded away from one.
assumptions_latex: The local reference method uses the full step \(\alpha=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistent damping is \(\liminf_k\alpha_k<1\), and it implies \(\neg\exists k_0\ \forall k\geq k_0:\alpha_k=1\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\liminf_k\alpha_k<1\) is equivalent to the existence of \(\varepsilon>0\) and an infinite subsequence \(K\) with \(\alpha_k\leq1-\varepsilon\) for \(k\in K\).
special_cases_latex: A constant damping sequence \(\alpha_k=\bar\alpha<1\) is uniformly persistently damped.
immediate_consequences_latex: A superlinear conclusion whose hypotheses require eventual full steps cannot be invoked.
The accepted iteration differs infinitely often from the undamped Newton-like iteration.
boundary_notes: Persistent damping does not by itself imply divergence or exclude linear convergence.
The condition \(\alpha_k<1\) infinitely often is weaker and does not imply persistent damping when \(\alpha_k\to1\).
This terminology packages the negation of the unit-step regime; it is not a separate impossibility theorem.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable and write \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained smooth optimization by low-storage two-term gradient-history directions coupled to exact or inexact line searches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear conjugate-gradient method generates \(p_0=-g_0\), chooses \(\alpha_k>0\) by a line search, sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), and defines \(p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}p_k\). The method family is distinguished by the scalar update, including \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{FR}}=\|g_{k+1}\|^2/\|g_k\|^2\), \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PR}}=g_{k+1}^T(g_{k+1}-g_k)/\|g_k\|^2\), and \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PR+}}=\max\{\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PR}},0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear conjugate-gradient method combines the new negative gradient with the preceding search direction using one scalar coefficient, then selects a step by line search. Fletcher–Reeves, Polak–Ribière, and truncated Polak–Ribière are canonical coefficient choices. The construction stores only a few vectors and does not form a Hessian matrix.
assumptions_latex: The iteration is evaluated only while \(g_k\neq0\).
The chosen line search and coefficient variant include any conditions needed to keep \(p_k\) a descent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_0=-g_0\), \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), and \(p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}p_k\) with a specified nonlinear conjugate-gradient coefficient.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under exact line search, \(g_{k+1}^Tp_k=0\), simplifying the descent relation for the next direction.
special_cases_latex: For a strongly convex quadratic with exact line searches, Fletcher–Reeves reduces to linear conjugate gradient.
Setting \(\beta_{k+1}=0\) produces a steepest-descent restart.
immediate_consequences_latex: Each direction update requires gradients, scalar products, and a small fixed number of stored vectors.
With inexact searches, descent is not automatic for every coefficient formula; strong Wolfe conditions or restarts are standard controls.
boundary_notes: Nonlinear conjugacy is generally not exact Hessian conjugacy away from quadratic objectives.
Different \(\beta\) formulas have different descent and global-convergence properties.
The family definition alone does not assert convergence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fletcher–Reeves Quadratic Reduction and Descent Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic specialization, computational profile, and exact-versus-inexact line-search conditions for Fletcher–Reeves directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(p_0=-g_0\), and
\[
p_k=-g_k+\beta_k^{\mathrm{FR}}p_{k-1},\qquad \beta_k^{\mathrm{FR}}=\frac{\|g_k\|^2}{\|g_{k-1}\|^2}.
\]
Then
\[
g_k^Tp_k=-\|g_k\|^2+\beta_k^{\mathrm{FR}}g_k^Tp_{k-1}.
\]
If \(f\) is a strongly convex quadratic and every step is an exact directional minimizer, the method reduces to linear conjugate gradient. More generally, an interior exact line minimizer at the preceding step gives \(g_k^Tp_{k-1}=0\), and hence \(g_k^Tp_k=-\|g_k\|^2<0\) whenever \(g_k\ne0\). With an unrestricted inexact line search, the second term can dominate and \(p_k\) can instead be an ascent direction. If each step satisfies
\[
f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\le f(x_k)+c_1\alpha_kg_k^Tp_k,
\]
\[
|\nabla f(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)^Tp_k|\le-c_2g_k^Tp_k,
\qquad 0<c_1<c_2<\tfrac12,
\]
then every nonstationary Fletcher\text{--}Reeves direction is a descent direction. Each iteration requires objective and gradient evaluations, no matrix operation for the step computation, and storage for only a few vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a strongly convex quadratic with exact line searches, Fletcher–Reeves reduces to linear CG. Exact line search makes every nonstationary direction descending, while an unrestricted inexact search can produce an ascent direction. Strong Wolfe steps with the stricter condition c2 below one half ensure descent. The step computation is matrix-free and needs only a few stored vectors, apart from objective and gradient evaluations.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is differentiable at the generated iterates and along the search lines.}
\text{The exact line minimizer is an interior differentiable minimizer for the orthogonality conclusion.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Exact line search, or strong Wolfe search with }c_2<\tfrac12,\text{ yields }g_k^Tp_k<0\text{ whenever }g_k\ne0;\text{ an unrestricted inexact search need not.}

children.title: Nonlinear-CG Recurrence Architecture
children.top_down_role: Structural recurrence forms, their quadratic ancestry, and their dependence on step-length selection.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\). All inner products and norms are Euclidean.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth, unconstrained deterministic optimization with line-search step selection; this definition describes the recurrence and does not impose a convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear conjugate-gradient recurrence is a sequence \((x_k,d_k,\alpha_k,\beta_k)\) initialized by \(d_0=-g_0\) and, whenever \(g_k\ne0\), satisfying \[\alpha_k>0,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k d_k,\qquad g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1}),\qquad d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k.\] The scalar \(\alpha_k\) is selected by a specified line-search rule along \(d_k\), while \(\beta_{k+1}\) is selected from current and stored first-order data. The architecture terminates when \(g_k=0\). A restart at index \(k+1\) is the specialization \(\beta_{k+1}=0\), hence \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear conjugate-gradient method starts from a point and the negative gradient. Each positive line-search step updates the iterate, after which the next direction is the new negative gradient plus a scalar multiple of the preceding direction. The step-length rule and the coefficient formula are separate components of the architecture. Setting the coefficient to zero performs a steepest-descent restart.
assumptions_latex: Each recurrence is evaluated only while \(g_k\ne0\), and every accepted step satisfies \(\alpha_k>0\).
Any denominator occurring in the chosen formula for \(\beta_{k+1}\) is nonzero.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k=\alpha_kd_k\), the memory term may equivalently be written \((\beta_{k+1}/\alpha_k)s_k\).
special_cases_latex: \(\beta_{k+1}=0\) gives a steepest-descent restart.
For a strictly convex quadratic objective and exact line searches, suitable classical coefficients recover linear conjugate gradients.
immediate_consequences_latex: The direction update requires gradient vectors and scalar products but no explicit Hessian matrix.
The line search and coefficient rule are mathematically coupled because \(g_{k+1}\), and often the sign of \(g_{k+1}^{T}d_k\), depend on \(\alpha_k\).
boundary_notes: The recurrence alone does not guarantee that every \(d_k\) is a descent direction.
Nonsmooth, constrained, stochastic, preconditioned, and Riemannian conjugate-gradient schemes require additional definitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Term Nonlinear-CG Recurrence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard nonlinear conjugate-gradient direction architecture with a method-dependent scalar coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a continuously differentiable function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), define \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\). A two-term nonlinear conjugate-gradient recurrence initializes \(d_0=-g_0\) and, after choosing \(\alpha_k>0\) and setting \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), forms
\[
d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k.
\]
The scalar \(\beta_k\) is determined by the chosen nonlinear-CG formula and available gradient or displacement data. A restart replaces \(\beta_k\) by zero, thereby resetting \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-term nonlinear CG combines the new negative gradient with one multiple of the preceding search direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Three-Term Nonlinear-CG Recurrences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonlinear-CG architecture augmented by a second correction direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), and \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\). A three-term nonlinear-CG recurrence initializes \(d_0=-g_0\) and constructs
\[
d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k+\theta_kw_k,
\]
where \(w_k\) is a specified auxiliary vector, commonly \(y_k\) or \(s_k\), and \(\beta_k,\theta_k\) are scalar functions of available iteration data. The defining method must specify these three choices; setting \(\theta_k=0\) recovers the two-term architecture.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Three-term nonlinear CG adds a gradient-difference or displacement correction to the usual negative-gradient and previous-direction terms.
assumptions_latex: The method specifies \(w_k\), \(\beta_k\), and \(\theta_k\) from available iteration data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k+\theta_kw_k\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). Fix a restart index \(t\), and put \(y_j=g_{j+1}-g_j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth unconstrained optimization; the canonical three-term object is the Beale restart-cycle recurrence, not an arbitrary recurrence containing three vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Within the restart cycle beginning at \(t\), a Beale-type three-term nonlinear conjugate-gradient recurrence is defined by \[d_{t+1}=-g_{t+1}+\beta_t d_t\] and, for \(t+2\le k\le t+n-1\), \[d_k=-g_k+\beta_{k-1}d_{k-1}+\gamma_{k-1}d_t,\] where \[\beta_{k-1}=\frac{g_k^Ty_{k-1}}{d_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1}},\qquad \gamma_{k-1}=\frac{g_k^Ty_t}{d_t^Ty_t}.\] At \(k=t+1\), the restart-direction coefficient is defined as \(\gamma_t=0\). Thus the third term retains the direction \(d_t\) that initiated the current cycle rather than merely adding another copy of the immediately preceding direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Beale three-term recurrence retains the restart direction throughout a cycle. The first post-restart direction uses the usual two-term update. Later directions combine the negative current gradient, the immediately preceding direction, and the fixed restart direction. The two coefficients are gradient-difference ratios that enforce the intended conjugacy structure in the quadratic exact-search regime.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^1(\mathbb{R}^n)\), and a restart index \(t\) has been fixed.
\(d_{k-1}^Ty_{k-1}\ne0\) and \(d_t^Ty_t\ne0\) whenever the displayed quotients are used.
The indices remain in one restart cycle: \(t+2\le k\le t+n-1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_{k-1}d_{k-1}+\gamma_{k-1}d_t\) with the displayed Beale coefficients.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The recurrence is a three-vector short-memory update with basis \(\{-g_k,d_{k-1},d_t\}\).
special_cases_latex: At \(k=t+1\), \(\gamma_t=0\), so the update is two-term.
The coefficient \(\beta_{k-1}\) may be replaced by another classical nonlinear-CG coefficient in variants, while the retained restart-direction term distinguishes the Beale architecture.
immediate_consequences_latex: Only the current gradient, preceding direction, fixed restart direction, and associated gradient differences are needed within a cycle.
The three-term form does not by itself imply descent; a separate descent test or restart mechanism may be imposed.
boundary_notes: The definition does not cover three-term methods whose third vector is \(y_{k-1}\) rather than a fixed restart direction.
Vanishing denominators require a restart, safeguard, or separately defined fallback.

notation.meaning: Index at which the current restart cycle begins.
Coefficient multiplying the retained restart direction.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^TGx-b^Tx+c\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(G=G^T\succ0\). Let \(g_k=Gx_k-b\), \(d_0=-g_0\), and let every \(\alpha_k\) minimize \(q(x_k+\alpha d_k)\) exactly over \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a definition of the quadratic correspondence property attached to a recurrence. It records the exact-arithmetic SPD-quadratic regime and does not assert the same properties for nonlinear objectives or inexact searches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear-CG recurrence has the quadratic conjugacy–termination correspondence if, whenever it is applied to the stated strictly convex quadratic with exact line searches, its nonzero directions satisfy \[d_i^TGd_j=0\quad(i\ne j),\] its gradients satisfy \[g_i^Tg_j=0\quad(i\ne j),\qquad g_i^Td_i=-\|g_i\|^2,\] and it reaches \(g_m=0\) for some \(m\le n\). Equivalently, before termination the direction and gradient spans coincide with the Krylov spaces \[\operatorname{span}\{d_0,\ldots,d_i\}=\operatorname{span}\{g_0,Gg_0,\ldots,G^ig_0\}.\] Classical FR, PRP, HS, CD, and DY coefficients coincide in this regime in the sense of generating the same conjugate directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic conjugacy–termination correspondence is the property that an NCG recurrence becomes ordinary conjugate gradients on a symmetric positive-definite quadratic when every line search is exact. Its directions are mutually conjugate in the Hessian metric, its gradients are mutually orthogonal, the generated spaces are Krylov spaces, and a stationary point is obtained after at most the ambient dimension many steps in exact arithmetic.
assumptions_latex: \(G=G^T\succ0\) and computations are performed in exact arithmetic.
Each step length is an exact one-dimensional minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The correspondence property consists of \(G\)-conjugacy, gradient orthogonality, Krylov-span equality, and termination at some \(m\le n\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an SPD quadratic, \(g_m=0\) is equivalent to \(x_m=G^{-1}b\).
If \(G\) has only \(r\) distinct eigenvalues relative to the initial Krylov space, termination may occur in at most \(r\le n\) steps.
special_cases_latex: The Fletcher–Reeves recurrence with exact searches possesses this correspondence.
The classical PRP, HS, CD, and DY formulas reduce to the same direction sequence under the exact quadratic orthogonality identities.
immediate_consequences_latex: The finite-termination statement belongs to the exact quadratic model, not to a general nonlinear objective.
The property explains why different nonlinear-CG coefficients can be algebraically equivalent on quadratics yet behave differently with inexact searches.
boundary_notes: Roundoff can destroy exact conjugacy and finite termination.
Indefinite or singular quadratic forms are excluded.
This definition does not claim finite termination for nonquadratic functions.

notation.meaning: Order-\(i\) Krylov space generated by \(G\) and \(g_0\).

children.title: Quadratic Conjugacy Regime
children.top_down_role: Conjugate-direction structure associated with quadratic objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Conjugacy Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite quadratic setting in which conjugacy is defined by the fixed Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Ax-b^{\mathsf T}x+c,
\qquad A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0.
\]
A collection of nonzero directions \(d_0,\ldots,d_m\) is conjugate for this quadratic precisely when
\[
d_i^{\mathsf T}Ad_j=0\qquad\text{for every }i\ne j.
\]
Because \(A\) is positive definite, any such collection is linearly independent and therefore contains at most \(n\) directions. The condition refers to one fixed matrix \(A\), namely the constant Hessian \(\nabla^2q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directions are conjugate for a strictly convex quadratic when distinct directions are orthogonal in the inner product induced by its Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_i^{\mathsf T}Ad_j=0\) for \(i\ne j\), and consequently the directions are linearly independent.

notation.meaning: Constant positive-definite Hessian of the quadratic.

children.title: Exact-Search Conjugacy

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Search Conjugacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical conjugate-gradient recurrence on a strictly convex quadratic with exact line searches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Ax-b^{\mathsf T}x+c\) with \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\). Starting from \(x_0\), set \(g_k=Ax_k-b\), \(d_0=-g_0\), choose \(\alpha_k\) as the exact minimizer of \(q(x_k+\alpha d_k)\), and set
\[
d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k,
\qquad
\beta_k=\frac{g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}g_{k+1}}{g_k^{\mathsf T}g_k}.
\]
Until termination, \(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}d_k=0\), the generated gradients are mutually orthogonal, and the generated directions are mutually \(A\)-conjugate: \(d_i^{\mathsf T}Ad_j=0\) whenever \(i\ne j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-definite quadratic, exact-search Fletcher–Reeves CG generates mutually orthogonal gradients and mutually Hessian-conjugate directions.
assumptions_latex: The recurrence uses the displayed Fletcher–Reeves coefficient until a zero gradient occurs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_i^{\mathsf T}g_j=0\) and \(d_i^{\mathsf T}Ad_j=0\) for all distinct generated indices \(i,j\).

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Finite-Termination Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic finite termination of conjugate gradient on a positive-definite quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the quadratic conjugate-gradient construction with \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), exact line searches, and exact arithmetic, either some \(g_k=0\) before iteration \(n\), or the nonzero directions \(d_0,\ldots,d_{n-1}\) form an \(A\)-conjugate basis of \(\mathbb{R}^n\). In either case, for some \(m\le n\),
\[
g_m=0,
\qquad
x_m=A^{-1}b=	ext{the unique minimizer of }q.
\]
More sharply, termination occurs in at most the number of distinct eigenvalues of \(A\) represented in the initial error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact-arithmetic conjugate gradient solves an n-dimensional positive-definite quadratic in at most n iterations, often fewer according to its active spectrum.
assumptions_latex: The conjugate-gradient recurrence uses exact line searches.
All computations are in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists m\le n:\;x_m=A^{-1}b\) and \(g_m=0\).

children.title: Nonquadratic Bridge Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits of transferring quadratic conjugacy or termination behavior to nonlinear objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonquadratic Bridge Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why exact-search orthogonality does not extend quadratic conjugacy and finite termination to general objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a twice continuously differentiable nonquadratic \(f\), exact minimization along \(d_k\) yields only
\[
\nabla f(x_{k+1})^{\mathsf T}d_k=0.
\]
Writing \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), the gradient change satisfies
\[
\nabla f(x_{k+1})-\nabla f(x_k)=\left(\int_0^1\nabla^2f(x_k+ts_k)\,dt\right)s_k.
\]
The averaged Hessian generally varies with \(k\); hence no single fixed positive-definite matrix need make all generated directions conjugate. Exact line search alone therefore does not imply mutual conjugacy, orthogonality of all gradients, or finite termination in at most \(n\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outside the quadratic case, exact line search gives adjacent orthogonality but no fixed Hessian metric, mutual conjugacy, or finite termination.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is twice continuously differentiable along each accepted segment.
Each accepted step exactly minimizes \(f(x_k+\alpha d_k)\) over an interval containing \(\alpha_k\) in its interior.
The Hessian is not assumed constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact search does not by itself imply \(d_i^{\mathsf T}Ad_j=0\) for one fixed \(A\), nor termination within \(n\) iterations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Line-search interface for nonlinear conjugate gradients
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f\in C^1(\mathbb{R}^n)\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and suppose \(d_k\) is a descent direction, so \(g_k^Td_k<0\). Define \(\phi_k(\alpha)=f(x_k+\alpha d_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic unconstrained optimization. The interface specifies admissible communication between direction generation and step selection; it does not prescribe a particular interpolation or bracketing implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear-CG line-search interface accepts \((x_k,f(x_k),g_k,d_k)\) and returns \(\alpha_k>0\), after which \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\) and \(g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1})\) are supplied to the coefficient rule. An exact interface returns \[\alpha_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha>0}\phi_k(\alpha).\] A strong-Wolfe interface with \(0<c_1<c_2<1\) returns a step satisfying \[f(x_{k+1})\le f(x_k)+c_1\alpha_kg_k^Td_k,\qquad |g_{k+1}^Td_k|\le -c_2g_k^Td_k.\] For the standard Fletcher–Reeves descent guarantee, the customary restriction is \(c_2<\tfrac12\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The line-search interface receives the current point, objective value, gradient, and descent direction and returns a positive step. It then exposes the new gradient to the NCG coefficient formula. The exact version minimizes the objective on the search ray. The practical strong-Wolfe version enforces sufficient decrease and bounds the magnitude of the new directional derivative.
assumptions_latex: For strong Wolfe, \(0<c_1<c_2<1\); the Fletcher–Reeves specialization uses \(c_2<1/2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfies either exact ray minimization or the displayed strong-Wolfe inequalities and defines \((x_{k+1},g_{k+1})\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Exact line search at an interior minimizer gives \(g_{k+1}^Td_k=\phi_k'(\alpha_k)=0\).
The strong curvature condition is \(|\phi_k'(\alpha_k)|\le c_2|\phi_k'(0)|\).
special_cases_latex: When \(d_k=-g_k\), the interface reduces to a gradient-method line search.
For a strictly convex quadratic, exact ray minimization has a unique positive solution whenever \(d_k\) is a descent direction.
immediate_consequences_latex: The coefficient rule may depend on \(g_{k+1}\), so it is evaluated only after the line search.
The curvature condition controls the memory term \(\beta_{k+1}d_k\) through the directional derivative \(g_{k+1}^Td_k\).
boundary_notes: Weak Wolfe replaces the absolute-value curvature inequality by a one-sided inequality and is a different interface.
If \(d_k\) is not a descent direction, the displayed Armijo condition is not the standard descent globalization condition.

children.title: Acceptance-Rule Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between nonlinear-CG coefficient families and line-search acceptance families.

knowledge_statements.title: Acceptance-Rule Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Line-search acceptance predicate commonly paired with nonlinear-CG recurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and require \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k<0\). A step length \(\alpha_k>0\) is compatible with the standard nonlinear-CG globalization interface when, for fixed \(0<c_1<c_2<1\), it satisfies the strong Wolfe conditions
\[
f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\le f(x_k)+c_1\alpha_k g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k,
\]
\[
\left|\nabla f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)^{\mathsf T}d_k\right|\le c_2\left|g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\right|.
\]
A particular nonlinear-CG recurrence may impose a stricter upper bound on \(c_2\) to preserve descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compatible nonlinear-CG line search ordinarily combines sufficient decrease with strong curvature control along a descent direction.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable along the search ray.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted \(\alpha_k\) satisfies both displayed strong Wolfe inequalities.

children.title: Curvature-Condition Effects
children.top_down_role: Influence of line-search curvature controls on nonlinear-CG directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Condition Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative control supplied by the strong Wolfe curvature inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k<0\), set \(g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\), and let the accepted step satisfy the strong Wolfe curvature condition with \(c_2\in(0,1)\). Then
\[
-c_2|g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k|\le g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}d_k\le c_2|g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k|.
\]
Consequently,
\[
y_k^{\mathsf T}d_k=(g_{k+1}-g_k)^{\mathsf T}d_k\ge(1-c_2)|g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k|>0.
\]
Thus the curvature test controls loss of directional orthogonality and ensures positivity of the secant denominator \(y_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\) used by several nonlinear-CG coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong Wolfe curvature control bounds residual directional correlation and makes the gradient-difference curvature product strictly positive.

knowledge_statements.title: Directional Descent Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform sufficient-descent invariant for nonlinear-CG directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\). A nonlinear-CG direction sequence preserves uniform directional descent on an index set \(I\) when there exists a constant \(\eta>0\), independent of \(k\), such that
\[
g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\le-\eta\lVert g_k\rVert^2
\qquad\text{for every }k\in I\text{ with }g_k\ne0.
\]
This predicate is stronger than merely requiring \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k<0\). If a recurrence fails it, a descent-preserving safeguard may restart by setting \(d_k=-g_k\), which satisfies the inequality with \(\eta=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform directional descent requires the gradient–direction inner product to be no greater than a fixed negative multiple of the squared gradient norm; restarting with the negative gradient restores this condition.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable at every indexed iterate.
Directions are assessed only at indices with \(g_k\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\eta>0\;\forall k\in I:\;g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\le-\eta\lVert g_k\rVert^2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Inexactness Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies instability of nonlinear-CG curvature denominators when exact line-search orthogonality is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, let \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k d_k\) with \(d_k\ne0\), and define \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1})\), \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\), and \(\rho_k=g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}d_k\). Then
\[
d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k=\rho_k-d_k^{\mathsf T}g_k.
\]
If \(\alpha_k\) is an interior minimizer of \(\phi_k(\alpha)=f(x_k+\alpha d_k)\), first-order stationarity gives \(\rho_k=0\). An inexact line search need not have this property, so its residual \(\rho_k\) perturbs the denominator \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\) used by the Hestenes–Stiefel and Dai–Yuan coefficients. Along any sequence for which \(\lvert d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\rvert\to0\) while the absolute value of the corresponding coefficient numerator is bounded below by a positive constant, the coefficient magnitude tends to infinity. A restart or an explicitly specified denominator safeguard can prevent the resulting unguarded division.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact line search can perturb the directional-curvature denominator used by the HS and DY formulas. If that denominator approaches zero while the associated numerator stays bounded away from zero, the coefficient magnitude diverges, motivating a restart or denominator safeguard.
assumptions_latex: For the exact-line-search implication, \(\alpha_k\) is an interior minimizer of \(\phi_k(\alpha)=f(x_k+\alpha d_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k=\rho_k-d_k^{\mathsf T}g_k\); if \(\lvert d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\rvert\to0\) while the corresponding numerator stays bounded away from zero, then the coefficient magnitude tends to infinity.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The classical nonlinear-CG coefficient family consists of \[\beta_k^{FR}=\frac{g_{k+1}^Tg_{k+1}}{g_k^Tg_k},\quad \beta_k^{PRP}=\frac{g_{k+1}^Ty_k}{g_k^Tg_k},\quad \beta_k^{HS}=\frac{g_{k+1}^Ty_k}{d_k^Ty_k},\] \[\beta_k^{DY}=\frac{g_{k+1}^Tg_{k+1}}{d_k^Ty_k},\quad \beta_k^{CD}=-\frac{g_{k+1}^Tg_{k+1}}{g_k^Td_k},\quad \beta_k^{LS}=-\frac{g_{k+1}^Ty_k}{g_k^Td_k}.\] Selecting one coefficient at every iteration and inserting it into the common two-term direction recurrence defines the corresponding classical method.

The truncation \(\max\{0,\beta_k^{PRP}\}\) is a modified, rather than untruncated classical, member.

knowledge_statements.title: Fletcher–Reeves Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical nonlinear conjugate-gradient iteration with the Fletcher–Reeves coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\) and \(d_0=-g_0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by a prescribed line search and set
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k,\qquad g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1}).
\]
If \(g_{k+1}=0\), return \(x_{k+1}\). Otherwise define
\[
\beta_k^{\mathrm{FR}}=\frac{\lVert g_{k+1}\rVert^2}{\lVert g_k\rVert^2},\qquad d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_k^{\mathrm{FR}}d_k.
\]
The generated iterate is the first stationary point encountered or the latest \(x_k\) when an external stopping test is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fletcher–Reeves updates the nonlinear-CG direction using the ratio of consecutive squared gradient norms, with step length supplied by a line search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+(\lVert g_{k+1}\rVert^2/\lVert g_k\rVert^2)d_k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Polak–Ribière–Polyak Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical nonlinear conjugate-gradient iteration using the untruncated PRP coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\) and \(d_0=-g_0\). After selecting \(\alpha_k>0\) by line search, compute
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k,\qquad g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1}),\qquad y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k.
\]
If \(g_{k+1}=0\), stop. Otherwise set
\[
\beta_k^{\mathrm{PRP}}=\frac{g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}y_k}{\lVert g_k\rVert^2},\qquad d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_k^{\mathrm{PRP}}d_k.
\]
The untruncated coefficient may be negative; replacing it by a nonnegative truncation defines a distinct safeguarded variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PRP forms the next direction using the new gradient’s inner product with the gradient change, divided by the previous squared gradient norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}y_k/\lVert g_k\rVert^2)d_k\).

\[
\beta_k^{\mathrm{PR}}=\frac{(g^{(k+1)})^\top(g^{(k+1)}-g^{(k)})}{(g^{(k)})^\top g^{(k)}}.
\]

knowledge_statements.title: Hestenes–Stiefel Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical nonlinear conjugate-gradient iteration using the Hestenes–Stiefel coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\), and \(d_0=-g_0\). Given \(d_k\), select \(\alpha_k>0\) by line search and compute
\[

\beta_k^{\mathrm{HS}}=\frac{g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}y_k}{d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k},\qquad d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_k^{\mathrm{HS}}d_k.
\]
When the denominator vanishes or is deemed too small, the coefficient must be safeguarded or the direction restarted.

knowledge_statements.title: Dai–Yuan Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical nonlinear conjugate-gradient iteration using the Dai–Yuan coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

\[
x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k,\qquad g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1}),\qquad y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k.
\]
If \(g_{k+1}=0\), stop. If \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\ne0\), define
\[

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate-Descent Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical nonlinear conjugate-gradient recurrence with the conjugate-descent coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\), and \(d_0=-g_0\). Given \(d_k\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by line search, then compute \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\) and \(g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1})\). If \(g_{k+1}=0\), stop. Provided \(d_k^{\mathsf T}g_k<0\), define
\[
\beta_k^{\mathrm{CD}}=-\frac{\lVert g_{k+1}\rVert^2}{d_k^{\mathsf T}g_k},\qquad d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_k^{\mathrm{CD}}d_k.
\]
If the denominator fails the descent condition, use a restart such as \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugate descent divides the new squared gradient norm by the negative directional derivative at the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}-(\lVert g_{k+1}\rVert^2/(d_k^{\mathsf T}g_k))d_k\).

For a descent direction, its denominator is negative, so the displayed coefficient is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugate descent normalizes the new squared gradient norm by the negative current directional derivative. The resulting nonnegative coefficient, when the current direction is descending, multiplies the previous direction in the two-term update.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha_k>0\) is selected by the line search.
special_cases_latex: Under exact line search on an SPD quadratic, conjugate descent is equivalent to Fletcher–Reeves.

immediate_consequences_latex: If \(g_k^Td_k<0\), then \(\beta_{k+1}^{CD}\ge0\).
The coefficient requires no gradient-difference vector.
boundary_notes: The formula is undefined for a direction orthogonal to the current gradient.
The definition does not itself prescribe how to recover when the current direction is non-descent.

knowledge_statements.title: Liu–Storey Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical nonlinear conjugate-gradient recurrence with the Liu–Storey coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\), and \(d_0=-g_0\). Choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by line search and compute
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k,\qquad g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1}),\qquad y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k.
\]
If \(g_{k+1}=0\), stop. Provided \(d_k^{\mathsf T}g_k\ne0\), define
\[
\beta_k^{\mathrm{LS}}=-\frac{g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}y_k}{d_k^{\mathsf T}g_k},\qquad d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_k^{\mathrm{LS}}d_k.
\]
If the denominator is zero or numerically unsafe, restart or apply an explicitly specified safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Liu–Storey divides the negative new-gradient curvature numerator by the previous directional derivative and inserts the coefficient into the nonlinear-CG recurrence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}-(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}y_k/(d_k^{\mathsf T}g_k))d_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An extended nonlinear-CG variant is a recurrence in which \(\widehat\beta_{k+1}\) is obtained from one or more classical coefficients by a specified nonlinear transformation or correction. Three-term variants extend the direction basis instead. A variant is not fully specified unless its coefficient transformation, denominator safeguards, and restart behavior are stated.

The selected truncation, hybrid, correction, and fallback maps are fixed before the recurrence is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat\beta_{k+1}=T_k(\beta_{k+1}^{FR},\beta_{k+1}^{PRP},\beta_{k+1}^{HS},\beta_{k+1}^{DY},\beta_{k+1}^{CD},\beta_{k+1}^{LS};g_k,g_{k+1},d_k,y_k)\) for an explicitly specified extension map \(T_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A coefficient-clipping variant is a projection of a raw coefficient onto an iteration-dependent interval.
A convex hybrid has \(\widehat\beta=(1-\theta)\beta^{(1)}+\theta\beta^{(2)}\) with \(\theta\in[0,1]\).
special_cases_latex: The identity map recovers a classical coefficient.
A zero-valued transformation produces a steepest-descent restart.

Extended variants can combine the restart behavior of gradient-difference formulas with bounds inherited from norm-squared formulas.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncated Polak–Ribière–Polyak Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical nonnegative and upper-bounded truncations of the PRP coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(g_k\ne0\), let \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\) and
\[
\beta_k^{\mathrm{PRP}}=\frac{g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}y_k}{\lVert g_k\rVert^2}.
\]
The PRP-plus truncation and a capped PRP truncation are respectively
\[
\beta_k^{\mathrm{PRP+}}=\max\{0,\beta_k^{\mathrm{PRP}}\},\qquad
\beta_k^{\mathrm{PRP}[0,B_k]}=\min\{B_k,\max\{0,\beta_k^{\mathrm{PRP}}\}\},
\]
where \(B_k\in(0,\infty]\). The direction update is \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k\). Thus every finite-cap member satisfies \(0\le\beta_k\le B_k\), and every negative raw PRP coefficient produces the steepest-descent restart \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncated PRP replaces a negative PRP coefficient by zero and may also cap positive values, thereby producing a steepest-descent restart when the raw coefficient is negative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta_k^{\mathrm{PRP}[0,B_k]}\in[0,B_k]\), with \(\beta_k=0\) whenever \(\beta_k^{\mathrm{PRP}}<0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-term smooth unconstrained NCG variants obtained by pointwise truncation or clipping of the raw PRP coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A truncated PRP method replaces \(\beta_{k+1}^{PRP}\) in \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k\) by a projection onto a prescribed interval. The canonical nonnegative truncation is \[\beta_{k+1}^{PRP+}=\max\{0,\beta_{k+1}^{PRP}\}.\] A bounded FR–PR clipping is \[\beta_{k+1}^{FR-PR}=\max\{-\beta_{k+1}^{FR},\min(\beta_{k+1}^{PRP},\beta_{k+1}^{FR})\}.\] More generally, for specified bounds \(\ell_k\le u_k\), the clipped family is \[\beta_{k+1}^{clip}=\min\{u_k,\max\{\ell_k,\beta_{k+1}^{PRP}\}\}.\] The bounds are part of the method and may depend only on information available at iteration \(k+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated PRP method projects the raw PRP coefficient onto a chosen interval before updating the direction. PRP+ discards negative values. FR–PR clips PRP between the negative and positive Fletcher–Reeves coefficients. The generic family permits any explicitly prescribed lower and upper bounds based on available iteration data.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta_{k+1}^{clip}=\operatorname{proj}_{[\ell_k,u_k]}(\beta_{k+1}^{PRP})\), including PRP+ and FR–PR as displayed specializations.

\(\beta^{FR-PR}=\operatorname{proj}_{[-\beta^{FR},\beta^{FR}]}(\beta^{PRP})\).

If \(\beta_{k+1}^{PRP}<0\), PRP+ sets the memory coefficient to zero and restarts along \(-g_{k+1}\).

FR–PR enforces \(|\beta_{k+1}^{FR-PR}|\le\beta_{k+1}^{FR}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Hestenes–Stiefel Hybrid Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hestenes–Stiefel candidate component used in HS–DY hybrid coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\), and suppose \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\ne0\). The Hestenes–Stiefel component of an HS–DY hybrid is
\[
\beta_k^{\mathrm{HS}}=rac{g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}y_k}{d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k}.
\]
Its numerator measures the component of the gradient change along the new gradient, while its denominator is the change in directional derivative along \(d_k\). A hybrid coefficient may select, truncate, or clip this scalar before applying
\[
d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k.
\]
The component is undefined without a separate convention when \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The HS component is the new-gradient curvature numerator divided by directional curvature; hybrid rules subsequently select or safeguard this scalar.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta_k^{\mathrm{HS}}=(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}y_k)/(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied for the role of the HS coefficient within the particular HS–DY hybrid family. In addition, the displayed formula contains the malformed command `rac` instead of a delimited `\frac`. Because the hybrid interpretation is source-dependent, the record cannot be repaired confidently until an authoritative hybrid source with a precise locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.title: Dai–Yuan Hybrid Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dai–Yuan candidate component used in HS–DY hybrid coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\), and suppose \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\ne0\). The Dai–Yuan component of an HS–DY hybrid is
\[
\beta_k^{\mathrm{DY}}=rac{\lVert g_{k+1}\rVert^2}{d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k}.
\]
When \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0\) and \(g_{k+1}\ne0\), this component is strictly positive. A hybrid rule may use it as the active coefficient or as an upper safeguard for another component before forming
\[
d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k.
\]
If the denominator is nonpositive or too small, a separate restart or denominator safeguard must be specified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The DY component is the new squared gradient norm divided by directional curvature and can serve as an active coefficient or hybrid upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta_k^{\mathrm{DY}}=\lVert g_{k+1}\rVert^2/(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k)\), and \(\beta_k^{\mathrm{DY}}>0\) when \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0\) and \(g_{k+1}\ne0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Switching Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise switching rule for a clipped HS–DY hybrid coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(\beta_k^{\mathrm{HS}}\) and \(\beta_k^{\mathrm{DY}}\) are defined. The nonnegative HS–DY switching criterion selects
\[
\beta_k^{\mathrm{hyb}}=
\max\!\left\{0,\min\!\left\{\beta_k^{\mathrm{HS}},\beta_k^{\mathrm{DY}}\right\}\right\}.
\]
Equivalently, it selects \(0\) if \(\min\{\beta_k^{\mathrm{HS}},\beta_k^{\mathrm{DY}}\}\le0\), selects \(\beta_k^{\mathrm{HS}}\) if \(0<\beta_k^{\mathrm{HS}}\le\beta_k^{\mathrm{DY}}\), and selects \(\beta_k^{\mathrm{DY}}\) if \(0<\beta_k^{\mathrm{DY}}<\beta_k^{\mathrm{HS}}\). The resulting search direction is \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_k^{\mathrm{hyb}}d_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The switching rule chooses zero for unsafe negative components and otherwise takes the smaller of the HS and DY coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta_k^{\mathrm{hyb}}=\max\{0,\min\{\beta_k^{\mathrm{HS}},\beta_k^{\mathrm{DY}}\}\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the switching-criteria leaf, and the piecewise description is algebraically equivalent to the displayed max-min rule. However, HS–DY hybrids use multiple conventions, and no source identifies this particular nonnegative minimum rule as the intended family member. A variant-specific authoritative citation with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Hybrid Coefficient Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Controls limiting undesirable hybrid coefficient or direction behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Coefficient Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection and restart safeguards for an HS–DY hybrid coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a raw hybrid candidate \(\widehat\beta_k\), a finite cap \(B_k>0\), and a denominator tolerance \(\varepsilon_k>0\), compute \(q_k=d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\). If \(q_k\le\varepsilon_k\), set \(\beta_k=0\) and restart with \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}\). Otherwise set
\[
\beta_k=\min\{B_k,\max\{0,\widehat\beta_k\}\},
\qquad d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k.
\]
When the Dai–Yuan component is positive and finite, the adaptive choice \(B_k=\beta_k^{\mathrm{DY}}\) gives \(0\le\beta_k\le\beta_k^{\mathrm{DY}}\). Terminate when the prescribed stationarity or iteration-limit test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The safeguard restarts on inadequate curvature and otherwise projects the raw hybrid coefficient onto a nonnegative bounded interval, optionally capped by Dai–Yuan.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_k\le\varepsilon_k\Rightarrow\beta_k=0\), while \(q_k>\varepsilon_k\Rightarrow0\le\beta_k\le B_k\).

An authoritative locator is required before the precise algorithm and its terminal-container fit can be confirmed.

knowledge_statements.title: Hager–Zhang Descent-Preserving Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained smooth nonlinear-CG direction using the unsafeguarded Hager–Zhang coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(y_{k-1}=g_k-g_{k-1}\), and suppose \(d_{k-1}^{\mathsf T}y_{k-1}\ne0\). Define
\[\beta_k^{\mathrm{HZ}}=\frac{\left(y_{k-1}-2d_{k-1}\frac{\lVert y_{k-1}\rVert^2}{d_{k-1}^{\mathsf T}y_{k-1}}\right)^{\mathsf T}g_k}{d_{k-1}^{\mathsf T}y_{k-1}},\qquad d_k=-g_k+\beta_k^{\mathrm{HZ}}d_{k-1}.\]
Then the direction satisfies the uniform sufficient-descent inequality
\[g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\le-\frac{7}{8}\lVert g_k\rVert^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Hager–Zhang coefficient adds a conjugate-gradient correction while guaranteeing that every defined direction has a uniform negative inner product with the current gradient.

knowledge_statements.title: Three-Term Descent-Preserving Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic three-term correction that enforces exact descent independently of its CG coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_k\ne0\), let \(d_{k-1}\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and choose any scalar \(\beta_k\). The three-term direction
\[d_k=-g_k+\beta_k d_{k-1}-\beta_k\frac{g_k^{\mathsf T}d_{k-1}}{\lVert g_k\rVert^2}g_k\]
can equivalently be written as \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_k P_kd_{k-1}\), where
\[P_k=I-\frac{g_kg_k^{\mathsf T}}{\lVert g_k\rVert^2}.\]
Because \(P_kd_{k-1}\) is orthogonal to \(g_k\), every member of this coefficient-parameterized family satisfies
\[g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k=-\lVert g_k\rVert^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting the inherited CG direction orthogonally to the current gradient produces a three-term recurrence with exact descent for any finite coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k=-\lVert g_k\rVert^2<0\).

notation.meaning: Orthogonal projector onto the complement of the current gradient.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\sigma\in(0,1)\) and \(\delta\in(0,1)\). Otherwise the method invokes its specified fallback, such as beginning a new cycle or replacing the candidate by a certified descent direction. In the cited Beale control, \(\delta=0.2\), while \(\sigma\) is a small positive constant. The coefficient and fallback rules are integral parts of each family member.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A three-term descent-preserving method first constructs a Beale-type direction from the negative gradient, the preceding direction, and the retained restart direction. It accepts that candidate only when it makes a uniformly acute angle with the negative gradient and when consecutive gradients pass a near-orthogonality test. Failure triggers the method’s stated restart or descent fallback.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Conjugate-Gradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selected-memory nonlinear-CG imposing conjugacy only against a chosen subset of stored secant pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\) and \(d_0=-g_0\). At iteration \(k\), choose a finite index set \(J_k\subseteq\{0,\ldots,k-1\}\), form matrices \(D_k=[d_j]_{j\in J_k}\) and \(Y_k=[y_j]_{j\in J_k}\), and solve
\[(Y_k^{\mathsf T}D_k)\gamma_k=Y_k^{\mathsf T}g_k.\]
Set \(d_k=-g_k+D_k\gamma_k\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by a descent line search, and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). If the system is singular or \(d_k\) is not descent, output the restarted direction \(-g_k\); otherwise the construction gives \(Y_k^{\mathsf T}d_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial CG enforces conjugacy only for selected stored pairs, solves the resulting small system, and restarts with steepest descent if the system or direction is unacceptable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y_k^{\mathsf T}d_k=0\) whenever \(Y_k^{\mathsf T}D_k\) is solved exactly; otherwise \(d_k=-g_k\).

notation.meaning: Selected indices whose conjugacy conditions are retained.
Matrices of selected directions and gradient differences.
Coefficients of the partial conjugacy correction.
