knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k d_k\) with \(\alpha_k>0\). For each \(k\), let \(J_k\subseteq\{0,\ldots,k-1\}\) be a selected set of earlier direction indices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth, deterministic unconstrained minimization. This candidate uses the broad partial-memory meaning because the hinted source section was available only as a catalogue entry and its particular convention could not be inspected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partial conjugate-gradient method is a line-search method whose direction has the form \[d_0=-g_0,\qquad d_k=-g_k+\sum_{j\in J_k}\beta_{k,j}d_j,\quad k\geq1,\] where \(J_k\) is a proper selected subset of the available earlier indices and the coefficients are chosen to impose selected conjugacy or secant-orthogonality conditions, such as \(d_k^T H_{k,j}d_j=0\) for \(j\in J_k\), whenever the denominators defining those coefficients are nonzero. Only the directions indexed by \(J_k\) participate in the conjugacy correction; information outside \(J_k\) is discarded. A restart is represented by \(J_k=\varnothing\), which gives \(d_k=-g_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial conjugate-gradient method minimizes a smooth function by a line search and forms each direction from the negative current gradient plus a linear combination of only a selected proper subset of earlier directions. The coefficients enforce the chosen conjugacy or secant-orthogonality relations on that subset. Choosing an empty subset produces a steepest-descent restart.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_k=-g_k+\sum_{j\in J_k}\beta_{k,j}d_j,\qquad J_k\subsetneq\{0,\\ldots,k-1\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(J_k=\{k-1\}\), the construction reduces to the usual two-term nonlinear-CG recurrence \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}\).
If \(J_k=\varnothing\), the partial correction vanishes and the method restarts with \(d_k=-g_k\).
special_cases_latex: A fixed memory length \(q\) is obtained with \(J_k\subseteq\{\max(0,k-q),\ldots,k-1\}\).
For a strictly convex quadratic \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^TAx-b^Tx\), the selected relations may be ordinary \(A\)-conjugacy, \(d_k^TAd_j=0\) for \(j\in J_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The number of stored direction vectors is at most \(|J_k|\), rather than \(k\).
Partial conjugacy does not by itself imply that \(g_k^Td_k<0\); a line-search restriction or direction safeguard may still be required.

This definition excludes truncated linear CG used as an inner solver for Newton or trust-region methods unless it also has the displayed nonlinear line-search recurrence.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(d_k^{\rm raw}=-g_k+\beta_k^{\rm raw}d_{k-1}\). Fix admissibility constants \(c_d>0\) and, when needed, coefficient bounds \(\ell_k\leq u_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear-CG methods. Stability means algebraic control of the recurrence, especially preservation or restoration of usable descent; it is not a claim of numerical backward stability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear-CG stability mechanism is a deterministic map \[\mathcal S_k:(\beta_k^{\rm raw},g_k,d_{k-1},\mathcal H_k)\longmapsto(\widehat\beta_k,d_k)\] such that \(\widehat\beta_k\) may be truncated, reset, or otherwise modified, and the accepted direction is either \(d_k=-g_k+\widehat\beta_kd_{k-1}\) or the restart direction \(-g_k\). Its defining acceptance condition is a descent test, for example \[-g_k^Td_k\geq c_d\|g_k\|\|d_k\|,\] or a sufficient-descent test \(g_k^Td_k\leq-c_d\|g_k\|^2\). Failure of the test forces a prescribed fallback, commonly \(\widehat\beta_k=0\) and \(d_k=-g_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear-CG stability mechanism takes the raw recurrence coefficient and direction, optionally truncates or resets the coefficient, tests the resulting direction for descent, and returns either that accepted direction or a prescribed safe fallback such as the negative gradient. Its defining feature is an explicit acceptance relation, not merely a heuristic change to the coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_k\in\{-g_k+\widehat\beta_kd_{k-1},-g_k\},\qquad g_k^Td_k<0\quad(g_k\neq0).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The normalized angle condition \(-g_k^Td_k/(\|g_k\|\|d_k\|)\geq c_d\) says that the accepted direction remains uniformly separated from orthogonality to \(-g_k\).
A restart mechanism is the special stability map that sets \(\widehat\beta_k=0\) on a specified trigger set.
special_cases_latex: Periodic and orthogonality-triggered restarts modify the recurrence through \(\widehat\beta_k=0\).
PR+ uses \(\widehat\beta_k=\max\{\beta_k^{\rm PR},0\}\), while FR–PR truncates \(\beta_k^{\rm PR}\) to an interval determined by \(\beta_k^{\rm FR}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Whenever the fallback is \(d_k=-g_k\), failure of the candidate test still yields \(g_k^Td_k=-\|g_k\|^2<0\) for \(g_k\neq0\).
A stability mechanism controls direction admissibility but does not alone specify the step length or establish convergence.
boundary_notes: Coefficient clipping without a direction test need not guarantee descent for every nonlinear-CG formula.
The definition does not cover stochastic-gradient variance control or floating-point error analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Periodic Restarts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic nonlinear-CG restart after a fixed number of recurrence steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a differentiable \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), an initial point \(x_0\), and an integer period \(p\ge1\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\) and \(d_0=-g_0\). For \(k\ge1\), compute a chosen nonlinear-CG coefficient \(\beta_k\) and set
\[d_k=\begin{cases}-g_k,&k\equiv0\pmod p,\\-g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1},&k\not\equiv0\pmod p.\end{cases}\]
Choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by the prescribed line search and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). Stop when the selected stationarity test holds and return the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every fixed number of iterations, discard the accumulated CG direction and restart from negative gradient; otherwise use the chosen nonlinear-CG recurrence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_k=-g_k\) at every iteration satisfying \(k\equiv0\pmod p\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable and let a nonlinear-CG iteration use \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and the ordinary recurrence \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}\). Fix an integer period \(q\geq1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic unconstrained minimization. The restart period may equal the dimension \(n\), as in the traditional nonlinear-CG construction, or be another fixed positive integer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A period-\(q\) restarted nonlinear conjugate-gradient method replaces the recurrence coefficient by \[\widehat\beta_k=\begin{cases}0,&k\in q\mathbb N,\\ \beta_k,&k\notin q\mathbb N,\end{cases}\qquad d_k=-g_k+\widehat\beta_kd_{k-1},\quad k\geq1.\] Thus every iteration whose index is a positive multiple of \(q\) starts a new cycle with the steepest-descent direction \(d_k=-g_k\). Equivalently, no cycle contains more than \(q\) directions before the accumulated conjugacy information is erased.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A periodic restart fixes a positive integer period and sets the nonlinear-CG coefficient to zero at every positive multiple of that period. The corresponding direction is exactly the negative current gradient, after which the usual recurrence begins a new cycle. Choosing the dimension as the period gives the traditional dimension-cycle restart.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[k\equiv0\pmod q\Longrightarrow\widehat\beta_k=0\Longrightarrow d_k=-g_k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With cycle counter \(r_k=k\bmod q\), a restart occurs exactly when \(r_k=0\) and \(k>0\).
The restart index set is \(K_R=\{q,2q,3q,\ldots\}\).
special_cases_latex: The traditional nonlinear-CG method uses \(q=n\), motivated by finite termination of linear CG in at most \(n\) exact-arithmetic iterations.
The choice \(q=1\) discards every conjugate correction and is simply steepest descent.
immediate_consequences_latex: At every restart with \(g_k\neq0\), \(g_k^Td_k=-\|g_k\|^2<0\).
If \(q\leq\bar q<\infty\), the number of iterations between successive restart directions is uniformly bounded.
boundary_notes: Periodic restarting is iteration-count based and is distinct from restarts triggered by gradient nonorthogonality or failed descent tests.
The definition itself gives no convergence rate and does not require exact line searches.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(d_k^{\rm raw}=-g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}\). Fix a threshold \(\nu\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic nonlinear-CG. The test measures loss of the consecutive-gradient orthogonality characteristic of exact line searches on quadratic objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An orthogonality-based restart applies the normalized trigger \[\rho_k=\frac{|g_k^Tg_{k-1}|}{\|g_k\|^2}\geq\nu.\] When the trigger holds, the accepted coefficient and direction are \(\widehat\beta_k=0\) and \(d_k=-g_k\); otherwise \(\widehat\beta_k=\beta_k\) and \(d_k=d_k^{\rm raw}\). The test is defined when \(g_k\neq0\); if \(g_k=0\), the iteration has reached a stationary point rather than a restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthogonality-based restart compares the absolute inner product of consecutive gradients with the squared norm of the current gradient. If the normalized value reaches a chosen threshold, the method discards the conjugate correction and takes the negative current gradient. A zero current gradient is treated as stationarity, not as a restart event.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\frac{|g_k^Tg_{k-1}|}{\|g_k\|^2}\geq\nu\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\widehat\beta_k=0,\qquad d_k=-g_k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The no-restart condition is \(|g_k^Tg_{k-1}|<\nu\|g_k\|^2\).
The trigger detects that \(g_{k-1}\) has a component along \(g_k\) whose normalized magnitude is too large.
special_cases_latex: A commonly cited threshold is \(\nu=0.1\).
For a strictly convex quadratic with exact line searches in exact arithmetic, consecutive CG gradients are orthogonal, so \(\rho_k=0\) and this trigger is inactive.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every triggered direction satisfies \(g_k^Td_k=-\|g_k\|^2<0\) when \(g_k\neq0\).
Unlike a periodic restart, the spacing between orthogonality-triggered restarts is data dependent.
boundary_notes: Other normalized orthogonality tests use \(\|g_{k-1}\|^2\) or \(\|g_k\|\|g_{k-1}\|\) in the denominator; those are nearby variants, not the formula fixed here.
This trigger does not test the candidate direction directly and therefore does not guarantee that every untriggered direction is descending.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Truncation Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection of a raw nonlinear-CG coefficient onto an admissible iteration-dependent interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), compute a raw nonlinear-CG coefficient \(\widehat\beta_k\in\mathbb{R}\) and choose finite bounds \(\ell_k\le u_k\). Define the safeguarded coefficient and direction by
\[\beta_k=\min\{u_k,\max\{\ell_k,\widehat\beta_k\}\},\qquad d_k=-g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}.\]
If a descent test \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\le-\sigma\lVert g_k\rVert^2\), with fixed \(\sigma>0\), fails, replace \(\beta_k\) by \(0\) and output \(d_k=-g_k\). Otherwise pass \(d_k\) to the line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clip the raw CG coefficient to prescribed bounds, form the direction, and restart with negative gradient if the clipped direction still fails sufficient descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta_k\in[\ell_k,u_k]\), and the accepted output satisfies \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\le-\sigma\lVert g_k\rVert^2\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(d_k^{\rm raw}=-g_k+\beta_k^{\rm raw}d_{k-1}\) be a nonlinear-CG candidate direction. Let finite bounds \(\ell_k\leq u_k\) be determined from the current state or from a reference coefficient.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic nonlinear-CG. The safeguard acts on the scalar recurrence coefficient before the new direction is formed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coefficient truncation safeguard replaces the raw coefficient by its projection onto an admissible interval, \[\widehat\beta_k=\Pi_{[\ell_k,u_k]}(\beta_k^{\rm raw})=\min\{u_k,\max\{\ell_k,\beta_k^{\rm raw}\}\},\qquad d_k=-g_k+\widehat\beta_kd_{k-1}.\] The bounds are part of the method definition. Truncation includes one-sided clipping, such as \(\widehat\beta_k=\max\{\beta_k^{\rm PR},0\}\), and symmetric reference clipping, such as \(\ell_k=-\beta_k^{\rm FR}\), \(u_k=\beta_k^{\rm FR}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coefficient truncation safeguard projects the raw nonlinear-CG coefficient onto a specified closed interval and forms the direction with the projected value. It includes one-sided nonnegative clipping and clipping relative to the magnitude of a reference coefficient. The admissible interval must be specified as part of the method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\widehat\beta_k\in[\ell_k,u_k],\qquad d_k=-g_k+\widehat\beta_kd_{k-1}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The projected value solves \(\widehat\beta_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{b\in[\ell_k,u_k]}|b-\beta_k^{\rm raw}|\).
PR+ is the one-sided projection \(\Pi_{[0,\infty)}(\beta_k^{\rm PR})\).
special_cases_latex: FR–PR clipping uses \(\widehat\beta_k=\Pi_{[-\beta_k^{\rm FR},\beta_k^{\rm FR}]}(\beta_k^{\rm PR})\).
A forced restart is the degenerate interval \([\ell_k,u_k]=[0,0]\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The correction obeys \(\|\widehat\beta_kd_{k-1}\|\leq\max\{|\ell_k|,|u_k|\}\|d_{k-1}\|\).
Projection alone constrains coefficient growth but need not imply \(g_k^Td_k<0\) unless the bounds and line-search regime provide that property.
boundary_notes: A direction replacement performed only after a descent test is a direction safeguard, not merely coefficient truncation.
Unbounded intervals are allowed for one-sided clipping, but a finite two-sided interval is needed for an absolute coefficient bound.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\neq0\), and let \(\beta_k^{\rm raw}\) be a proposed nonlinear-CG coefficient. Fix coefficient bounds \(\ell_k\leq u_k\) and a direction constant \(\eta\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic nonlinear-CG. The system first limits the scalar coefficient and then validates the entire direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coefficient-direction safeguard system is the two-stage map \[\widetilde\beta_k=\Pi_{[\ell_k,u_k]}(\beta_k^{\rm raw}),\qquad \widetilde d_k=-g_k+\widetilde\beta_kd_{k-1},\] followed by \[(\widehat\beta_k,d_k)=\begin{cases}(\widetilde\beta_k,\widetilde d_k),&-g_k^T\widetilde d_k\geq\eta\|g_k\|\|\widetilde d_k\|,\\(0,-g_k),&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] Thus the candidate is accepted only if it is sufficiently downhill; otherwise both the coefficient and direction are replaced by their restart values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coefficient-direction safeguard first clips the proposed nonlinear-CG coefficient, forms the corresponding candidate direction, and then checks whether that direction makes a sufficiently acute angle with the negative gradient. If the check fails, it sets the coefficient to zero and uses the negative gradient. Both scalar growth and directional admissibility are therefore controlled.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The acceptance condition is \(\cos\theta_k\geq\eta\), where \(\theta_k\) is the angle between \(d_k\) and \(-g_k\).
A sufficient-descent variant replaces the normalized test by \(g_k^T\widetilde d_k\leq-c\|g_k\|^2\).
special_cases_latex: With \([\ell_k,u_k]=\mathbb R\), the construction becomes a pure direction safeguard.
With \(\eta=0\) interpreted as strict negativity, it accepts every strictly descending truncated candidate.
immediate_consequences_latex: The fallback always satisfies the normalized test with cosine equal to one.
Every accepted direction is a descent direction, so a sufficiently small positive step decreases \(f\) locally.
boundary_notes: The direction-angle test does not itself choose a step satisfying Armijo or Wolfe conditions.
If \(g_k=0\), the method should terminate; the normalized test is then undefined.

notation.meaning: Coefficient after truncation but before direction acceptance.
Required lower bound on the cosine with the negative gradient.

children.title: Denominator Degeneracy Protection
children.top_down_role: Protection against unreliable nonlinear-CG coefficient denominators.

knowledge_statements.title: Denominator Degeneracy Protection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity test for quotient-defined nonlinear-CG coefficients before division.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a raw nonlinear-CG coefficient has the quotient form \(\widehat\beta_k=N_k/D_k\). Given absolute and relative tolerances \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}>0\) and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}>0\), and a nonnegative scale \(S_k\), declare the denominator admissible exactly when
\[\lvert D_k\rvert>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}S_k.\]
Evaluate \(N_k/D_k\) only under this condition. If the condition fails, do not form the quotient; set \(\beta_k=0\) and use the restarted direction \(d_k=-g_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quotient coefficient is evaluated only when its denominator exceeds combined absolute and scale-relative tolerances; otherwise the method restarts without dividing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lvert D_k\rvert\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}S_k\Rightarrow(\beta_k=0\ \text{and}\ d_k=-g_k)\).

notation.meaning: Problem-scaled reference magnitude for the denominator.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports this mixed absolute-relative denominator test.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits denominator-degeneracy protection, but the mixed absolute-relative threshold, the unspecified scale S_k, and mandatory restart convention are design choices rather than a uniquely standard mathematical rule. They require a specific source.

children.title: Coefficient Magnitude Control
children.top_down_role: Restrictions on coefficient magnitudes produced by poorly scaled numerical data.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Magnitude Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-dependent cap on the inherited nonlinear-CG coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a proposed coefficient \(\widehat\beta_k\in\mathbb{R}\) and a finite cap \(B_k\ge0\), define
\[\beta_k=\operatorname{sgn}(\widehat\beta_k)\min\{\lvert\widehat\beta_k\rvert,B_k\}.\]
Equivalently, \(\beta_k\) is the Euclidean projection of \(\widehat\beta_k\) onto \([-B_k,B_k]\). The magnitude-control condition is therefore \(\lvert\beta_k\rvert\le B_k\); if \(B_k=0\), the recurrence is suppressed and \(d_k=-g_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the proposed coefficient onto a bounded symmetric interval. A zero cap suppresses the inherited direction and produces a steepest-descent restart.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lvert\beta_k\rvert\le B_k\), with \(B_k=0\Rightarrow d_k=-g_k\).
review_flags: No supplied locator identifies this symmetric coefficient-cap convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The symmetric projection formula correctly enforces the stated magnitude cap and fits the local safeguard container, but neither the symmetric-cap convention nor the choice of B_k is sourced. An authoritative locator for this particular control rule is required.

children.title: Direction Scaling Control
children.top_down_role: Scaling choices used to maintain numerically usable search directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Direction Scaling Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaling of the inherited CG component relative to the current gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_k\ne0\), let \(q_k=\beta_kd_{k-1}\), and fix \(\Delta>0\). Define
\[\tau_k=\begin{cases}1,&q_k=0,\\\min\left\{1,\dfrac{\Delta\lVert g_k\rVert}{\lVert q_k\rVert}\right\},&q_k\ne0,\end{cases}\qquad d_k=-g_k+\tau_kq_k.\]
Then the inherited component is bounded by
\[\lVert d_k+g_k\rVert=\lVert\tau_kq_k\rVert\le\Delta\lVert g_k\rVert,\]
and consequently \(\lVert d_k\rVert\le(1+\Delta)\lVert g_k\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale the inherited CG component so it cannot exceed a fixed multiple of the current gradient norm, thereby controlling the full direction norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert d_k+g_k\rVert\le\Delta\lVert g_k\rVert\) and \(\lVert d_k\rVert\le(1+\Delta)\lVert g_k\rVert\).
review_flags: No supplied source locator supports this particular norm-based scaling construction.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The norm bounds follow from the displayed scaling construction, but this is primarily a safeguard construction or condition rather than merely a property. More importantly, the particular scaling rule and parameter convention have no supporting source, so the mathematical version cannot yet be reviewed as established knowledge.

children.title: Restart Escalation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which local safeguards give way to a nonlinear-CG restart.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Escalation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary at which coefficient or direction safeguards escalate to a full restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(\sigma>0\) and \(\Gamma\ge1\). Let \(\widetilde d_k=-g_k+\widetilde\beta_kd_{k-1}\) be the direction remaining after denominator, coefficient, and scaling safeguards. Define the restart event
\[\mathcal R_k=\left\{g_k^{\mathsf T}\widetilde d_k>-\sigma\lVert g_k\rVert^2\right\}\cup\left\{\lVert\widetilde d_k\rVert>\Gamma\lVert g_k\rVert\right\}\cup\left\{\widetilde d_k\ \text{is not finite}\right\}.\]
The escalation rule is \(d_k=-g_k\) on \(\mathcal R_k\), and \(d_k=\widetilde d_k\) otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Escalate to a full negative-gradient restart when the safeguarded candidate lacks sufficient descent, is excessively large, or contains a nonfinite value.
assumptions_latex: \(\widetilde d_k\) is the candidate after lower-level safeguards.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_k\Rightarrow d_k=-g_k\); otherwise \(d_k=\widetilde d_k\).
review_flags: The supplied inventory lacks a locator for this composite escalation boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restart event is precise and fits the escalation-boundary container as a condition, but its union of descent, norm, and finiteness tests and the thresholds sigma and Gamma constitute a specific composite policy with no cited support.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable. At iteration \(k\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and let \(M_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite. Define the metric-scaled gradient \(z_k=M_kg_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth deterministic unconstrained minimization with fixed or iteration-dependent symmetric positive-definite inverse metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A metric-scaled nonlinear-CG method is a line-search iteration \[x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k,\qquad d_0=-z_0,\qquad d_k=-z_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}\quad(k\geq1),\] where \(z_k=M_kg_k\), \(M_k\succ0\), and \(\beta_k\) is a specified scaled nonlinear-CG coefficient computed from current and previous metric-gradient data. The positivity condition gives \(g_k^T(-z_k)=-g_k^TM_kg_k<0\) whenever \(g_k\neq0\); the conjugate correction may require a compatible line search or safeguard to preserve descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A metric-scaled nonlinear-CG method replaces the negative Euclidean gradient in the ordinary recurrence by the negative gradient transformed through a symmetric positive-definite inverse metric. It then adds a scalar multiple of the previous direction and performs a line search. The metric may be fixed or may vary by iteration, but the coefficient formula must state how the scaled data are paired.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[d_k=-M_kg_k+\beta_kd_{k-1},\qquad M_k=M_k^T\succ0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(W_k=M_k^{-1}\), the base direction is the solution of \(W_kz_k=g_k\), namely \(-z_k=-W_k^{-1}g_k\).
If \(M=C^{-1}C^{-T}\) is fixed, the method is ordinary nonlinear CG in coordinates \(z=Cx\), subject to the corresponding transformed coefficient formula.
special_cases_latex: The Euclidean family is recovered with \(M_k=I\).
A fixed preconditioner has \(M_k\equiv M\); a variable preconditioner permits \(M_k\) to depend on \(k\), \(x_k\), or stored curvature data.
immediate_consequences_latex: The restart direction \(-M_kg_k\) is descending for every nonzero gradient.
If \(mI\preceq M_k\preceq MI\), then \(-g_k^TM_kg_k\leq-m\|g_k\|^2\) and \(\|M_kg_k\|\leq M\|g_k\|\).
boundary_notes: Positive definiteness is essential for the scaled negative gradient to be unconditionally descending.
This family does not fix a unique coefficient; preconditioned FR-, PR-, HS-, and projection-based formulas are distinct members.

notation.meaning: Symmetric positive-definite inverse metric or preconditioning operator.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Metric Nonlinear-CG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioned nonlinear-CG using one fixed symmetric positive-definite metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite. Given \(x_0\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\), solve \(Mz_0=g_0\), and set \(d_0=-z_0\). For \(k\ge1\), solve \(Mz_k=g_k\), compute a selected preconditioned nonlinear-CG coefficient \(\beta_k\), and set
\[d_k=-z_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}.\]
Choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by a line search along \(d_k\), update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and stop when the prescribed stationarity test holds. A failed descent test triggers \(d_k=-z_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply a fixed positive-definite inverse metric to each gradient, then combine the preconditioned negative gradient with the preceding direction and restart when necessary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_k=-M^{-1}g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}\), with restart direction \(-M^{-1}g_k\).

notation.meaning: Fixed symmetric positive-definite metric or preconditioner.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable and let \(M=M^T\succ0\) be fixed throughout the iteration. Set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(z_k=Mg_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic unconstrained minimization with one fixed symmetric positive-definite inverse metric. The displayed coefficient is the fixed-metric Fletcher–Reeves member.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The fixed-metric Fletcher–Reeves nonlinear-CG method is \[d_0=-z_0,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k,\qquad \beta_{k+1}^{M\!FR}=\frac{g_{k+1}^TMg_{k+1}}{g_k^TMg_k},\qquad d_{k+1}=-z_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}^{M\!FR}d_k.\] The same matrix \(M\) is used at every iteration. If \(M=C^{-1}C^{-T}\), this recurrence is the Fletcher–Reeves construction in the fixed coordinates \(u=C^Tx\), with transformed gradient \(C^{-1}g_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-metric nonlinear CG chooses one symmetric positive-definite inverse metric and uses it at every iteration. The scaled gradient is the metric times the ordinary gradient, the initial direction is its negative, and the fixed-metric Fletcher–Reeves coefficient is the ratio of consecutive squared gradient norms in that metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[M_k\equiv M\succ0,\qquad d_{k+1}=-Mg_{k+1}+\frac{g_{k+1}^TMg_{k+1}}{g_k^TMg_k}d_k.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(W=M^{-1}=C^TC\), the scaled gradient solves \(Wz_k=g_k\).
The metric norm satisfies \(g_k^TMg_k=\|C^{-1}g_k\|^2\).
special_cases_latex: For \(M=I\), the method is ordinary Fletcher–Reeves nonlinear CG.
For a strictly convex quadratic and compatible exact line search, the recurrence is fixed-preconditioner linear CG.
immediate_consequences_latex: The restart direction satisfies \(g_k^T(-Mg_k)=-g_k^TMg_k<0\) whenever \(g_k\neq0\).
Because \(M\) is fixed, the coefficient is invariant under the associated single linear change of coordinates.
boundary_notes: If the metric changes with \(k\), the fixed-coordinate interpretation and this exact ratio no longer follow automatically.
The formula is undefined after stationarity because its denominator vanishes; the algorithm should terminate when \(g_k=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Preconditioned Nonlinear-CG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonlinear-CG with an iteration-dependent symmetric positive-definite preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\), choose \(M_0=M_0^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), solve \(M_0z_0=g_0\), and take \(d_0=-z_0\). At iteration \(k\ge1\), choose \(M_k=M_k^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), solve \(M_kz_k=g_k\), compute a coefficient \(\beta_k\) whose formula is defined for the variable-preconditioned recurrence, and set
\[d_k=-z_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}.\]
If \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\ge0\), restart with \(d_k=-z_k\). Otherwise perform the prescribed line search, update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and return an iterate satisfying the stopping test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The preconditioner may change each iteration; the coefficient must match that variable metric, and any non-descent candidate is replaced by the preconditioned negative gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_k=-M_k^{-1}g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}\), and the accepted direction satisfies \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k<0\).

notation.meaning: Coefficient chosen for the variable-preconditioned recurrence.

review_flags: No supplied locator specifically treats variable-preconditioned nonlinear conjugate gradients.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record identifies the high-level variable-preconditioned recurrence but leaves the coefficient only as one “defined for” that recurrence. Because variable preconditioning materially changes admissible coefficient formulas and convergence behavior, an authoritative source and a specific coefficient rule or explicitly scoped family definition are required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable. At iteration \(k\), choose \(W_k=W_k^T\succ0\), set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and solve \(W_kz_k=g_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic unconstrained minimization with an iteration-dependent symmetric positive-definite preconditioner. A coefficient rule must explicitly accommodate the varying preconditioned gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A variable-preconditioned nonlinear-CG method has the recurrence \[d_0=-z_0,\qquad d_{k+1}=-z_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}^{\rm VPCG}d_k,\qquad z_k=W_k^{-1}g_k,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k,\] where \(W_k\succ0\) may vary with \(k\), and \(\beta_{k+1}^{\rm VPCG}\) is a specified formula using data consistent with that variation. Equivalently, a projection form may be used, for example \[d_{k+1}=-\left(I-\frac{d_ky_k^T}{d_k^Ty_k}\right)W_{k+1}^{-1}g_{k+1},\qquad y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k,\] when \(d_k^Ty_k\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable-preconditioned nonlinear CG chooses a new symmetric positive-definite preconditioner as the iterations proceed, solves for the corresponding preconditioned gradient, and combines its negative with the preceding search direction. Because the preconditioner changes, the coefficient or projection formula must explicitly specify which current and previous scaled quantities it uses.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(M_k=W_k^{-1}\), the base direction is \(-M_kg_k\).
The displayed projection formula is a preconditioned Hestenes–Stiefel-type recurrence derived from transformed coordinates.
special_cases_latex: If \(W_k\equiv W\), the method reduces to fixed-metric nonlinear CG.
Diagonal, incomplete-factorization, and limited-memory quasi-Newton operators are possible choices when they remain positive definite.
immediate_consequences_latex: At a restart, \(d_k=-W_k^{-1}g_k\) and \(g_k^Td_k=-g_k^TW_k^{-1}g_k<0\).
Uniform spectral bounds on \(W_k\) give uniform norm equivalence between the Euclidean and preconditioned gradient norms.
boundary_notes: Substituting a varying preconditioner into the fixed-metric Fletcher–Reeves ratio is not automatically equivalent to a single coordinate transformation.
The projection formula requires \(d_k^Ty_k\neq0\) and may still require a descent safeguard.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Nonlinear-CG Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-scaled nonlinear-CG recurrence with an explicit positive scaling of the preconditioned gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), set \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\), choose \(M_0\succ0\) and \(\theta_0>0\), and define \(d_0=-\theta_0M_0^{-1}g_0\). For \(k\geq0\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by a line search, set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), \(g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1})\), and \(z_{k+1}=M_{k+1}^{-1}g_{k+1}\). Select an explicit scale \(\theta_{k+1}>0\) and nonlinear-CG coefficient \(\beta_{k+1}\), then update \[d_{k+1}=-\theta_{k+1}z_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k.\] Stop when \(\lVert g_{k+1}\rVert\leq\varepsilon\); otherwise continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale the preconditioned negative gradient explicitly, add the nonlinear-CG memory term, and use line search steps until the gradient tolerance is met.
assumptions_latex: \(M_k\) is symmetric positive definite and \(\theta_k>0\) for every \(k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioner–Scaling Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step compatibility condition ensuring sufficient descent for a scaled, preconditioned nonlinear-CG direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_k\succ0\), \(z_k=M_k^{-1}g_k\), and \(d_k=-\theta_kz_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}\), where \(\theta_k>0\). For a prescribed \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), the preconditioner, scaling, and memory coefficient are descent-compatible at iteration \(k\) when \[\beta_k g_k^{\mathsf T}d_{k-1}\leq(1-\sigma)\theta_k g_k^{\mathsf T}M_k^{-1}g_k.\] Under this predicate, \[g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\leq-\sigma\theta_k g_k^{\mathsf T}M_k^{-1}g_k<0\] whenever \(g_k\neq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The memory contribution must not consume more than a fixed fraction of the descent supplied by the scaled preconditioned gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\leq-\sigma\theta_k g_k^{\mathsf T}M_k^{-1}g_k<0\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathfrak M\) be a class of nonlinear-CG recurrences \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k\), with \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\). Let \(\mathfrak L\) be a class of line-search rules and \(\mathfrak F\) a class of smooth objectives.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A formal classification of deterministic finite-dimensional nonlinear-CG results, including descent, global stationarity, asymptotic rates, and boundaries between coefficient and line-search regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The convergence theory of a nonlinear-CG family is the collection \[\mathcal C=\{(M,L,F,H,Q):M\in\mathfrak M,\ L\in\mathfrak L,\ F\in\mathfrak F,\ H\text{ is a complete hypothesis set, and }H\Rightarrow Q\},\] where \(Q\) is an explicit conclusion such as descent \(g_k^Td_k<0\), sufficient descent, \(\liminf_k\|g_k\|=0\), convergence of accumulation points to stationarity, convergence of \(x_k\), or a stated local rate. Distinct coefficient formulas and line-search conditions define distinct members; conclusions are not transferred between members without their hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlinear-CG convergence theory is the indexed collection of formal results that pair a particular recurrence, line search, objective class, and complete set of assumptions with an explicit descent, stationarity, iterate-convergence, or rate conclusion. Results for different coefficients or line searches remain separate unless an implication between their hypotheses is established.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal C\subseteq\mathfrak M\times\mathfrak L\times\mathfrak F\times\mathfrak H\times\mathfrak Q,\qquad (M,L,F,H,Q)\in\mathcal C\Longleftrightarrow H\Rightarrow Q.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A convergence chart is the partial map \((M,L,F,H)\mapsto Q\) whose domain contains only supported method-regime combinations.
The global portion of \(\mathcal C\) records stationarity conclusions independent of proximity of \(x_0\); the local portion may assume that \(x_0\) lies near a nondegenerate minimizer.
special_cases_latex: The Fletcher–Reeves strong-Wolfe route records \(\liminf_k\|g_k\|=0\) under bounded-level-set and Lipschitz-gradient assumptions.
The exact-line-search routes for FR, restarted Crowder–Wolfe, and uniformly convex PRP have different hypotheses and conclusions.
immediate_consequences_latex: A descent lemma and a global convergence theorem are different records even when the former is used as a hypothesis of the latter.
A rate claim requires additional local structure and cannot be inferred merely from global stationarity.
boundary_notes: The definition is a theory-organizing object, not a universal theorem asserting convergence of every nonlinear-CG method.
Nonsmooth, stochastic, infinite-dimensional, and constrained variants are outside this scope unless separately indexed.

children.title: NCG Descent Preservation
children.top_down_role: Families of conditions and mechanisms ensuring that nonlinear-CG directions retain usable descent.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(d_k\) be the direction accepted by a nonlinear-CG recurrence at every nonstationary iteration.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic unconstrained minimization. The definition distinguishes ordinary descent from uniform angle and sufficient-descent properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear-CG method preserves descent on an index set \(K\) if \[g_k^Td_k<0\qquad\text{for every }k\in K\text{ with }g_k\neq0.\] It preserves sufficient descent if there is a constant \(c>0\), independent of \(k\), such that \[g_k^Td_k\leq-c\|g_k\|^2\qquad(k\in K).\] It preserves an angle condition if there is \(\delta>0\) such that \[-g_k^Td_k\geq\delta\|g_k\|\|d_k\|.\] A line search, coefficient formula, or safeguard is descent preserving when its stated hypotheses imply the relevant inequality for every generated nonstationary direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlinear CG preserves descent when every accepted direction has a strictly negative inner product with the current gradient. Stronger forms require either a uniform negative multiple of the squared gradient norm or a uniform positive cosine with the negative gradient. The quantifier covers every nonstationary generated iteration in the stated regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[g_k\neq0\Longrightarrow g_k^Td_k<0,\] with sufficient descent given by \(g_k^Td_k\leq-c\|g_k\|^2\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Ordinary descent is equivalent to the angle between \(d_k\) and \(-g_k\) being strictly less than \(\pi/2\).
The uniform angle condition is \(\cos\theta_k=-g_k^Td_k/(\|g_k\|\|d_k\|)\geq\delta\).
special_cases_latex: The restart direction \(d_k=-g_k\) has sufficient-descent constant \(c=1\).
For Fletcher–Reeves with strong Wolfe curvature constant \(c_2<1/2\), the source gives explicit two-sided bounds on \(g_k^Td_k/\|g_k\|^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For a continuously differentiable objective, every descent direction admits sufficiently small positive step lengths that decrease the objective.
Ordinary descent alone does not ensure a uniform angle bound or global convergence.
boundary_notes: The zero gradient is excluded from strict descent because every directional derivative is then zero.
A direction may be descending but nearly orthogonal to \(-g_k\), so the three properties are not interchangeable without additional bounds.

notation.meaning: Iteration indices on which the preservation property is asserted.
Angle between d_k and the negative gradient.

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search-Induced Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fletcher–Reeves descent bound induced by the strong Wolfe curvature condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(d_0=-g_0\) and \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_k^{\mathrm{FR}}d_{k-1}\), where \(\beta_k^{\mathrm{FR}}=\lVert g_k\rVert^2/\lVert g_{k-1}\rVert^2\). If every accepted step satisfies the strong Wolfe curvature condition with \(0<c_2<1/2\), then, before termination, \[-\frac{1}{1-c_2}\leq\frac{g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k}{\lVert g_k\rVert^2}\leq-\frac{1-2c_2}{1-c_2}.\] Consequently each \(d_k\) is a descent direction, with a uniform sufficient-descent constant determined by \(c_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For Fletcher–Reeves updates, a strong Wolfe line search with curvature constant below one half enforces uniform descent.
assumptions_latex: \(\lvert g_k^{\mathsf T}d_{k-1}\rvert\leq c_2\lvert g_{k-1}^{\mathsf T}d_{k-1}\rvert\) with \(0<c_2<1/2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\leq-\frac{1-2c_2}{1-c_2}\lVert g_k\rVert^2<0\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable and let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\). Consider \(d_0=-g_0\), \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_k^{FR}d_{k-1}\), where \(\beta_k^{FR}=\|g_k\|^2/\|g_{k-1}\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic Fletcher–Reeves nonlinear CG. Descent is induced by exact line-search orthogonality or by the strong Wolfe curvature restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Fletcher–Reeves recurrence has line-search-induced descent when the accepted step \(\alpha_{k-1}\) enforces either \[g_k^Td_{k-1}=0\] through exact line search, or the strong Wolfe conditions \[f(x_{k-1}+\alpha_{k-1}d_{k-1})\leq f(x_{k-1})+c_1\alpha_{k-1}g_{k-1}^Td_{k-1},\] \[|g_k^Td_{k-1}|\leq-c_2g_{k-1}^Td_{k-1},\qquad0<c_1<c_2<\tfrac12.\] Under the latter regime, every direction satisfies \[-\frac1{1-c_2}\leq\frac{g_k^Td_k}{\|g_k\|^2}\leq\frac{2c_2-1}{1-c_2}<0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fletcher–Reeves descent is induced by the line search when exact minimization makes the new gradient orthogonal to the preceding direction, or when a strong Wolfe step with curvature constant below one half controls the residual directional derivative. In the strong-Wolfe case, an explicit negative interval contains the normalized directional derivative at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[g_k^Td_k<0\quad\text{for every }k\text{ with }g_k\neq0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under exact line search, the recurrence identity becomes \(g_k^Td_k=-\|g_k\|^2\).
The upper strong-Wolfe bound supplies sufficient descent with \(c=(1-2c_2)/(1-c_2)>0\).
special_cases_latex: As \(c_2\downarrow0\), the normalized bounds approach the exact-line-search value \(-1\).
The conclusion applies specifically to the Fletcher–Reeves coefficient; strong Wolfe conditions alone do not guarantee descent for unmodified PRP.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every generated nonstationary FR direction is admissible as a local descent direction.
The explicit bound prevents the normalized directional derivative from approaching zero while \(c_2<1/2\) is fixed.
boundary_notes: The condition \(c_2<1/2\) is stronger than the usual generic strong-Wolfe allowance \(c_2<1\).
This definition states descent, not the separate global conclusion \(\liminf_k\|g_k\|=0\).

notation.meaning: Strong Wolfe sufficient-decrease and curvature constants.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Intrinsic Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dai–Yuan coefficient identity yielding descent once the Wolfe curvature denominator is positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\) and define \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DY}}d_k\), where \[\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DY}}=\frac{\lVert g_{k+1}\rVert^2}{d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k}.\] If \(d_k\) is a descent direction and the Wolfe curvature condition holds, then \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0\), and the update satisfies \[g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}d_{k+1}=\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DY}}g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k<0.\] Thus descent follows from the coefficient’s algebraic structure together with denominator positivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Dai–Yuan coefficient transfers the previous negative directional derivative to the new direction when Wolfe curvature makes its denominator positive.
assumptions_latex: The Wolfe curvature inequality \(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}d_k\geq c_2g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\) holds for some \(c_2\in(0,1)\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(g\neq0\) be a current gradient, let \(p\) be the preceding direction, and let \(\mathcal A\) be the set of states admitted by a coefficient formula, including its denominator and curvature conditions. Define \(d(\beta)=-g+\beta p\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An algebraic property of a nonlinear-CG coefficient rule relative to its explicitly stated admissible state set; no post hoc direction replacement is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear-CG coefficient rule \(\beta=B(g,g^-,p,y,\ldots)\) is coefficient-intrinsically descent preserving on \(\mathcal A\) if there exists \(c>0\) such that \[g^T\bigl(-g+B(g,g^-,p,y,\ldots)p\bigr)\leq-c\|g\|^2\] for every admissible state in \(\mathcal A\). The direction must satisfy the inequality directly from the coefficient formula and the defining admissibility conditions; no subsequent restart or clipping based on testing \(g^Td\) is allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coefficient rule has intrinsic descent when, for every state satisfying the rule's stated denominator and curvature conditions, substituting that coefficient into the two-term nonlinear-CG recurrence directly yields a uniform sufficient-descent inequality. A later test that rejects the direction is not part of intrinsic descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall s\in\mathcal A:\quad g(s)^Td(B(s))\leq-c\|g(s)\|^2<0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(g^Tp\neq0\), the condition is the scalar restriction \(\beta g^Tp\leq(1-c)\|g\|^2\).
Ordinary intrinsic descent is obtained by allowing a state-dependent positive constant instead of one uniform \(c\).
special_cases_latex: Under exact line-search orthogonality \(g^Tp=0\), every finite coefficient gives \(g^Td=-\|g\|^2\); this is line-search-induced rather than coefficient-discriminating.
Descent-preserving modern coefficients can satisfy an intrinsic bound on the state set defined by their Wolfe or curvature denominator conditions.
immediate_consequences_latex: No separate direction safeguard is needed to establish descent on \(\mathcal A\).
The property is lost if the method is applied outside the coefficient's admissible denominator or curvature regime.
boundary_notes: A coefficient that is descending only after clipping or restart belongs under safeguard-restored descent.

Because many nonlinear-CG descent results use line-search curvature assumptions, “intrinsic” here means intrinsic to the coefficient plus its declared admissible state, not independent of all line-search information.

notation.meaning: Admissible algebraic states for the coefficient rule.

source_refs.locator: Section 5.2, recurrence identity (5.42) and coefficient formulas (5.49)–(5.50) described as guaranteeing descent under Wolfe conditions, pp. 121–124

The admissible-state qualification is necessary because the cited coefficient guarantees retain line-search conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Safeguard-Restored Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient clipping or restart that restores a prescribed sufficient-descent inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(g_k\neq0\), a tentative coefficient \(\widehat\beta_k\), and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), form \(\widehat d_k=-g_k+\widehat\beta_kd_{k-1}\). If \(g_k^{\mathsf T}\widehat d_k\leq-\sigma\lVert g_k\rVert^2\), accept \(d_k=\widehat d_k\). Otherwise restart with \(d_k=-g_k\), or choose a clipped \(\beta_k\) satisfying \[\beta_k g_k^{\mathsf T}d_{k-1}\leq(1-\sigma)\lVert g_k\rVert^2\] and set \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}\). In either case the output obeys \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\leq-\sigma\lVert g_k\rVert^2<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept the proposed nonlinear-CG direction only if sufficiently descending; otherwise restart or clip its coefficient to restore descent.
assumptions_latex: A tentative nonlinear-CG coefficient \(\widehat\beta_k\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\leq-\sigma\lVert g_k\rVert^2<0\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\neq0\), and let \(\widetilde d_k=-g_k+\widetilde\beta_kd_{k-1}\) be a candidate direction. Fix \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth deterministic nonlinear-CG. The raw coefficient may be arbitrary; descent is guaranteed by an accept-or-restart rule applied after forming the candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A safeguard restores descent when the accepted direction is \[d_k=\begin{cases}\widetilde d_k,&g_k^T\widetilde d_k\leq-c\|g_k\|^2,\\-g_k,&g_k^T\widetilde d_k>-c\|g_k\|^2,\end{cases}\qquad \widehat\beta_k=\begin{cases}\widetilde\beta_k,&\widetilde d_k\text{ accepted},\\0,&\text{restart}.
\end{cases}\] Consequently, every accepted direction satisfies \(g_k^Td_k\leq-\min\{c,1\}\|g_k\|^2<0\). An angle-based version may instead require \(-g_k^T\widetilde d_k\geq\eta\|g_k\|\|\widetilde d_k\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Safeguard-restored descent forms a candidate nonlinear-CG direction and accepts it only if it satisfies a prescribed sufficient-descent or angle condition. Otherwise it resets the coefficient to zero and uses the negative gradient. Thus descent is guaranteed by the fallback even when the original coefficient formula can produce a non-descent direction.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The rule is an accept-or-project map from the candidate direction to the admissible set \(D_k=\{d:g_k^Td\leq-c\|g_k\|^2\}\), using \(-g_k\) as the designated feasible fallback.
With an angle test, the admissible set becomes \(D_k^\eta=\{d:-g_k^Td\geq\eta\|g_k\|\|d\|\}\).
special_cases_latex: A traditional nonlinear-CG implementation restarts whenever the recurrence produces a non-descent direction.
The sufficiently-downhill check of Gill–Murray–Wright uses a normalized angle bound and discards an unacceptable three-term direction.
immediate_consequences_latex: The method never sends a nonstationary iterate to a line search with an ascending direction.
The fallback requires no division and remains defined when a coefficient denominator is unusable.
boundary_notes: This definition does not assert that the raw coefficient is stable or that the safeguard is triggered only finitely often.
At \(g_k=0\), termination replaces the safeguard because strict descent is impossible.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Family of nonlinear-CG global convergence statements
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), where \(d_k\) is generated by a specified nonlinear-CG coefficient family and \(\alpha_k\) by a specified line search.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth deterministic nonlinear-CG. “Global” concerns admissible starting points rather than global minimization, and conclusions may range from a stationary accumulation point to full iterate convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An NCG global convergence theorem family is an indexed set \[\mathfrak T=\{(B,L,H,Q)\},\] where \(B\) fixes the coefficient or restart rule, \(L\) fixes the exact, Wolfe, or strong-Wolfe line-search regime, \(H\) states all objective and level-set assumptions, and \(Q\) is one of the explicit conclusions \[\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|g_k\|=0,\qquad \exists\bar x\in\operatorname{acc}\{x_k\}:\nabla f(\bar x)=0,\qquad \text{or}\qquad x_k\to x^*,\ \nabla f(x^*)=0.\] Membership requires the exact method-regime implication \(H(B,L,f,x_0)\Rightarrow Q\); no conclusion is inherited merely because two methods coincide on quadratics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonlinear-CG global convergence theorem family is the indexed collection of method-specific implications. Each member fixes a coefficient or restart rule, a compatible line search, all smoothness and boundedness assumptions, and an explicit stationarity or iterate-convergence conclusion. Different coefficient and line-search routes are separate members.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(B,L,H,Q)\in\mathfrak T\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad H(B,L,f,x_0)\Longrightarrow Q.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The family is a relation, rather than a single theorem, because the same conclusion can require different hypotheses for FR, PRP, restarted, and modern descent-preserving methods.
A theorem concluding only \(\liminf_k\|g_k\|=0\) is weaker than one asserting that every accumulation point is stationary or that \(x_k\) converges.
special_cases_latex: FR with exact line search on a bounded level set has stationary accumulation-point conclusions in the cited source.
Restarted Crowder–Wolfe with exact line search and Lipschitz gradient, and uniformly convex PRP with exact line search, form distinct routes.
FR with strong Wolfe conditions and \(c_2<1/2\) yields \(\liminf_k\|g_k\|=0\) under standard bounded-level-set and Lipschitz-gradient assumptions.
immediate_consequences_latex: The coefficient formula, line search, and conclusion strength must all be retained when comparing family members.
A counterexample or boundary for one coefficient family does not automatically invalidate another member.
boundary_notes: Global convergence does not mean convergence to a global minimizer for a nonconvex objective.
Rate statements are not part of this family unless appended as separate local or complexity conclusions.

notation.meaning: Specified nonlinear-CG coefficient or restart rule.
Explicit global stationarity or convergence conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Fletcher–Reeves Convergence Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global first-order convergence of Fletcher–Reeves nonlinear CG under strong Wolfe search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be bounded below on the level set containing the iterates, and suppose \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz continuous on a neighborhood of that set. Generate \(d_0=-g_0\), \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_k^{\mathrm{FR}}d_{k-1}\), with \(\beta_k^{\mathrm{FR}}=\lVert g_k\rVert^2/\lVert g_{k-1}\rVert^2\), and choose steps satisfying the strong Wolfe conditions with \(0<c_1<c_2<1/2\). If no iterate is stationary, then \[\liminf_{k\to\infty}\lVert g_k\rVert=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fletcher–Reeves nonlinear CG with a sufficiently restrictive strong Wolfe search has gradient norms approaching zero along a subsequence.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable, bounded below on the initial level set, and has Lipschitz gradient nearby.
The Fletcher–Reeves recurrence uses strong Wolfe steps with \(0<c_1<c_2<1/2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert=0\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(\mathcal L=\{x:f(x)\leq f(x_0)\}\). Define \(d_0=-g_0\), \(\beta_{k+1}^{FR}=\|g_{k+1}\|^2/\|g_k\|^2\), and \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}^{FR}d_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth deterministic Fletcher–Reeves nonlinear CG with an inexact strong-Wolfe line search. This route concludes subsequential first-order stationarity, not convergence of the entire iterate sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The strong-Wolfe Fletcher–Reeves convergence route is the method-regime tuple in which \(\mathcal L\) is bounded, \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz continuous on an open neighborhood of \(\mathcal L\), and every step satisfies \[f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\leq f(x_k)+c_1\alpha_kg_k^Td_k,\qquad |g_{k+1}^Td_k|\leq-c_2g_k^Td_k,\] with \(0<c_1<c_2<\tfrac12\). Its associated global conclusion is \[\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|\nabla f(x_k)\|=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Fletcher–Reeves strong-Wolfe route combines the standard Fletcher–Reeves recurrence with a bounded initial level set, Lipschitz continuity of the gradient near that set, and strong Wolfe steps whose curvature constant is below one half. The route's conclusion is that a subsequence of gradient norms approaches zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|\nabla f(x_k)\|=0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: There exists a subsequence \(\{k_j\}\) such that \(\|\nabla f(x_{k_j})\|\to0\).
The gradient sequence cannot remain uniformly bounded away from zero.
special_cases_latex: With exact line search, \(g_{k+1}^Td_k=0\), and a source-supported FR route gives stationary accumulation-point conclusions under bounded-level-set assumptions.
Periodic restarting with uniformly bounded cycle length supplies another route to the same liminf-type conclusion through restart subsequences.
immediate_consequences_latex: The strong-Wolfe curvature condition also makes every FR direction descending.
If a subsequence \(x_{k_j}\) converges and \(\|g_{k_j}\|\to0\), continuity of the gradient makes its limit stationary.
boundary_notes: The conclusion does not assert \(\|g_k\|\to0\), convergence of \(x_k\), or attainment of a global minimum.
The restriction \(c_2<1/2\) is part of this route and must not be weakened to the generic strong-Wolfe condition \(c_2<1\) without another theorem.

knowledge_statements.title: Polak–Ribière-Type Convergence Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded Polak–Ribière-plus route using sufficient descent and controlled directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_{k-1}=g_k-g_{k-1}\) and \(\beta_k^{\mathrm{PR+}}=\max\{0,g_k^{\mathsf T}y_{k-1}/\lVert g_{k-1}\rVert^2\}\). Suppose the resulting directions, possibly after restart or clipping, satisfy \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\leq-\sigma\lVert g_k\rVert^2\) and \(\lVert d_k\rVert\leq C\lVert g_k\rVert\) for fixed \(\sigma,C>0\). If \(f\) is bounded below, its gradient is Lipschitz on the relevant level set, and the steps satisfy the Wolfe conditions, then \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert g_k\rVert^2<\infty,\qquad \lim_{k\to\infty}\lVert g_k\rVert=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A safeguarded PR-plus method converges globally when sufficient descent, controlled direction lengths, Wolfe steps, and standard smoothness assumptions hold.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below on the initial level set and has Lipschitz gradient nearby.
Wolfe steps are used, and fixed \(\sigma,C>0\) give sufficient descent and \(\lVert d_k\rVert\leq C\lVert g_k\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert=0\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuously differentiable, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and the nonlinear-CG iteration is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), \(p_0=-g_0\), \(p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}p_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition covers unconstrained, deterministic, smooth nonlinear conjugate-gradient methods using the Polak–Ribière coefficient or its nonnegative truncation. It distinguishes the recurrence from any particular convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Polak–Ribière-type convergence route is the nonlinear-CG recurrence with \[\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PR}}=\frac{g_{k+1}^{T}(g_{k+1}-g_k)}{\|g_k\|^2},\qquad g_k\ne0,\] or the safeguarded coefficient \[\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PR+}}=\max\{\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PR}},0\}.\] The step \(\alpha_k>0\) is supplied by a specified line search. The route is called descent-preserving when \(g_k^Tp_k<0\) for every nonstationary iterate, and globally stationary when its stated hypotheses imply \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|g_k\|=0\) or the stronger limit \(\|g_k\|\to0\). PR and PR+ are distinct routes because ordinary strong Wolfe conditions alone do not generally ensure descent for untruncated PR, whereas an appropriate modification combined with PR+ can enforce descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth unconstrained objective, a Polak–Ribière-type route uses the nonlinear-CG recurrence with coefficient \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PR}}=g_{k+1}^{T}(g_{k+1}-g_k)/\|g_k\|^2\), or its safeguarded version \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PR+}}=\max\{\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PR}},0\}\). A line search chooses \(\alpha_k>0\). The route is descent-preserving if \(g_k^Tp_k<0\) at every nonstationary iterate, and globally stationary if its accompanying assumptions yield \(\liminf_k\|g_k\|=0\) or \(\|g_k\|\to0\). The untruncated and truncated routes must be distinguished because ordinary strong Wolfe conditions do not by themselves guarantee descent for PR.
assumptions_latex: \(\alpha_k>0\) is chosen by an explicitly specified exact or inexact line search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta_{k+1}\in\{\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PR}},\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PR+}}\}\) together with \(p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}p_k\) defines the Polak–Ribière-type route.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\), \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PR}}=g_{k+1}^Ty_k/(g_k^Tg_k)\).
special_cases_latex: For a strictly convex quadratic and exact line searches, the PR coefficient agrees with the Fletcher–Reeves coefficient in exact arithmetic.
If \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PR}}<0\), PR+ sets \(p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}\), producing a steepest-descent restart.
immediate_consequences_latex: When \(g_{k+1}\approx g_k\), one has \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PR}}\approx0\), so the next direction is close to \(-g_{k+1}\).
boundary_notes: The definition alone does not assert convergence on general nonconvex objectives; unmodified PR can fail even with an ideal line search.
Nonsmooth, stochastic, constrained, and inexact-gradient variants are outside this scope.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative truncation of the Polak–Ribière coefficient.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\), and \(p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}p_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the smooth, unconstrained, deterministic family distinguished by the Hestenes–Stiefel and Dai–Yuan denominators. A denominator must be nonzero whenever its coefficient is evaluated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Hestenes–Stiefel–Dai–Yuan family consists of nonlinear-CG recurrences using either \[\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{HS}}=\frac{g_{k+1}^Ty_k}{y_k^Tp_k}\] or \[\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DY}}=\frac{\|g_{k+1}\|^2}{y_k^Tp_k},\] followed by \(p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}p_k\). The HS coefficient imposes conjugacy of \(p_{k+1}\) and \(p_k\) with respect to the average Hessian along the accepted segment when that Hessian representation is valid. The DY member uses the same secant denominator but the squared new-gradient norm in the numerator. A convergence route based on either member additionally specifies a line-search condition, a denominator safeguard or restart rule, and the stationarity conclusion being sought.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Hestenes–Stiefel–Dai–Yuan family uses the nonlinear-CG recurrence with either \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{HS}}=g_{k+1}^Ty_k/(y_k^Tp_k)\) or \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DY}}=\|g_{k+1}\|^2/(y_k^Tp_k)\), where \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\). HS is associated with conjugacy relative to the average Hessian along the accepted step; DY retains the secant denominator but changes the numerator. A complete convergence route must also state its line search, denominator safeguard or restart, and stationarity target.
assumptions_latex: \(y_k^Tp_k\ne0\) whenever an HS or DY coefficient is formed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta_{k+1}\in\{\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{HS}},\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DY}}\}\) defines the named coefficient family.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(f\in C^2\), then \(y_k=\alpha_k\bar G_kp_k\), where \(\bar G_k=\int_0^1\nabla^2f(x_k+t\alpha_kp_k)\,dt\); the HS formula is the coefficient satisfying \(p_{k+1}^T\bar G_kp_k=0\).
special_cases_latex: On a strictly convex quadratic with exact line searches, HS reduces to the classical linear-CG coefficient.
The DY formula is equation (5.49) in the cited source.
immediate_consequences_latex: A zero or numerically tiny value of \(y_k^Tp_k\) makes the raw coefficients undefined or unstable and therefore requires a safeguard.
boundary_notes: The formulas alone do not supply global convergence; the relevant Wolfe conditions and descent properties must be stated separately.
Hybrid, truncated, and preconditioned variants are not identified solely by these two raw coefficients.

notation.meaning: Average Hessian along the accepted line-search segment.

knowledge_statements.title: Hestenes–Stiefel Convergence Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded Hestenes–Stiefel route under strong Wolfe search and uniform direction control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y_{k-1}=g_k-g_{k-1}\) and define the Hestenes–Stiefel trial coefficient by \[\widehat\beta_k^{\mathrm{HS}}=\frac{g_k^{\mathsf T}y_{k-1}}{d_{k-1}^{\mathsf T}y_{k-1}}.\] Suppose a restart or clipping safeguard produces \(d_k=-g_k+\beta_kd_{k-1}\) satisfying \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\leq-\sigma\lVert g_k\rVert^2\) and \(\lVert d_k\rVert\leq C\lVert g_k\rVert\). If \(f\) is bounded below with Lipschitz gradient on the relevant level set and strong Wolfe steps are used, then \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\lVert g_k\rVert=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A safeguarded Hestenes–Stiefel method is globally convergent when strong Wolfe steps, sufficient descent, and bounded relative direction lengths are enforced.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below on the initial level set and has Lipschitz gradient nearby.
Strong Wolfe steps are used and safeguards enforce fixed sufficient-descent and direction-norm bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{k\to\infty}\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dai–Yuan Convergence Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global subsequential convergence of Dai–Yuan nonlinear CG under Wolfe search, with stationary termination treated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and set \(d_0=-g_0\). At every nonstationary iteration \(k\geq0\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfying the Wolfe conditions, set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and define \[d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DY}}d_k,\qquad \beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DY}}=\frac{\lVert g_{k+1}\rVert^2}{d_k^{\mathsf T}(g_{k+1}-g_k)}.\] Suppose \(f\) is bounded below on the initial level set and \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz continuous on a neighborhood of that set. If some \(g_j=0\), the method has reached a stationary point. Otherwise, when the Wolfe constants satisfy \(0<c_1<c_2<1\), the denominators are positive, every \(d_k\) is a descent direction, and \[\liminf_{k\to\infty}\lVert g_k\rVert=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard smoothness and Wolfe search, Dai–Yuan nonlinear CG either reaches a stationary iterate or generates descending directions whose gradient norms approach zero along a subsequence.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuously differentiable, is bounded below on the initial level set, and has Lipschitz-continuous gradient on a neighborhood of that set.
At every nonstationary iteration, the step satisfies the Wolfe conditions with \(0<c_1<c_2<1\).
The Dai–Yuan recurrence is initialized by \(d_0=-g_0\), where \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either \(g_j=0\) for some \(j\), or \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k<0\) for every \(k\) and \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Shared Line-Search Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong Wolfe conditions commonly supporting Hestenes–Stiefel and Dai–Yuan convergence routes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an iterate \(x_k\), descent direction \(d_k\), and trial step \(\alpha_k>0\), the shared strong Wolfe regime requires constants \(0<c_1<c_2<1\) such that \[f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\leq f(x_k)+c_1\alpha_k g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\] and \[\left|\nabla f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)^{\mathsf T}d_k\right|\leq c_2\left|g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\right|.\] The ordinary Wolfe regime replaces the absolute-value inequality by \(\nabla f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)^{\mathsf T}d_k\geq c_2g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The shared regime combines sufficient decrease with either Wolfe curvature or its stronger absolute-value form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha_k\) satisfies sufficient decrease and the selected Wolfe curvature inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Route-Specific Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Denominator and curvature failures separating the Hestenes–Stiefel and Dai–Yuan routes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Both coefficients contain \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\) in the denominator, but their failure effects differ. If Wolfe curvature is absent, one may have \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\leq0\), so the Dai–Yuan coefficient is nonpositive or undefined and its inherited-descent identity no longer certifies descent. Even when \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0\), values approaching zero can make the Hestenes–Stiefel coefficient \(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}y_k/(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k)\) arbitrarily large, destroying uniform direction bounds. Thus denominator positivity supports Dai–Yuan descent, whereas Hestenes–Stiefel generally also requires clipping, restart, or quantitative denominator control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without curvature, Dai–Yuan can lose denominator positivity; Hestenes–Stiefel can additionally become unbounded when a positive denominator approaches zero.
assumptions_latex: The relevant update uses a denominator \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\leq0\) invalidates the Dai–Yuan descent route, while \(d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\downarrow0\) can destabilize Hestenes–Stiefel.

notation.meaning: curvature denominator shared by the two coefficients

knowledge_statements.title: Descent-Preserving Modern Convergence Routes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coefficient-independent convergence template for safeguarded modern nonlinear-CG updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\) be any nonlinear-CG-type method. Suppose \(f\) is bounded below on the initial level set, \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz continuous nearby, and Wolfe steps are used. If fixed constants \(\sigma,C>0\) satisfy \[g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\leq-\sigma\lVert g_k\rVert^2,\qquad \lVert d_k\rVert\leq C\lVert g_k\rVert\] for every nonstationary iterate, then the Zoutendijk summability condition implies \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert g_k\rVert^2<\infty.\] Hence \(\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert\to0\), independently of the particular safeguarded coefficient formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any modern nonlinear-CG formula converges globally if safeguards uniformly preserve descent and control direction length under Wolfe search and standard smoothness.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below on the initial level set and has Lipschitz gradient nearby.
Uniform sufficient descent and \(\lVert d_k\rVert\leq C\lVert g_k\rVert\) hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert^2<\infty\) and \(\lVert\nabla f(x_k)\rVert\to0\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), set \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\), \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), and \(p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}p_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition concerns smooth unconstrained nonlinear-CG formulas designed so that descent follows from standard Wolfe-type line searches, rather than from exact minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A descent-preserving modern convergence route is a nonlinear-CG coefficient and line-search pair for which every nonstationary generated direction satisfies a uniform sufficient-descent inequality \[-g_k^Tp_k\ge \eta\|g_k\|^2\quad\text{for some fixed }\eta>0.\] A canonical member is the Hager–Zhang-type coefficient \[\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{HZ}}=\left(y_k-2p_k\frac{\|y_k\|^2}{y_k^Tp_k}\right)^T\frac{g_{k+1}}{y_k^Tp_k},\qquad y_k^Tp_k\ne0.\] The route includes an explicit Wolfe line search and a safeguard when the denominator is too small. Its convergence designation records whether the supported conclusion is subsequential stationarity, \(\liminf_k\|g_k\|=0\), or full gradient convergence, \(\|g_k\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A modern descent-preserving nonlinear-CG route pairs a coefficient formula and a Wolfe-type line search so that every nonstationary direction satisfies \(-g_k^Tp_k\ge\eta\|g_k\|^2\) for a fixed \(\eta>0\). A canonical member is the Hager–Zhang-type coefficient \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{HZ}}=(y_k-2p_k\|y_k\|^2/(y_k^Tp_k))^Tg_{k+1}/(y_k^Tp_k)\). The route must specify a safeguard for a small denominator and whether its convergence conclusion is subsequential or full stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(y_k^Tp_k\ne0\) when the raw coefficient is evaluated.
The step length satisfies the stated Wolfe conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining invariant is \(-g_k^Tp_k\ge\eta\|g_k\|^2>0\) at every nonstationary iterate.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The sufficient-descent condition is equivalent to \(g_k^Tp_k\le-\eta\|g_k\|^2\).
special_cases_latex: The Dai–Yuan coefficient \(\|g_{k+1}\|^2/(y_k^Tp_k)\) is another cited modern formula with descent properties under Wolfe conditions.
immediate_consequences_latex: Sufficient descent excludes ascent directions and directions orthogonal to \(-g_k\) unless their norm becomes unbounded relative to \(\|g_k\|\).
boundary_notes: Descent alone is not a complete global-convergence theorem; level-set regularity and line-search assumptions remain necessary.
Finite-precision implementations require an explicit denominator tolerance not fixed by the mathematical formula.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider nonlinear-CG iterates \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) for a differentiable unconstrained objective \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition classifies convergence statements by objective geometry and line-search accuracy. It does not claim that every nonlinear-CG coefficient converges in every regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The nonlinear-CG convergence regime family is the ordered classification \(\mathcal R=\{\mathcal R_Q,\mathcal R_{SC},\mathcal R_{NC}\}\), where: \(\mathcal R_Q\) is the strictly convex quadratic, exact-line-search, exact-arithmetic regime; \(\mathcal R_{SC}\) is the smooth strongly convex regime, with exact or explicitly controlled inexact line searches and rate conclusions stated in a chosen error measure; and \(\mathcal R_{NC}\) is the general smooth nonconvex regime, where the standard global target is first-order stationarity, commonly \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|\nabla f(x_k)\|=0\). A convergence statement belongs to one regime only after identifying the coefficient formula, descent condition, line-search rule, regularity assumptions, and exact conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonlinear-CG convergence regime family separates three settings: \(\mathcal R_Q\), strictly convex quadratics with exact line searches and exact arithmetic; \(\mathcal R_{SC}\), smooth strongly convex objectives with a stated line-search accuracy and rate measure; and \(\mathcal R_{NC}\), general smooth nonconvex objectives, for which the usual global target is \(\liminf_k\|\nabla f(x_k)\|=0\). A valid convergence statement must additionally identify the coefficient, descent condition, line search, regularity assumptions, and conclusion.
assumptions_latex: The nonlinear-CG coefficient and line-search rule are specified for the particular member being classified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_Q\), \(\mathcal R_{SC}\), and \(\mathcal R_{NC}\) distinguish finite-termination, rate, and stationarity analyses, respectively.
