knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Finite-Termination Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic finite termination of linear conjugate gradients on a positive-definite quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12 x^{\mathsf T}Ax-b^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive definite, and let \(g_k=Ax_k-b\). If \(g_0=0\), stop with \(x_0=x_*\). Otherwise set \(d_0=-g_0\). At every nonterminal iteration, choose \(\alpha_k=-(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k)/(d_k^{\mathsf T}Ad_k)\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and compute \(g_{k+1}=Ax_{k+1}-b\). If \(g_{k+1}=0\), stop; otherwise set \(\beta_{k+1}=\|g_{k+1}\|_2^2/\|g_k\|_2^2\) and \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k\). In exact arithmetic, the generated nonzero directions are mutually \(A\)-conjugate, and the method reaches the unique minimizer \(x_*=A^{-1}b\) after at most \(n\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In exact arithmetic, conjugate gradients with exact line searches either recognizes an initially stationary point or minimizes an SPD quadratic within at most the ambient dimension, and its generated nonzero directions are mutually conjugate.
assumptions_latex: Arithmetic and line searches are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(m\in\{0,1,\ldots,n\}\) such that \(x_m=x_*\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^TAx-b^Tx+c\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(A=A^T\succ0\), and let \(x_*=A^{-1}b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The regime is finite-dimensional and assumes exact arithmetic and exact one-dimensional minimization. It identifies when nonlinear-CG formulas reduce to linear conjugate gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The quadratic finite-termination regime consists of iterations initialized with \(p_0=-g_0\), where \(g_k=Ax_k-b\), and updated by \[x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k,\qquad \alpha_k=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}f(x_k+\alpha p_k),\] \[p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}p_k,\] with a coefficient that coincides with the linear-CG coefficient under exact line search. In exact arithmetic, the generated nonzero directions are \(A\)-conjugate, and the regime's defining termination property is the existence of \(m\le n\) such that \(x_m=x_*\). More sharply, if \(A\) has \(r\) distinct eigenvalues, one may take \(m\le r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quadratic finite-termination regime uses a strictly convex quadratic \(f(x)=x^TAx/2-b^Tx+c\) with \(A\) symmetric positive definite, initial direction \(p_0=-g_0\), exact line searches, exact arithmetic, and a nonlinear-CG coefficient that reduces to linear CG. The nonzero directions are \(A\)-conjugate, and an iterate equals the unique minimizer after at most \(n\) steps; if \(A\) has only \(r\) distinct eigenvalues, at most \(r\) steps are needed.
assumptions_latex: All arithmetic and line searches are exact.
\(p_0=-g_0\), and the selected coefficient reduces to linear CG on the quadratic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists m\le n\) such that \(x_m=x_*\); if \(A\) has \(r\) distinct eigenvalues, \(m\le r\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Finite termination is equivalent to \(g_m=Ax_m-b=0\).
It is also equivalent to \(\|x_m-x_*\|_A=0\), where \(\|v\|_A=(v^TAv)^{1/2}\).
special_cases_latex: PR and HS reduce to the Fletcher–Reeves coefficient on a strictly convex quadratic with exact line searches.
immediate_consequences_latex: The minimizer is unique because \(A\succ0\).
A restart with \(p=-g\) inside an exactly quadratic region reinitializes the finite-termination mechanism.
boundary_notes: The result is an exact-arithmetic property; rounding error can destroy conjugacy and finite termination.
For a nonquadratic smooth objective, the nearby analogue is an asymptotic multi-step rate, not literal finite termination.

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Rate Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear convergence under uniform descent, direction bounds, and Armijo backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and let \(f_*=\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\). Suppose directions satisfy \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\le-c\|g_k\|_2^2\) and \(\|d_k\|_2\le C\|g_k\|_2\) for fixed \(c,C>0\). From an initial trial step \(A_k\ge\bar\alpha>0\), let Armijo backtracking with \(\sigma,\rho\in(0,1)\) choose \(\alpha_k\in\{A_k,\rho A_k,\rho^2A_k,\ldots\}\) satisfying \(f(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\le f(x_k)+\sigma\alpha_k g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). Then \(\alpha_k\ge\alpha_{\min}:=\rho\min\{\bar\alpha,2(1-\sigma)c/(LC^2)\}\), and \[f(x_{k+1})-f_*\le q\bigl(f(x_k)-f_*\bigr),\qquad q:=1-2\mu\sigma c\alpha_{\min}\in[0,1).\] Consequently, the objective residual converges globally Q-linearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strongly convex smooth objective, uniformly gradient-related directions combined with explicitly specified Armijo backtracking give a uniform positive step bound and a global Q-linear contraction of the objective residual.
assumptions_latex: Armijo backtracking uses fixed \(\sigma,\rho\in(0,1)\) and initial trials \(A_k\ge\bar\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(k\ge0\), \(f(x_k)-f_*\le q^k\bigl(f(x_0)-f_*\bigr)\) with \(q\in[0,1)\).

notation.meaning: uniform lower bound on accepted step lengths

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) have unique minimizer \(x_*\), and let \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) be generated by a specified nonlinear-CG method.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition describes the assumptions and error measures of the strongly convex rate regime; it does not assign a universal rate to every nonlinear-CG coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A nonlinear-CG analysis is in the strongly convex rate regime when there exist constants \(0<\mu\le L<\infty\) such that, on a set containing all iterates, \[f(y)\ge f(x)+
abla f(x)^T(y-x)+ rac{\mu}{2}\|y-x\|^2,\qquad \|
abla f(y)-
abla f(x)\|\le L\|y-x\|.\] A rate statement in this regime must specify a nonnegative error measure \(E_k\), such as \(f(x_k)-f(x_*)\), \(\|x_k-x_*\|\), or \(\|
abla f(x_k)\|\), and an explicit estimate such as \(E_{k+1}\leho E_k\) with \(0<ho<1\), or a multi-step analogue. The coefficient and exact or inexact line-search assumptions are part of the regime specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear-CG analysis lies in the strongly convex rate regime when the objective is \(\mu\)-strongly convex and has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient on a set containing the iterates. A complete rate statement identifies an error measure, such as objective error, distance to the unique minimizer, or gradient norm, and gives an explicit one-step or multi-step contraction. The coefficient formula and line-search accuracy must be stated because strong convexity alone does not give one universal nonlinear-CG rate.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on the relevant set.
The nonlinear-CG coefficient and line-search rule are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A supported rate is expressed as an explicit bound on a declared error measure \(E_k\), not merely as \(x_k\to x_*\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(f\in C^2\), the inequalities \(\mu I\preceq\nabla^2f(x)\preceq LI\) on the relevant convex set imply the stated strong-convexity and Lipschitz-gradient conditions.
special_cases_latex: For a positive-definite quadratic, \(\mu=\lambda_{\min}(A)\) and \(L=\lambda_{\max}(A)\).
The cited source states full gradient convergence for Polak–Ribière under strong convexity and exact line search.
immediate_consequences_latex: Strong convexity gives a unique minimizer \(x_*\).
Objective error, distance, and gradient norm are quantitatively comparable up to constants depending on \(\mu\) and \(L\).
boundary_notes: No coefficient-independent contraction factor is asserted.
General convex objectives with \(\mu=0\) and general nonconvex objectives lie outside this regime.

knowledge_statements.title: General Nonconvex Stationarity Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zoutendijk-type stationarity for nonlinear CG with uniformly gradient-related directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable and bounded below on the level set \(\mathcal L_0:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}\), and suppose \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz continuous on an open set containing \(\mathcal L_0\). Define \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), choose nonzero directions \(d_k\) satisfying \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k<0\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\) satisfying the Wolfe conditions with fixed parameters \(0<c_1<c_2<1\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). If \(-g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\ge\delta\|g_k\|_2\|d_k\|_2\) for a fixed \(\delta>0\), then \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k)^2}{\|d_k\|_2^2}<\infty\] and consequently \(\|g_k\|_2\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth objective bounded below on the initial level set, Wolfe steps and a uniform angle bound between each negative gradient and search direction imply a finite Zoutendijk sum and convergence of the gradient norms to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below on \(\mathcal L_0\), and \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz continuous on an open set containing \(\mathcal L_0\).
Directions are nonzero descent directions, and accepted steps satisfy the Wolfe conditions with fixed \(0<c_1<c_2<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k)^2/\|d_k\|_2^2<\infty\) and \(\|g_k\|_2\to0\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). Define \(\mathcal L_0=\{x:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This regime permits nonconvex smooth objectives. Its usual global conclusion is first-order stationarity or subsequential stationarity, not convergence to a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The general nonconvex stationarity regime consists of line-search nonlinear-CG analyses in which \(\mathcal L_0\) is bounded, \(f\) is continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of \(\mathcal L_0\), and \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz continuous there. Directions are required to be descent directions, \(g_k^Tp_k<0\), and accepted steps satisfy stated Wolfe conditions. The canonical global target is \[\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|g_k\|=0.\] A stronger route may establish \(\|g_k\|\to0\), but this must be stated separately. Under these assumptions, the associated Zoutendijk summability relation is \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\cos^2\theta_k\,\|g_k\|^2<\infty,\qquad \cos\theta_k=\frac{-g_k^Tp_k}{\|g_k\|\|p_k\|}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The general smooth nonconvex stationarity regime assumes a bounded initial level set, continuous differentiability and a Lipschitz gradient on a neighborhood of that set, descent directions, and Wolfe line searches. Its canonical target is \(\liminf_k\|g_k\|=0\), meaning that a subsequence approaches first-order stationarity. Full convergence \(\|g_k\|\to0\) is stronger and must be justified separately. The standard summability object is \(\sum_k\cos^2\theta_k\|g_k\|^2<\infty\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^1\) on a neighborhood of \(\mathcal L_0\), with Lipschitz-continuous gradient there.
\(g_k^Tp_k<0\), and \(\alpha_k\) satisfies the stated Wolfe conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime's canonical stationarity criterion is \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|\nabla f(x_k)\|=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\liminf_k\|g_k\|=0\) is equivalent to the existence of a subsequence \(k_j\to\infty\) with \(\|g_{k_j}\|\to0\).
special_cases_latex: If steepest-descent restarts occur with a uniformly bounded number of iterations between them, the cited analysis yields subsequential stationarity.
immediate_consequences_latex: The conclusion does not identify a global minimizer and does not exclude convergence to a saddle point or local maximizer solely from first-order information.
boundary_notes: Unmodified Polak–Ribière can fail in this regime even with an ideal line search.
Nonsmooth objectives and stochastic gradients require different stationarity notions.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: The objective oracle returns \((f(x),\nabla f(x))\) for \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). The method maintains an iteration state and invokes a line-search procedure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The interface is for deterministic smooth unconstrained optimization and formalizes the data exchanged among the recurrence, line search, termination rule, restart rule, and assessment layer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear-CG execution interface is a state-transition system with state \[S_k=(x_k,f_k,g_k,p_k,k),\] initialization \(g_0=\nabla f(x_0)\), \(p_0=-g_0\), and transition \[\alpha_k=\operatorname{LS}(x_k,f_k,g_k,p_k),\quad x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k,\] \[g_{k+1}=\nabla f(x_{k+1}),\quad p_{k+1}=\begin{cases}-g_{k+1},&\operatorname{Restart}(S_k,S_{k+1}),\\-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}p_k,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}\] Execution returns either a state satisfying \(\operatorname{Stop}(S_k)=\mathrm{true}\) or a declared failure when a prescribed resource limit or line-search failure condition is reached. The interface exposes iteration counts and objective/gradient evaluation counts for assessment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear-CG execution interface maintains \(S_k=(x_k,f_k,g_k,p_k,k)\), initializes \(p_0=-g_0\), asks a line search for \(\alpha_k\), updates \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), evaluates the new gradient, and chooses either the recurrence direction or the restarted direction \(-g_{k+1}\). It terminates when a declared stopping predicate holds or reports failure at a line-search or resource limit. Iteration and oracle-evaluation counts are exposed for numerical assessment.
assumptions_latex: The objective and gradient oracle is defined at every trial point accepted or evaluated by the line search.
The coefficient routine, line search, stopping predicate, restart predicate, and resource limits are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface maps \((f,x_0,\text{controls})\) to a terminal state and execution counters, or to a declared failure status.
special_cases_latex: With \(\operatorname{Restart}\equiv\mathrm{false}\) and the Fletcher–Reeves coefficient, the transition is Algorithm 5.4 in the cited source.
Setting \(\beta_{k+1}=0\) implements a restart without changing the interface.
immediate_consequences_latex: Only a fixed number of length-\(n\) vectors is required by the basic interface.
Different coefficient families can share the same line-search and stopping interfaces.
boundary_notes: The interface does not prescribe a programming language, floating-point format, or parallel execution model.
Constrained, stochastic, and derivative-free oracles require additional state and are outside this definition.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Vectors lie in \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and a nonlinear-CG iteration uses \(x_k\), \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(p_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition concerns the algebraic storage of the basic unpreconditioned nonlinear-CG recurrence, excluding storage internal to the objective oracle and line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear-CG implementation has a low-storage reuse architecture when the transition \[x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k,\qquad p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}p_k\] is performed using a number of length-\(n\) work vectors bounded independently of \(k\) and \(n\), with obsolete vectors overwritten once their last required scalar product has been formed. For FR, the live vector data may be represented by \((x_k,g_k,p_k,g_{k+1})\); PR and related formulas additionally require access to \(g_k\) while forming \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\). No matrix or history \((p_0,\ldots,p_{k-1})\) is stored. Thus the recurrence storage is \(O(n)\), and its vector arithmetic outside objective and gradient evaluation is \(O(n)\) per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear-CG implementation is low-storage when it executes the iterate and direction recurrences with only a fixed number of length-\(n\) vectors, overwriting old values after their final use. FR needs the current iterate, gradient, direction, and new gradient; PR-like formulas retain the old gradient long enough to form \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\). No matrix or growing direction history is stored. The recurrence therefore uses \(O(n)\) storage and \(O(n)\) vector work per iteration, excluding oracle and line-search costs.
assumptions_latex: The coefficient is computable from a fixed number of current or immediately preceding vectors and scalar products.
Objective-oracle and line-search internal storage are excluded from the recurrence-storage count.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recurrence requires \(O(n)\) storage with a constant independent of the iteration count.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Low storage means \(\sup_k m_k<\infty\), where \(m_k\) is the number of simultaneously live length-\(n\) recurrence vectors.
special_cases_latex: PR or PR+ requires one more retained gradient vector than a minimal FR realization.
A restart sets \(p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}\) and discards inherited direction information.
immediate_consequences_latex: The architecture is suitable for large problems for which dense \(n\times n\) matrix storage is infeasible.
boundary_notes: Preconditioners, checkpointing, automatic differentiation, and cached application data can increase total storage.
The definition is an asymptotic storage property, not a claim about memory bandwidth or wall-clock performance.

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient Retention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retention rule preventing redundant gradient evaluations in nonlinear CG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given retained \(g_k=
abla f(x_k)\) and direction \(d_k\), a line search may cache every evaluated pair \((f(x_k+\alpha d_k),
abla f(x_k+\alpha d_k))\). When it accepts \(\alpha_k\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\) and retain the already computed \(g_{k+1}=
abla f(x_{k+1})\). Compute \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\) and all scalar products required by \( eta_{k+1}\) before overwriting \(g_k\). Stop when the prescribed stationarity test holds; otherwise form the next direction without reevaluating \(
abla f(x_{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cache the gradient at the accepted trial point and form gradient differences before overwriting, avoiding a redundant gradient evaluation at the next iteration.
assumptions_latex: The line-search oracle returns a gradient at the accepted trial point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No additional evaluation of \(\nabla f(x_{k+1})\) is required after line-search acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Direction Vector Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: In-place reuse of the preceding nonlinear-CG direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After the accepted-step gradient \(g_{k+1}\) and recurrence scalar \(\beta_{k+1}\) are available, update the stored direction in place by \[d\leftarrow\beta_{k+1}d-g_{k+1}.\] The vector \(d\), formerly equal to \(d_k\), then equals \(d_{k+1}\). If a restart is required, use \(\beta_{k+1}=0\), so the same operation produces \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}\). The old direction may be overwritten only after all line-search and recurrence quantities depending on \(d_k\) have been computed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once dependent scalar products are computed, overwrite the old direction with the two-term update; setting the recurrence coefficient to zero implements restart.
assumptions_latex: All quantities requiring \(d_k\) are computed before overwriting it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One stored direction vector suffices for both continuation and restart.

children.title: Memory–Evaluation Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs between retained state and repeated derivative evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory–Evaluation Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exchange between cached trial data, storage, and repeated oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a line search evaluates \(m_k\) trial points during iteration \(k\). Retaining only accepted-point data requires \(O(n)\) persistent vector storage but may repeat an objective or gradient call if acceptance logic later needs discarded trial data. Caching all trial gradients requires \(O(m_kn)\) temporary storage and eliminates those repeated gradient calls. Caching only trial step lengths and objective values costs \(O(m_k)\) scalars but cannot reconstruct discarded gradients without reevaluation. Therefore storage and oracle counts must be reported separately; linear persistent storage alone does not determine evaluation complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Caching more trial-point information can prevent repeated oracle calls, while strict linear-memory implementations may reevaluate discarded trial points; storage and evaluations are distinct costs.
assumptions_latex: Each gradient is a vector in \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Full trial-gradient caching costs \(O(m_kn)\) temporary memory, whereas accepted-point retention costs \(O(n)\).

notation.meaning: number of line-search trial points at iteration k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonlinear-CG Termination and Restart Decision System
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iteration \(k\), the available state includes \(x_k\), \(f_k=f(x_k)\), \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(p_k\), iteration count, and evaluation counts.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The system combines an approximate-stationarity stopping test, resource-limit failure, and steepest-descent restart predicates for smooth unconstrained nonlinear CG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A termination–restart decision system is a pair of predicates \((T_k,R_{k+1})\). A canonical termination predicate is \[T_k:\quad \|g_k\|_\infty\le \varepsilon_g(1+|f_k|),\] augmented by a maximum iteration or evaluation count that declares failure rather than convergence. A canonical restart predicate is \[R_k:\quad \frac{|g_k^Tg_{k-1}|}{\|g_k\|^2}\ge\nu,\qquad 0<\nu<1,\] with restart action \(\beta_k:=0\) and \(p_k:=-g_k\). Periodic restart is the alternative predicate \(k\equiv0\pmod m\), and PR+ supplies an implicit restart whenever \(\beta_k^{\mathrm{PR}}<0\). Termination is evaluated before forming a coefficient whose denominator contains \(\|g_k\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A termination–restart system consists of a stopping predicate and a restart predicate. A canonical stopping rule is \(\|g_k\|_\infty\le\varepsilon_g(1+|f_k|)\), with iteration or evaluation caps reported as failures. A canonical restart checks whether consecutive gradients are far from orthogonal: \(|g_k^Tg_{k-1}|/\|g_k\|^2\ge\nu\). Restarting sets \(\beta_k=0\) and \(p_k=-g_k\). Periodic restarts and the negative-coefficient truncation in PR+ are alternative mechanisms.
assumptions_latex: The gradient norm and inner products are finite.
A resource cap, if used, is distinguished from successful termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(T_k\) holds, execution returns \(x_k\); if \(R_k\) holds and \(T_k\) does not, the next search direction is \(-g_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The restart action \(p_k=-g_k\) is equivalent within the nonlinear-CG recurrence to setting \(\beta_k=0\).
special_cases_latex: The cited numerical tests use \(\varepsilon_g=10^{-5}\) and a cap of \(10{,}000\) iterations.
A typical cited orthogonality threshold is \(\nu=0.1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A restart erases accumulated conjugate-direction information while preserving the current iterate.
Testing stationarity first avoids division by zero in gradient-normalized coefficients and restart ratios.
boundary_notes: Meeting a positive gradient tolerance certifies approximate, not exact, stationarity.
Stagnation, NaN detection, and noisy-gradient tests require additional predicates not fixed here.

children.title: Stationarity Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators used to assess whether nonlinear-CG execution should terminate near stationarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled first-order stopping test for unconstrained nonlinear CG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For tolerances \(\varepsilon_g\ge0\) and scale floor \(s_g>0\), declare approximate first-order stationarity at iterate \(x_k\) when \[\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_\infty\le \varepsilon_g\max\{s_g,|f(x_k)|,\|x_k\|_\infty\}.\] For an unscaled absolute test, use \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2\le\varepsilon_g\). Either predicate certifies only approximate first-order stationarity; it does not by itself certify local minimality or global optimality for a nonconvex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Terminate for stationarity when a chosen gradient norm falls below an explicit absolute or scale-aware tolerance; this alone does not certify optimality in nonconvex problems.
assumptions_latex: The norm, scaling convention, and tolerance are fixed before the run.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality declares \(x_k\) approximately first-order stationary.

children.title: Progress-Stall Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators of insufficient objective, gradient, or step progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Progress-Stall Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed tests for negligible objective and iterate progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a window length \(w\ge1\), relative tolerances \(\varepsilon_f,\varepsilon_x\ge0\), and positive floors \(s_f,s_x\). Declare a progress stall at iteration \(k\ge w\) if both \[|f(x_k)-f(x_{k-w})|\le\varepsilon_f\max\{s_f,|f(x_{k-w})|\}\] and \[\|x_k-x_{k-w}\|_2\le\varepsilon_x\max\{s_x,\|x_{k-w}\|_2\}.\] A stall is a computational diagnostic, not a stationarity certificate: if the gradient test fails, the appropriate response may be restart, rescaling, or line-search repair rather than successful termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A windowed stall occurs when both objective and iterate changes are negligible, but it is not successful convergence unless a stationarity test also passes.
assumptions_latex: The tolerances and positive scale floors are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conjunction of the two displayed inequalities flags insufficient numerical progress.

children.title: Restart Trigger Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators supporting reinitialization of the nonlinear-CG direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Trigger Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable loss-of-descent and loss-of-orthogonality restart predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), a proposed direction \(d_k\), the previous gradient \(g_{k-1}\), and thresholds \(\eta_d>0\), \(\eta_o\in[0,1)\), trigger a restart if \[g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k>-\eta_d\|g_k\|_2\|d_k\|_2\quad\text{or}\quad |g_k^{\mathsf T}g_{k-1}|>\eta_o\|g_k\|_2^2.\] A restart replaces the proposed direction by \(d_k=-g_k\), equivalently setting the nonlinear-CG recurrence coefficient to zero. The first predicate protects descent; the second detects excessive residual-gradient correlation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart when the proposed direction is insufficiently descending or successive gradients are excessively correlated, then replace the direction by steepest descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If either predicate holds, set \(d_k=-g_k\).

children.title: Termination-versus-Restart Decisions
children.top_down_role: Interface-level distinction between ending execution and continuing from a restarted direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Termination-versus-Restart Decisions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Priority rule separating successful termination from recoverable recurrence failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), evaluate the stationarity predicate \(T_k\), the progress-stall predicate \(P_k\), and the restart predicate \(R_k\). If \(T_k\) holds, terminate successfully and return \(x_k\). Otherwise, if \(R_k\) holds, set \(d_k=-g_k\) and continue. If \(P_k\) holds but \(R_k\) does not, attempt a bounded recovery such as restart or line-search reset; terminate with a stall status only after the prescribed recovery budget is exhausted. Thus neither loss of conjugacy nor small objective change is reported as successful convergence without stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Give stationarity highest priority; otherwise restart on recurrence failure, and report a stall only after bounded recovery fails.
assumptions_latex: The predicates \(T_k\), \(P_k\), and \(R_k\) are defined with fixed tolerances.
A finite recovery budget is prescribed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful termination occurs only when \(T_k\) holds; restart and stall have distinct statuses.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Performance Assessment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reproducible evaluation protocol for nonlinear-CG implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed test set \(\mathcal P\), starting points, tolerances, resource limits, and computing environment, assess each solver using at least: success count under the same stationarity predicate; objective evaluations \(N_f(p)\); gradient evaluations \(N_g(p)\); iterations \(N_i(p)\); elapsed time \(T(p)\); and terminal status for every \(p\in\mathcal P\). Comparisons must treat failures and resource-limit exits explicitly and must not replace separate oracle counts by iterations, because line searches can perform multiple evaluations per iteration. Report accuracy at termination alongside cost so that inexpensive inaccurate runs are not ranked as successes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare nonlinear-CG solvers on identical problems and stopping rules, reporting success, separate oracle counts, iterations, time, terminal status, and achieved accuracy.
assumptions_latex: All solvers use identical test instances, starts, tolerances, and resource limits.
Success is defined by one common stationarity predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Performance comparisons separate reliability, achieved accuracy, oracle work, iterations, and elapsed time.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Numerical Performance Assessment for Nonlinear CG
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite test set and \(\mathcal A\) a finite collection of nonlinear-CG solvers run under common stopping and resource rules.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition covers deterministic comparative assessment through success status, iterations, and function/gradient evaluations. It does not substitute empirical results for convergence guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A numerical performance assessment assigns to every solver–problem pair \((a,p)\in\mathcal A\times\mathcal P\) a record \[M(a,p)=(s_{a,p},k_{a,p},N^f_{a,p},N^g_{a,p},m_{a,p}),\] where \(s_{a,p}\in\{\mathrm{success},\mathrm{failure}\}\), \(k_{a,p}\) is the iteration count, \(N^f_{a,p}\) and \(N^g_{a,p}\) are objective and gradient evaluation counts, and \(m_{a,p}\) counts specified safeguards or coefficient modifications. Success must use one common termination rule, such as \(\|g_k\|_\infty<\varepsilon_g(1+|f_k|)\), and failure must use a common resource cap. Comparisons are valid only for identical problem instances, initial points, line-search tolerances, and success criteria.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear-CG performance assessment records, for every solver and test problem, success or failure, iterations, objective evaluations, gradient evaluations, and any declared safeguard count. All solvers use the same stopping test and resource cap, as well as identical instances, starting points, and comparable line-search settings. The resulting measurements describe empirical efficiency and robustness; they do not establish a convergence theorem.
assumptions_latex: Every run uses a declared common success criterion and resource limit.
Evaluation-count conventions are identical across solvers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each run produces a comparable metric tuple \(M(a,p)\) or is marked missing if the protocol was not executed.
special_cases_latex: The cited comparison reports combined function/gradient evaluations and counts PR+ modifications.
A run not satisfying the stopping test within \(10{,}000\) iterations is marked as a failure in the cited experiment.
immediate_consequences_latex: Success rate measures robustness under the protocol, while evaluation counts measure oracle work conditional on the counting convention.
Iteration counts alone need not reflect line-search cost.
boundary_notes: Results on a finite test set do not imply dominance on all objectives.
Wall-clock comparisons additionally require controlled hardware, software, and timing methodology.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: This chapter-native boundary covers geometric direction failures and failure of the assumptions supporting Wolfe-based descent globalization. Noisy, stochastic, nonsmooth, and constrained cases are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The descent-globalization failure boundary is the set of iteration states at which at least one required globalization condition is absent: \[\mathcal B=\mathcal B_{\mathrm{desc}}\cup\mathcal B_{\mathrm{angle}}\cup\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}},\] where \[\mathcal B_{\mathrm{desc}}=\{k:g_k^Tp_k\ge0,\ g_k\ne0\},\] \[\mathcal B_{\mathrm{angle}}=\left\{\{k_j\}:k_j\to\infty,\ \cos\theta_{k_j}\to0\right\},\] and \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{reg}}\) denotes failure of the smoothness, lower-boundedness, or level-set Lipschitz-gradient assumptions used to guarantee acceptable steps and Zoutendijk summability. Membership marks the boundary of the standard guarantee; it is not by itself a statement that every numerical run must diverge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The descent-globalization failure boundary contains nonstationary states with \(g_k^Tp_k\ge0\), subsequences whose directions become orthogonal to steepest descent so that \(\cos\theta_{k_j}\to0\), and problems violating the smoothness, lower-bound, or Lipschitz-gradient assumptions underlying Wolfe-step existence and Zoutendijk analysis. Crossing this boundary removes the standard guarantee but does not logically force every run to fail.
assumptions_latex: The geometric components are evaluated only when \(g_k\ne0\) and \(p_k\ne0\).
The reference globalization framework is a smooth unconstrained line-search method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B\) identifies states or problem regimes not covered by the standard descent-and-Wolfe globalization guarantee.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For nonzero \(g_k,p_k\), \(g_k^Tp_k<0\) is equivalent to \(\cos\theta_k>0\).
special_cases_latex: Pure Newton directions with indefinite Hessians may lie in \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{desc}}\).
Nonlinear-CG recurrences can enter \(\mathcal B_{\mathrm{desc}}\) when an inexact line search fails to preserve descent.
immediate_consequences_latex: A line search predicated on \(\phi_k'(0)=g_k^Tp_k<0\) loses its standard basis when \(k\in\mathcal B_{\mathrm{desc}}\).
boundary_notes: The set is a failure-of-guarantee boundary, not a divergence theorem.
Finite-precision interpolation and evaluation failures are implementation phenomena requiring additional numerical models.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition separates sign, angle, and magnitude defects for smooth unconstrained line-search directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given quality constants \(\eta>0\), \(\delta>0\), and \(0<m\le M<\infty\), a search direction has acceptable quality when \[q_k\ge\eta,\qquad c_k\ge\delta,\qquad m\le s_k\le M.\] A direction-quality failure occurs when at least one condition fails. The three components are loss of sufficient descent \(q_k<\eta\), near orthogonality \(c_k<\delta\), and poor magnitude scaling \(s_k\notin[m,M]\). The limiting global failure occurs when no fixed positive \(\eta,\delta,m\) and finite \(M\) control the relevant generated sequence. The identity \(q_k=c_ks_k\) couples the angle and scale measures but does not make their failure modes identical.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nonzero gradient and direction, define sufficient-descent quality \(q_k=-g_k^Tp_k/\|g_k\|^2\), angular quality \(c_k=-g_k^Tp_k/(\|g_k\|\|p_k\|)\), and relative magnitude \(s_k=\|p_k\|/\|g_k\|\). Acceptable directions have uniform positive lower bounds on \(q_k\) and \(c_k\), and upper and lower bounds on \(s_k\). Failure means loss of sufficient descent, near orthogonality, or poor scaling. Although \(q_k=c_ks_k\), the three defects remain mathematically distinct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Direction-quality failure is the complement of \(\{q_k\ge\eta,\ c_k\ge\delta,\ m\le s_k\le M\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(q_k=c_ks_k\).
Strict descent is the weaker condition \(q_k>0\), equivalently \(c_k>0\).
special_cases_latex: Steepest descent has \(q_k=c_k=s_k=1\).
A direction can be descent but have poor angular quality when \(0<c_k\ll1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The direction \(p_k\) is a strict descent direction at \(x_k\) when \[g_k^Tp_k<0.\] Loss of descent occurs when \[g_k^Tp_k\ge0.\] The case \(g_k^Tp_k=0\) is first-order neutral, while \(g_k^Tp_k>0\) is an ascent direction. Equivalently, with \(\phi_k(\alpha)=f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\), loss of descent is \(\phi_k'(0)\ge0\). It marks failure of the standard premise used by positive-step Armijo and Wolfe line searches; it does not assert that \(f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\ge f(x_k)\) for every \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a nonstationary point, \(p_k\) is a strict descent direction exactly when \(g_k^Tp_k<0\). Loss of descent means \(g_k^Tp_k\ge0\): equality is first-order neutrality and strict positivity is ascent. Equivalently, the directional line function \(\phi_k(\alpha)=f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\) satisfies \(\phi_k'(0)\ge0\). This removes the standard premise for positive-step Armijo and Wolfe searches but does not prove that every positive step increases the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Loss of descent is precisely \(g_k^Tp_k\ge0\), equivalently \(\phi_k'(0)\ge0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(\theta_k\) the angle between \(p_k\) and \(-g_k\), loss of descent is \(\cos\theta_k\le0\).
special_cases_latex: The steepest-descent direction \(p_k=-g_k\) never loses descent when \(g_k\ne0\).
An unmodified Newton direction can lose descent when the Hessian is not positive definite.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(g_k^Tp_k<0\), differentiability implies that sufficiently small positive steps decrease \(f\); this standard local conclusion is unavailable after loss of descent.
boundary_notes: At a stationary point \(g_k=0\), every directional derivative is zero; this is termination, not a direction-quality failure.
Nonsmooth descent uses directional derivatives or subgradients and is outside this definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Orthogonal Search Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing angle-quality boundary for smooth descent directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) have an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, and let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\ne0\) and \(g_k^\top p_k<0\). Define \(\cos\theta_k=-g_k^\top p_k/(\lVert g_k\rVert\lVert p_k\rVert)\). For Armijo parameter \(c_1\in(0,1)\), every \(\alpha\) satisfying \[0<\alpha\le \frac{2(1-c_1)(-g_k^\top p_k)}{L\lVert p_k\rVert^2}\] is guaranteed to satisfy sufficient decrease. If \(\cos\theta_k\to0\) while \(\lVert g_k\rVert/\lVert p_k\rVert\) remains bounded, this guaranteed step-size threshold tends to zero, so no uniform positive acceptance bound follows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As descent directions become orthogonal to the negative gradient, the smoothness-based step-size guarantee can collapse to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on every relevant trial segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\cos\theta_k\to0\) with bounded \(\lVert g_k\rVert/\lVert p_k\rVert\) forces the displayed guaranteed Armijo threshold to converge to \(0\).

notation.meaning: angle between the search direction and negative gradient

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition measures angular quality independently of direction magnitude. It applies to smooth unconstrained line-search methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a tolerance \(0<\delta<1\), a descent direction \(p_k\) is near-orthogonal to the steepest-descent direction \(-g_k\) when \[0<\cos\theta_k\le\delta.\] A sequence is asymptotically near-orthogonal when there exists a subsequence \(k_j\to\infty\) such that \(\cos\theta_{k_j}\to0^+\). This is a direction-quality failure because the first-order decrease per unit direction norm, \[-\frac{g_k^Tp_k}{\|p_k\|}=\|g_k\|\cos\theta_k,\] becomes small relative to \(\|g_k\|\). Under Zoutendijk summability, persistent nonvanishing gradients can be compatible only with sufficiently poor angular behavior; uniform \(\cos\theta_k\ge\delta>0\) rules out that escape route.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a chosen \(0<\delta<1\), a descent direction is near-orthogonal to \(-g_k\) when its angle cosine satisfies \(0<\cos\theta_k\le\delta\). A sequence is asymptotically near-orthogonal if some subsequence has \(\cos\theta_{k_j}\to0\). The normalized first-order decrease is then \(\|g_k\|\cos\theta_k\), so angular progress becomes small. This differs from loss of descent because the cosine remains positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Near orthogonality is \(0< -g_k^Tp_k/(\|g_k\|\|p_k\|)\le\delta\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The acute angle between \(p_k\) and \(-g_k\) lies in \([\arccos\delta,\pi/2)\).
Asymptotic near orthogonality is \(-g_{k_j}^Tp_{k_j}=o(\|g_{k_j}\|\|p_{k_j}\|)\).
special_cases_latex: Steepest descent has \(\cos\theta_k=1\) and is never near-orthogonal for \(\delta<1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Near orthogonality can produce tiny productive steps even though strict descent is retained.
Angle tests that enforce \(\cos\theta_k\ge\delta\) exclude this failure but may interfere with useful ill-conditioned directions.
boundary_notes: The numerical value of \(\delta\) is problem- and method-dependent.
Orthogonality to \(-g_k\) is not the same as conjugacy with respect to a Hessian or preconditioner.

knowledge_statements.title: Poorly Scaled Search Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo step-length degradation caused solely by rescaling a fixed descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) have an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, let \(q\) satisfy \(\nabla f(x)^\top q<0\), and set \(p_\tau=\tau q\) for \(\tau>0\). The direction angle is unchanged, but the standard guaranteed Armijo threshold becomes \[\bar\alpha_\tau=\frac{2(1-c_1)(-\nabla f(x)^\top q)}{L\tau\lVert q\rVert^2}.\] Thus \(\bar\alpha_\tau\to0\) as \(\tau\to\infty\). Conversely, if trial parameters remain bounded and \(\tau\to0\), then \(\lVert\alpha p_\tau\rVert\to0\). Direction scaling can therefore cause arbitrarily many reductions or arbitrarily small physical displacement without changing the descent ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rescaling a descent direction preserves its ray but can force the safe line-search parameter or the actual displacement toward zero.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on the trial segment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Large \(\tau\) makes the guaranteed parameter \(O(\tau^{-1})\), while small \(\tau\) makes bounded-parameter displacements vanish.

notation.meaning: fixed descent direction defining the search ray

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(g_k=
abla f(x_k)
e0\) and \(p_k
e0\). Define the relative magnitude \(s_k=\|p_k\|/\|g_k\|\) and angular quality \(c_k=-g_k^Tp_k/(\|g_k\|\|p_k\|)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition concerns scaling of a generated direction relative to the gradient in a fixed norm. It is distinct from poor scaling of the variables or objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given constants \(0<m\le M<\infty\), a search direction is well scaled relative to the gradient when \[m\le\frac{\|p_k\|}{\|g_k\|}\le M.\] It is poorly scaled when \[\frac{\|p_k\|}{\|g_k\|}<m\quad\text{or}\quad\frac{\|p_k\|}{\|g_k\|}>M.\] For a sequence, scaling degenerates if \(s_{k_j}\to0\) or \(s_{k_j}\to\infty\) along a subsequence. Because \[-\frac{g_k^Tp_k}{\|g_k\|^2}=c_ks_k,\] magnitude scaling and angular quality jointly determine normalized descent. In the Fletcher–Reeves analysis, \(c_k\) is comparable to \(\|g_k\|/\|p_k\|=s_k^{-1}\); hence a very large direction relative to the gradient is associated with a nearly orthogonal poor direction under those hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direction is well scaled relative to the gradient when \(m\le\|p_k\|/\|g_k\|\le M\) for fixed positive finite bounds. It is poorly scaled if the ratio is too small or too large, and a sequence degenerates when the ratio tends to zero or infinity along a subsequence. Since normalized descent equals angular quality times relative magnitude, scale and angle interact but are not identical. Under the cited Fletcher–Reeves bounds, an excessively large direction relative to the gradient accompanies a nearly orthogonal direction.
assumptions_latex: The norm and thresholds \(0<m\le M<\infty\) are fixed before classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Poor relative scaling is \(\|p_k\|/\|g_k\|\notin[m,M]\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The upper-scale failure is \(\|g_k\|/\|p_k\|<1/M\); the lower-scale failure is \(\|g_k\|/\|p_k\|>1/m\).
special_cases_latex: Steepest descent \(p_k=-g_k\) has \(s_k=1\).
Multiplying a direction by a positive scalar changes \(s_k\) but not its angle, demonstrating that scaling and near orthogonality are distinct.
immediate_consequences_latex: A line-search step \(\alpha_kp_k\) may remain moderate despite poor direction scaling only if the accepted \(\alpha_k\) compensates for it.
boundary_notes: The thresholds depend on the chosen norm and coordinate system.
Problem ill-conditioning can cause poor directions but is not itself the definition of a poorly scaled direction.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), let \(x_k,p_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfy \(\nabla f(x_k)^Tp_k<0\), and define \(\phi_k(\alpha)=f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\). Let \(\widehat\phi_k\), \(\widehat\phi_k'\), and \(\widehat x(\alpha)\) denote their finite-precision evaluations. Let \(\mathcal A_k\subset(0,\alpha_{\max}]\) be the set of exact step lengths satisfying the prescribed acceptance conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is an operational definition for deterministic smooth line searches in finite-precision arithmetic. It separates numerical termination from nonexistence of an acceptable exact step and does not classify failures caused by a non-descent direction or an unbounded objective along the search ray.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A line-search numerical failure occurs at iteration \(k\) if \(\mathcal A_k\neq\varnothing\), but the finite-precision line-search procedure terminates without returning an accepted \(\widehat\alpha_k>0\) because at least one numerical stopping event occurs: \[\widehat x(\alpha_j)=x_k,\qquad \widehat\phi_k(\alpha_j)=\widehat\phi_k(0),\qquad \frac{\|\widehat x(\alpha_j)-x_k\|}{\max\{1,\|x_k\|\}}\leq\tau_x,\qquad\text{or}\qquad j=N_{\max},\] where the last event is accompanied by failure to distinguish an acceptable reduction during the allowed trials. Equivalently, with \(\mathsf{Accept}_k(\alpha)\) denoting the exact predicate and \(\widehat{\mathsf{Accept}}_k(\alpha)\) its computed test, failure means \[\exists\alpha\in(0,\alpha_{\max}]:\mathsf{Accept}_k(\alpha)=1,\qquad \widehat{\mathsf{Accept}}_k(\alpha_j)=0\ \text{for every tested }j,\] followed by a finite-precision stagnation or trial-limit exit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An iteration has a line-search numerical failure when an acceptable positive step exists in exact arithmetic, yet the implemented search returns no step because the computed trial point no longer differs from the current point, computed function values are indistinguishable, the relative change in the iterate is below \(\tau_x\), or the trial limit \(N_{\max}\) is reached without resolving acceptance. Thus the defining feature is disagreement between existence under the exact acceptance predicate and termination under its finite-precision evaluation.
assumptions_latex: \(p_k\) is an exact descent direction: \(\nabla f(x_k)^Tp_k<0\).
The exact acceptance set is nonempty: \(\mathcal A_k\neq\varnothing\).
The implementation uses finite tolerances \(\tau_x>0\) and \(N_{\max}\in\mathbb N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The failure event is \(\mathsf{NF}_k=\{\mathcal A_k\neq\varnothing\}\cap\{\text{no computed trial is returned before a numerical stopping event}\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The event may be expressed as a false-negative termination of the computed acceptance predicate: \(\mathcal A_k\neq\varnothing\) while \(\widehat{\mathcal A}_k\cap\{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_J\}=\varnothing\).
special_cases_latex: For an Armijo search, \(\mathsf{Accept}_k(\alpha)\) is \(\phi_k(\alpha)\leq\phi_k(0)+c_1\alpha\phi_k'(0)\).
For a strong-Wolfe search, the exact predicate additionally requires \(|\phi_k'(\alpha)|\leq c_2|\phi_k'(0)|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A failure with \(\mathcal A_k=\varnothing\) is excluded: it is a mathematical or modeling failure, not a numerical line-search failure under this definition.
Equality \(\widehat x(\alpha_j)=x_k\) implies that further reduction of a representable positive \(\alpha_j\) cannot produce a distinct trial point in the same arithmetic and direction.
boundary_notes: The thresholds and trial budget are implementation parameters; the cited source describes these stopping mechanisms but does not assign a universal tolerance.
NaN, overflow, domain violations, and failures of an external function evaluator require additional predicates and are not included here.

knowledge_statements.title: Excessive Backtracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-count boundary furnished by a guaranteed acceptance region for geometric Armijo backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\alpha_0>0\) and \(\rho\in(0,1)\), and test \(\alpha_j=\rho^j\alpha_0\) until Armijo acceptance. Suppose every trial with \(0<\alpha\le\bar\alpha\) is guaranteed acceptable, where \(0<\bar\alpha<\alpha_0\). The first trial certainly lying in this region has index \[J=\left\lceil\frac{\log(\alpha_0/\bar\alpha)}{\log(1/\rho)}\right\rceil.\] Thus acceptance occurs no later than trial \(J\), although it may occur earlier. As \(\bar\alpha\downarrow0\), this guarantee requires an unbounded number of reductions, so no uniform finite function-evaluation bound can be derived from the guaranteed region unless \(\bar\alpha\) has a uniform positive lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric backtracking reaches its guaranteed safe region after logarithmically many reductions, and this guarantee provides no uniform evaluation bound when the safe threshold can vanish.
assumptions_latex: Every trial in \((0,\bar\alpha]\) is acceptable, with \(0<\bar\alpha<\alpha_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance is guaranteed by index \(J\), but the bound \(J\) is not uniform when \(\inf\bar\alpha=0\).

notation.meaning: threshold below which acceptance is guaranteed
first index guaranteed to enter the acceptance region

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi_k(\alpha)=f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\), where \(p_k\) is a descent direction. Fix \(\bar\alpha_k>0\), \(c_1\in(0,1)\), and contraction factors \(\rho_{k,j}\in[\rho_{\min},\rho_{\max}]\subset(0,1)\). Define \(\alpha_{k,0}=\bar\alpha_k\) and \(\alpha_{k,j+1}=\rho_{k,j}\alpha_{k,j}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition concerns Armijo backtracking for a single outer iteration. Because “excessive” has no scale-free universal cutoff, it is defined relative to an explicit evaluation budget \(B_k\) or minimum useful step \(\alpha_{\min,k}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the backtracking count by \[J_k=\inf\left\{j\in\mathbb N_0:\phi_k(\alpha_{k,j})\leq\phi_k(0)+c_1\alpha_{k,j}\phi_k'(0)\right\},\] with \(J_k=+\infty\) when the set is empty. Backtracking is excessive relative to \((B_k,\alpha_{\min,k})\) if \[J_k>B_k\quad\text{or}\quad \alpha_{k,J_k}<\alpha_{\min,k}.\] If a fixed contraction \(\rho\in(0,1)\) is used, then \(\alpha_{k,j}=\rho^j\bar\alpha_k\), and the second condition is equivalent to \[J_k>\frac{\log(\alpha_{\min,k}/\bar\alpha_k)}{\log\rho}.\] The definition therefore records either too many rejected trials or acceptance only after the step has fallen below the declared useful scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Excessive backtracking is backtracking that exceeds a stated resource or step-size threshold. Starting from \(\bar\alpha_k\), let \(J_k\) be the first trial index satisfying Armijo sufficient decrease. The event occurs when \(J_k>B_k\), or when the accepted step \(\alpha_{k,J_k}\) is smaller than \(\alpha_{\min,k}\). With a constant contraction \(\rho\), this is equivalent to a logarithmic threshold on \(J_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(B_k\in\mathbb N_0\) and \(0<\alpha_{\min,k}\leq\bar\alpha_k\) are declared before classifying the iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The excessive-backtracking event is \(\mathsf{EB}_k=\{J_k>B_k\}\cup\{J_k<\infty,\ \alpha_{k,J_k}<\alpha_{\min,k}\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: When cost is measured by function evaluations and each rejected trial costs one evaluation, \(J_k>B_k\) is equivalent to exceeding the rejection-evaluation budget.
For constant \(\rho\), \(J_k>B_k\) implies \(\alpha_{k,J_k}<\rho^{B_k}\bar\alpha_k\).
special_cases_latex: Taking \(\alpha_{\min,k}=0\) leaves the pure budget criterion \(J_k>B_k\).
Taking \(B_k=+\infty\) leaves the useful-step criterion \(\alpha_{k,J_k}<\alpha_{\min,k}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A large initial scaling can increase \(J_k\) even when the Armijo condition is eventually satisfied.
Finite termination of ordinary backtracking does not preclude excessive backtracking relative to a finite budget.
boundary_notes: No universal value of \(B_k\) is canonical; it depends on evaluation cost and the implementation contract.
This definition does not declare every small accepted step erroneous, since a genuinely narrow region of sufficient decrease may require one.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a line search maintain a nondegenerate interval \(I_j=[a_j,b_j]\subset(0,\alpha_{\max}]\), with width \(w_j=b_j-a_j>0\). An interpolation or extrapolation rule proposes \(\widetilde\alpha_j=P(D_j)\), where \(D_j\) contains sampled values of the line function \(\phi\) and possibly \(\phi'\). Fix an interior safeguard fraction \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition covers instability of quadratic, cubic, or extrapolative trial generators. It concerns the numerical proposal mechanism, not whether the objective itself is nonconvex or whether an accepted step ultimately exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The proposal at trial \(j\) is stable relative to \((I_j,\eta)\) when it is finite and lies in the safeguarded interior, \[\widetilde\alpha_j\in S_\eta(I_j):=[a_j+\eta w_j,\ b_j-\eta w_j].\] A trial-proposal instability occurs when \[\widetilde\alpha_j
otin S_\eta(I_j)\quad	ext{or}\quad \widetilde\alpha_j
otin\mathbb R,\] so that the raw proposal is outside the bracket, too close to an endpoint, or nonfinite and must be replaced by a safeguarded value. A sequence belongs to the persistent instability family if for some \(m\geq1\), \[\widetilde\alpha_{j+r}
otin S_\eta(I_{j+r})\quad	ext{for every }r=0,\ldots,m-1.\] Equivalently, its normalized endpoint distance \(\delta_j=\min\{\widetilde\alpha_j-a_j,b_j-\widetilde\alpha_j\}/w_j\) fails \(\delta_j\geq\eta\), with any proposal outside \(I_j\) assigned \(\delta_j<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trial proposal is unstable when the raw interpolated or extrapolated step is nonfinite, lies outside the current admissible interval, or lies closer than the fraction \(\eta\) of the interval width to an endpoint. Persistent proposal instability means this occurs on \(m\) consecutive trials, forcing the line search to use a safeguarded substitute each time. The normalized endpoint-distance test \(\delta_j\geq\eta\) gives an equivalent classification.
assumptions_latex: The proposal rule \(P\) is evaluated from finite-precision sampled data \(D_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The instability event is \(\mathsf{PI}_j=\{P(D_j)\notin S_\eta(I_j)\}\cup\{P(D_j)\notin\mathbb R\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a finite proposal inside \(I_j\), instability is equivalent to \(\delta_j<\eta\).
A midpoint fallback replaces an unstable proposal by \((a_j+b_j)/2\in S_\eta(I_j)\) for every \(\eta\leq1/2\).
special_cases_latex: In decreasing Armijo interpolation, instability includes a proposed \(\alpha_{j+1}\) that is too close to \(\alpha_j\) or is excessively smaller than \(\alpha_j\).
In zoom, instability includes a quadratic or cubic proposal too close to either bracket endpoint.
immediate_consequences_latex: Safeguarding an unstable proposal guarantees an interior trial but does not establish the Wolfe or Armijo conditions.
Repeated fallback indicates failure of the proposal model to provide usable localization information at the current arithmetic scale.
boundary_notes: The choice of \(\eta\) is implementation-dependent.
A proposal near an endpoint is classified by the safeguard contract even if it would accidentally satisfy the acceptance conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Interpolation Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ill-conditioning boundary for a quadratic line-search proposal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:[0,a]\to\mathbb{R}\) be sampled through \(\phi(0)\), \(\phi'(0)<0\), and \(\phi(a)\), where \(a>0\). The minimizer of the quadratic interpolant matching these data is \[\alpha_q=-\frac{\phi'(0)a^2}{2D},\qquad D=\phi(a)-\phi(0)-a\phi'(0),\] when \(D>0\). For perturbations with fixed numerator, \(\lvert\delta\alpha_q\rvert/\lvert\alpha_q\rvert\) is first-order proportional to \(\lvert\delta D\rvert/\lvert D\rvert\). Hence cancellation making \(D\) comparable to data error renders the proposal unreliable; if \(D\le0\), the interpolant has no finite positive minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic interpolation becomes ill-conditioned when its curvature denominator nearly cancels, and it loses a finite positive minimizer when that denominator is nonpositive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Small \(\lvert D\rvert\) causes large relative proposal sensitivity, while \(D\le0\) invalidates the finite positive minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Extrapolation Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ill-conditioning boundary for derivative-secant extrapolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0\le a<b\), set \(A=\phi'(b)\), \(B=\phi'(a)\), and suppose a line search extrapolates to the zero of the affine interpolant of \(\phi'\): \[\alpha_s=b-A\frac{b-a}{A-B}.\] The proposal is uniquely defined only when \(A\ne B\). With respect to perturbations of \((A,B)\), its Euclidean absolute condition number is \[\left\lVert\nabla_{(A,B)}\alpha_s\right\rVert=\frac{(b-a)\sqrt{A^2+B^2}}{|A-B|^2}.\] Hence derivative samples that approach one another while \(\sqrt{A^2+B^2}\) does not vanish comparably make the proposal ill-conditioned. If additionally \(|A|/|A-B|\to\infty\), then \(|\alpha_s-b|\to\infty\). When \(A=B\), the affine derivative model determines no unique finite secant zero, so a bounded extrapolation safeguard or fallback is required for uniformly bounded proposals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative-secant extrapolation becomes ill-conditioned when the sampled derivatives nearly coincide; if the numerator does not vanish comparably, the proposal can move arbitrarily far from the sampled interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: As \(|A-B|\to0\), the proposal loses uniform conditioning unless the derivative data vanish sufficiently rapidly; if \(|A|/|A-B|\to\infty\), the extrapolation distance is unbounded.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ill-conditioning boundary for derivative-secant extrapolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0\le a<b\), set \(A=\phi'(b)\), \(B=\phi'(a)\), and suppose a line search extrapolates to the zero of the affine interpolant of \(\phi'\): \[\alpha_s=b-A\frac{b-a}{A-B}.\] The proposal is uniquely defined only when \(A\ne B\). With respect to perturbations of \((A,B)\), its Euclidean absolute condition number is \[\left\lVert\nabla_{(A,B)}\alpha_s\right\rVert=\frac{(b-a)\sqrt{A^2+B^2}}{|A-B|^2}.\] Hence derivative samples that approach one another while \(\sqrt{A^2+B^2}\) does not vanish comparably make the proposal ill-conditioned. If additionally \(|A|/|A-B|\to\infty\), then \(|\alpha_s-b|\to\infty\). When \(A=B\), the affine derivative model determines no unique finite secant zero, so a bounded extrapolation safeguard or fallback is required for uniformly bounded proposals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative-secant extrapolation becomes ill-conditioned when the sampled derivatives nearly coincide; if the numerator does not vanish comparably, the proposal can move arbitrarily far from the sampled interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: As \(|A-B|\to0\), the proposal loses uniform conditioning unless the derivative data vanish sufficiently rapidly; if \(|A|/|A-B|\to\infty\), the extrapolation distance is unbounded.

children.title: Trial-Proposal Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of proposed steps to evaluation noise, curvature estimates, or sample placement.

knowledge_statements.title: Trial-Proposal Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local conditioning boundary for implicitly defined trial proposals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let line-search data be represented by \(z\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and let a proposal \(\alpha(z)\) be locally defined by \(Q(\alpha,z)=0\), where \(Q\) is continuously differentiable and \(Q_\alpha(\alpha,z)\ne0\). The implicit-function derivative is \[D\alpha(z)=-\frac{Q_z(\alpha,z)}{Q_\alpha(\alpha,z)}.\] Thus a local absolute condition number is \(\kappa=\lVert Q_z\rVert/\lvert Q_\alpha\rvert\). Along any data sequence for which \(\lVert Q_z\rVert\) stays bounded away from zero while \(Q_\alpha\to0\), the proposal condition number diverges, and arbitrarily small data perturbations may cause order-one trial changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An implicitly computed trial becomes ill-conditioned when its defining equation is nearly flat with respect to the trial parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is continuously differentiable near the proposal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(Q_\alpha\to0\) while \(\lVert Q_z\rVert\not\to0\), then \(\kappa\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: vector of sampled values, derivatives, and endpoints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The implicit-function derivative and local condition-number formula are standard, but no source is supplied. Moreover, divergence of local derivatives along a sequence does not by itself establish that arbitrarily small perturbations cause order-one changes without uniform control of neighborhoods and nonlinear remainders.

children.title: Proposal Safeguard Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Limits beyond which trial-step safeguards no longer prevent unstable proposals.

knowledge_statements.title: Proposal Safeguard Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of uniform bracket contraction when interior proposal safeguards fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the current bracket be \([\ell,u]\) with width \(w=u-\ell>0\). If every proposal satisfies \[\ell+\tau w\le\alpha\le u-\tau w\] for a fixed \(\tau\in(0,1/2]\), then replacing either endpoint by \(\alpha\) produces a new bracket of width at most \((1-\tau)w\). If no uniform \(\tau>0\) is enforced, proposals may satisfy \((\alpha_j-\ell_j)/w_j\to0\) or \((u_j-\alpha_j)/w_j\to0\). Endpoint replacement can then yield \(w_{j+1}/w_j\to1\), so uniform geometric contraction and finite tolerance termination are no longer guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interior safeguards ensure geometric bracket contraction; proposals arbitrarily near an endpoint can make contraction ratios approach one.
assumptions_latex: \([\ell,u]\) is a valid line-search bracket with \(u>\ell\).
Each update retains one endpoint and replaces the other by the proposal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A fixed interior margin gives \(w_{+}\le(1-\tau)w\); loss of that margin permits \(w_{j+1}/w_j\to1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Roundoff-Limited Acceptance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo decision boundary under bounded function-evaluation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let computed values satisfy \(\widehat f(y)=f(y)+e_y\) with \(|e_y|\le\varepsilon_f\). For an exact directional derivative \(d=\nabla f(x)^\top p<0\), define the exact and computed Armijo margins by \[M(\alpha)=f(x)+c_1\alpha d-f(x+\alpha p),\qquad \widehat M(\alpha)=\widehat f(x)+c_1\alpha d-\widehat f(x+\alpha p).\] Then \(|\widehat M(\alpha)-M(\alpha)|\le2\varepsilon_f\). Therefore \(M(\alpha)>2\varepsilon_f\) guarantees computed acceptance and \(M(\alpha)<-2\varepsilon_f\) guarantees computed rejection. If \(|M(\alpha)|<2\varepsilon_f\), admissible errors can produce either decision; when \(|M(\alpha)|=2\varepsilon_f\), the computed margin can reach the decision boundary. Function values satisfying only this error model cannot robustly classify trials in that uncertainty band.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computed Armijo decision is robust only when the exact margin lies more than twice the function-evaluation error away from zero; inside that band, admissible errors can change the decision.
assumptions_latex: \(|\widehat f(y)-f(y)|\le\varepsilon_f\) at the base and trial points.
\(d=\nabla f(x)^\top p<0\) is treated as exact.
Computed acceptance is determined by \(\widehat M(\alpha)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sign of the computed margin is guaranteed only when \(|M(\alpha)|>2\varepsilon_f\); for \(|M(\alpha)|<2\varepsilon_f\), both signs are compatible with the error model.

notation.meaning: exact directional derivative at the base point

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi(\alpha)=f(x+\alpha p)\), where \(\phi'(0)<0\), and fix \(c_1\in(0,1)\). Define the exact Armijo residual \(R(\alpha)=\phi(\alpha)-\phi(0)-c_1\alpha\phi'(0)\), so acceptance requires \(R(\alpha)\leq0\). Suppose computed quantities satisfy absolute error bounds \(|\widehat\phi(\alpha)-\phi(\alpha)|\leq e_\alpha\), \(|\widehat\phi(0)-\phi(0)|\leq e_0\), and \(|\widehat{\phi'(0)}-\phi'(0)|\leq e_d\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition addresses finite-precision ambiguity in sufficient-decrease testing. It does not assert that the step satisfies a curvature condition, nor does it cover stochastic evaluation noise without deterministic error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[\widehat R(\alpha)=\widehat\phi(\alpha)-\widehat\phi(0)-c_1\alpha\widehat{\phi'(0)},\qquad E(\alpha)=e_\alpha+e_0+c_1\alpha e_d.\] Acceptance is roundoff-limited at \(\alpha>0\) when the uncertainty interval for the exact residual intersects both acceptance and rejection regions: \[|\widehat R(\alpha)|\leq E(\alpha).\] Equivalently, \(0\in[\widehat R(\alpha)-E(\alpha),\widehat R(\alpha)+E(\alpha)]\), so the signs \(R(\alpha)\leq0\) and \(R(\alpha)>0\) cannot be certified from the computed data and stated error bounds. A particularly visible case is \(\widehat\phi(\alpha)=\widehat\phi(0)\) while the required decrease \(-c_1\alpha\widehat{\phi'(0)}\) is comparable to the evaluation uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Armijo decision is roundoff-limited when its computed residual is no larger in magnitude than its total error bound. In that case the interval of possible exact residuals crosses zero, so the available floating-point values cannot certify either acceptance or rejection. Equality of the computed trial and current function values near a solution is a common special case.
assumptions_latex: The bounds \(e_\alpha,e_0,e_d\geq0\) cover all errors used in the acceptance residual.
The decision is based on the computed Armijo residual \(\widehat R(\alpha)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The roundoff-limited set is \(\mathcal R=\{\alpha>0:|\widehat R(\alpha)|\leq E(\alpha)\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\alpha\in\mathcal R\) if and only if \(0\in[\widehat R(\alpha)-E(\alpha),\widehat R(\alpha)+E(\alpha)]\).
A certified acceptance requires \(\widehat R(\alpha)+E(\alpha)\leq0\); a certified rejection requires \(\widehat R(\alpha)-E(\alpha)>0\).
special_cases_latex: If the derivative error is neglected, then \(E(\alpha)=e_\alpha+e_0\).
If \(\widehat x(\alpha)=x\), the computed function values normally coincide and the trial cannot demonstrate a nonzero representable decrease.
immediate_consequences_latex: Repeated contraction need not resolve the decision because the requested Armijo decrease also tends to zero with \(\alpha\).
A forced acceptance or rejection inside \(\mathcal R\) is a policy decision rather than a conclusion certified by the error model.
boundary_notes: The definition requires explicit error bounds; machine epsilon alone is not an error bound for an arbitrary function evaluator.
The exact step may be acceptable or unacceptable—the defining condition is numerical undecidability, not either exact outcome.

notation.meaning: Absolute uncertainty bound for the residual.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi:[0,\alpha_{\max}]\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable with \(\phi'(0)<0\). A strong-Wolfe zoom procedure maintains endpoints \(\alpha_{\mathrm{lo}},\alpha_{\mathrm{hi}}\) whose bounded interval contains acceptable steps and generates an interior trial \(\alpha_j\). Let \(\operatorname{next}(a,b)\) denote the least representable number strictly larger than \(a\) toward \(b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition concerns failure of the zoom mechanism at the boundary of finite representability, assuming the mathematical bracket invariants remain valid. It excludes an incorrectly formed bracket and exact nonexistence of strong-Wolfe steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A zoom state lies on the bracket-zoom failure boundary when no representable interior trial remains, \[\operatorname{next}(\min\{\alpha_{\mathrm{lo}},\alpha_{\mathrm{hi}}\},\max\{\alpha_{\mathrm{lo}},\alpha_{\mathrm{hi}}\})=\max\{\alpha_{\mathrm{lo}},\alpha_{\mathrm{hi}}\},\] or, equivalently for the working arithmetic, every computed proposal satisfies \(\widehat\alpha_j\in\{\alpha_{\mathrm{lo}},\alpha_{\mathrm{hi}}\}\), while neither endpoint has been certified to satisfy the strong Wolfe conditions. More generally, with a relative stopping threshold \(\tau_\alpha>0\), the practical boundary is \[\frac{|\alpha_{\mathrm{hi}}-\alpha_{\mathrm{lo}}|}{\max\{1,|\alpha_{\mathrm{lo}}|,|\alpha_{\mathrm{hi}}|\}}\leq\tau_\alpha\] together with failure to certify an acceptable endpoint or interior trial. A bracket-zoom failure is termination at this boundary without returning a strong-Wolfe step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bracket-and-zoom search reaches its failure boundary when the current endpoints are adjacent at the working precision, or their relative separation is below \(\tau_\alpha\), and no endpoint has been certified acceptable. At exact adjacency every computed interior proposal equals an endpoint, so zoom cannot shrink the interval or produce a new sample. Termination there without a strong-Wolfe step is a bracket-zoom failure.
assumptions_latex: The bracket invariants of the strong-Wolfe zoom procedure hold before the boundary is reached.
Neither endpoint is already certified to satisfy both strong Wolfe inequalities.
Trial steps and endpoints are represented in a fixed finite-precision number system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The failure boundary is the set of unresolved zoom states with no representable safeguarded interior point, or with relative width at most \(\tau_\alpha\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Exact representable adjacency is equivalent to the open interval between the endpoints containing no floating-point number.
With a safeguard fraction \(\eta>0\), the boundary is reached earlier if the safeguarded interior contains no representable number.
special_cases_latex: Bisection stagnates when the rounded midpoint equals an endpoint.
Cubic or quadratic interpolation stagnates when its safeguarded and rounded proposal equals an endpoint.
immediate_consequences_latex: At representable adjacency, another zoom iteration using the same arithmetic and endpoints cannot create a distinct interior trial.
The bracket may still contain an acceptable real step; the failure is inability to resolve it numerically.
boundary_notes: Small interval width alone is successful termination only when an accepted-step or approximate-stationarity policy explicitly permits it.
Loss of bracket invariants before stagnation is a logical bracket failure, not the representability boundary defined here.

notation.meaning: Next representable number after a toward b.

children.title: Bracketing Failure Modes
children.top_down_role: Cases where the search cannot establish a usable interval for refinement.

knowledge_statements.title: Bracketing Failure Modes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure to obtain a finite strong-Wolfe bracket during expansion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable with \(\phi'(0)<0\), and let \(0<c_1<c_2<1\). A standard expansion phase can continue while every tested \(\alpha_j\) satisfies Armijo decrease and \(\phi'(\alpha_j)<0\), because neither excessive value nor derivative sign reversal supplies a bracket. The concrete function \(\phi(\alpha)=-\alpha\) satisfies \[\phi(\alpha)\le\phi(0)+c_1\alpha\phi'(0),\qquad \lvert\phi'(\alpha)\rvert=1>c_2\lvert\phi'(0)\rvert\] for every \(\alpha>0\). Thus no finite expansion produces a strong-Wolfe point or a derivative-sign bracket.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function decreasing linearly forever passes Armijo but never satisfies strong curvature or produces a derivative-sign bracket.
assumptions_latex: Expansion seeks a finite bracket supporting a strong-Wolfe search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(\phi(\alpha)=-\alpha\), finite expansion cannot bracket or locate a strong-Wolfe step.

children.title: Zoom Stagnation Modes
children.top_down_role: Cases where bracket refinement ceases to make useful progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Zoom Stagnation Modes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested-bracket stagnation caused by asymptotically endpoint-adjacent zoom trials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let zoom maintain nested brackets \([\ell_j,u_j]\) of widths \(w_j=u_j-\ell_j>0\). Suppose an update retains \(u_j\) and sets \(\ell_{j+1}=\alpha_j\), \(u_{j+1}=u_j\), where \(\alpha_j=\ell_j+\eta_jw_j\) and \(0<\eta_j<1\). Then \[w_{j+1}=(1-\eta_j)w_j,\qquad w_j=w_0\prod_{i=0}^{j-1}(1-\eta_i).\] If \(\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\eta_i<\infty\), this product has a positive limit, so the bracket never reaches any smaller width tolerance. The symmetric failure occurs for trials approaching the upper endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zoom can stagnate at positive bracket width when endpoint-adjacent trial fractions are summable, even though every update strictly shrinks the interval.
assumptions_latex: Zoom brackets are nested and have positive widths.
The indicated update replaces exactly one endpoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i\eta_i<\infty\) implies \(\lim_{j\to\infty}w_j>0\), so width-based zoom termination can fail.

notation.meaning: width of the zoom bracket at iteration \(j\)
relative distance of the proposal from the replaced endpoint

children.title: Interval-Contraction Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Numerical or geometric obstacles to meaningful reduction of the search interval.

knowledge_statements.title: Interval-Contraction Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction between uniform contraction and merely strict interval shrinkage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \([\ell_j,u_j]\) be nested closed intervals with widths \(w_j=u_j-\ell_j>0\). A uniform contraction \(w_{j+1}\le q w_j\) for some fixed \(q\in(0,1)\) implies \(w_j\le q^jw_0\). Consequently, for every tolerance \(\varepsilon\) satisfying \(0<\varepsilon<w_0\), termination with \(w_j\le\varepsilon\) occurs after at most \[\left\lceil\frac{\log(w_0/\varepsilon)}{\log(1/q)}\right\rceil\] updates. Strict decrease alone is insufficient: the nested intervals \([0,1+1/(j+1)]\) satisfy \(w_{j+1}<w_j\) and \(w_{j+1}/w_j\to1\), yet their widths converge to \(1\), not to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform contraction guarantees finite termination below every tolerance smaller than the initial width, whereas strict interval shrinkage alone may leave a positive limiting width.
assumptions_latex: The intervals are nested and closed, with \(w_j>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A fixed factor \(q\in(0,1)\) yields geometric termination, whereas strict shrinkage with ratios approaching \(1\) can stagnate at positive width.

children.title: Bracketed-Search Termination Boundary
children.top_down_role: Conditions requiring unsuccessful termination of the bracketed search.

knowledge_statements.title: Bracketed-Search Termination Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical termination boundary for a bracket-and-zoom line search seeking an acceptable trial step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi(\alpha)=f(x+\alpha d)\), where \(d\) is a descent direction, and let \([a_j,b_j]\) be the current bracket. A bracketed search reaches its numerical termination boundary without success when no accepted step has been found and either \[b_j-a_j\leq \tau_{\mathrm{abs}}+\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{|a_j|,|b_j|\},\] every representable interior trial equals an endpoint, or all permitted trials or evaluations have been exhausted. Returning an endpoint as a successful step is valid only if that endpoint independently satisfies the stated acceptance conditions; bracket contraction alone is not an acceptance certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zoom fails numerically when its bracket cannot be contracted or sampled further before an acceptable step is found; a bracket endpoint is not automatically acceptable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{boundary reached}\not\Rightarrow\text{acceptance condition satisfied}\).

notation.meaning: one-dimensional objective along the search ray
