knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure Set of a Two-Term Nonlinear Conjugate-Gradient Recurrence
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), and \(p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}p_k\). The scalar \(\beta_{k+1}\) is supplied by a nonlinear-CG formula, and the line search is expected to satisfy conditions appropriate to that formula.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is an umbrella definition for deterministic two-term nonlinear conjugate-gradient methods. It isolates failures caused by the recurrence or its interaction with the line search, rather than generic function-evaluation or hardware failures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An iteration has a nonlinear-CG-specific failure when the two-term recurrence is not well posed or does not retain its required descent/progress property. Formally, define \[\mathsf F_k^{\mathrm{NCG}}=\mathsf F_k^{\mathrm{coef}}\cup\mathsf F_k^{\mathrm{desc}}\cup\mathsf F_k^{\mathrm{compat}}\cup\mathsf F_k^{\mathrm{prog}},\] where \[\mathsf F_k^{\mathrm{coef}}=\{\beta_{k+1}\notin\mathbb R\},\qquad \mathsf F_k^{\mathrm{desc}}=\{g_{k+1}^Tp_{k+1}\geq0\},\] \(\mathsf F_k^{\mathrm{compat}}\) is failure of the accepted \(\alpha_k\) to satisfy the line-search condition required for the selected \(\beta\)-formula, and, for declared \(\eta,\tau>0\), \[\mathsf F_k^{\mathrm{prog}}=\left\{\frac{-g_k^Tp_k}{\|g_k\|\|p_k\|}\leq\eta,\ \|\alpha_kp_k\|\leq\tau,\ \|g_k\|>\varepsilon_g\right\}.\] Thus the class comprises undefined coefficients, loss of descent, formula–line-search incompatibility, and nonstationary near-orthogonal tiny-step stagnation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear-CG-specific failure occurs when the recurrence coefficient is undefined or nonfinite, the new direction is not a descent direction, the accepted step fails the line-search requirement needed by the chosen coefficient formula, or the method takes a tiny step along a direction nearly orthogonal to steepest descent while the gradient remains non-small. These events form the union \(\mathsf F_k^{\mathrm{NCG}}\).
assumptions_latex: \(g_k\neq0\) whenever the directional-angle diagnostic is evaluated.
The nonlinear-CG variant specifies both a formula for \(\beta_{k+1}\) and its required line-search conditions.
The progress thresholds \(\eta,\tau,\varepsilon_g\) are fixed diagnostic parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Iteration \(k\) is in the nonlinear-CG-specific failure set exactly when \(\mathsf F_k^{\mathrm{NCG}}\) occurs.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Loss of descent is equivalently failure of \(-g_{k+1}^Tp_{k+1}>0\).
For finite \(\beta_{k+1}\), \(g_{k+1}^Tp_{k+1}=-\|g_{k+1}\|^2+\beta_{k+1}g_{k+1}^Tp_k\), making the recurrence-specific descent test explicit.
special_cases_latex: For Fletcher–Reeves, strong Wolfe with \(c_2<1/2\) supplies the standard descent-compatible regime.
For unmodified Polak–Ribière, the ordinary strong Wolfe conditions alone do not guarantee descent.
For Hestenes–Stiefel and Dai–Yuan formulas, a vanishing or tiny \(y_k^Tp_k\) triggers \(\mathsf F_k^{\mathrm{coef}}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A restart \(p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}\) removes coefficient undefinedness and restores strict descent whenever \(g_{k+1}\neq0\).
Generic line-search roundoff may coexist with, but is not by itself, an NCG-specific failure.
boundary_notes: The union is a failure taxonomy; its components need not be mutually exclusive.
A negative \(\beta_{k+1}\) is not automatically a failure unless the chosen variant forbids it or descent/progress is lost.

notation.meaning: Gradient at the kth nonlinear-CG iterate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Near-Orthogonal Tiny-Step Regime in Nonlinear CG
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) be a nonlinear conjugate-gradient iteration for a continuously differentiable \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), with \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\neq0\). Define the descent-angle cosine \(\chi_k=-g_k^Tp_k/(\|g_k\|\|p_k\|)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition captures lack of practical progress while the method remains away from its gradient stopping condition. It is diagnostic and threshold-relative; it does not claim mathematical divergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(m\in\mathbb N\), \(\eta\in(0,1)\), \(\tau_x>0\), and \(\varepsilon_g>0\). The method is in an \((m,\eta,\tau_x,\varepsilon_g)\) progress-failure regime starting at \(k\) when, for every \(r=0,\ldots,m-1\), \[0<\chi_{k+r}\leq\eta,\qquad \frac{\|x_{k+r+1}-x_{k+r}\|}{\max\{1,\|x_{k+r}\|\}}\leq\tau_x,\qquad \|g_{k+r}\|>\varepsilon_g.\] The first inequality says the direction is descent but nearly orthogonal to \(-g_{k+r}\); the second says the accepted displacement is tiny; and the third excludes termination near a stationary point. For Fletcher–Reeves, the associated persistence mechanism is characterized by \(g_{k+1}\approx g_k\), \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{FR}}\approx1\), and hence \(p_{k+1}\approx p_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear-CG progress-failure regime is a block of \(m\) iterations in which every direction remains a descent direction but is nearly orthogonal to steepest descent, every accepted displacement is relatively tiny, and every gradient norm stays above \(\varepsilon_g\). For Fletcher–Reeves, a tiny step can leave consecutive gradients nearly equal, make \(\beta^{\mathrm{FR}}\) close to one, and reproduce the poor direction on the next iteration.
assumptions_latex: The iteration uses the two-term nonlinear-CG recurrence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The progress-failure regime is the intersection, over \(r=0,\ldots,m-1\), of the near-orthogonality, tiny-displacement, and nonstationarity events.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Near orthogonality is \(-g_k^Tp_k\leq\eta\|g_k\|\|p_k\|\) with \(g_k^Tp_k<0\).
For Fletcher–Reeves, \(g_{k+1}\approx g_k\) implies \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{FR}}=\|g_{k+1}\|^2/\|g_k\|^2\approx1\).
special_cases_latex: Setting \(m=1\) defines a single progress-failure iteration.
Periodic or adaptive restart terminates the persistence condition by replacing the inherited direction with \(-g_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The regime does not satisfy a gradient-based convergence test because \(\|g_{k+r}\|>\varepsilon_g\).
A restart gives \(\chi_k=1\) whenever \(g_k\neq0\), so it exits the near-orthogonal component for every \(\eta<1\).
boundary_notes: Small steps near a stationary point are excluded by the gradient threshold.
A single poor step is not persistent failure when \(m>1\).

notation.meaning: Cosine of the angle between the search direction and negative gradient.
Required number of consecutive deficient-progress iterations.

children.title: Nonlinear-CG Jamming Regimes
children.top_down_role: Direction or coefficient behavior associated with repeatedly ineffective nonlinear-CG progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear-CG Jamming Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observable progress-failure regime for nonlinear conjugate-gradient iterations away from stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k d_k\) with \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k\). The iteration is in a jamming regime on an infinite index set \(K\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) if there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(\|g_k\|\geq\varepsilon\) for every \(k\in K\), while \(\alpha_k\|d_k\|\to0\) and \(f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\to0\) as \(k\to\infty\) through \(K\). When \(d_k\neq0\), the additional behavior \(-g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k/(\|g_k\|\|d_k\|)\to0\) along \(K\) is a directional indicator that can accompany jamming, but it neither implies the two vanishing-progress conditions by itself nor proves convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlinear CG is jammed along an infinite subsequence when gradients stay bounded away from zero while accepted displacements and objective decreases vanish. Near-orthogonality of the directions to the negative gradients can accompany this regime but is not sufficient by itself to establish it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{k\in K}\|g_k\|>0\) together with subsequentially vanishing displacement and objective decrease constitutes nonstationary jamming.

children.title: Stagnation Indicators
children.top_down_role: Observable evidence that iterates, objective values, or gradients have ceased useful progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Stagnation Indicators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window diagnostic certificate for suspected nonlinear-CG stagnation, not a stationarity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a window \(W_k=\{k-m+1,\ldots,k\}\), define \[S_x=\max_{i\in W_k}\frac{\|x_{i+1}-x_i\|}{1+\|x_i\|},\qquad S_f=\max_{i\in W_k}\frac{|f(x_{i+1})-f(x_i)|}{1+|f(x_i)|}.\] The window certifies suspected nonstationary stagnation when \(S_x\leq\tau_x\), \(S_f\leq\tau_f\), and \(\min_{i\in W_k}\|g_i\|>\tau_g\). These inequalities are directly verifiable from stored iterates, values, and gradients. They certify negligible recorded progress with gradients above tolerance, but do not certify that no lower objective value exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small relative step and objective changes over a window, combined with gradients above tolerance, certify suspected nonstationary stagnation but not optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(m\geq1\) and all quantities in the window are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_x\leq\tau_x\), \(S_f\leq\tau_f\), and \(\min_{i\in W_k}\|g_i\|>\tau_g\) certify suspected stagnation.

notation.meaning: largest relative displacement in the window
largest relative objective change in the window

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Responsiveness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery property obtained by replacing a defective nonlinear-CG direction with steepest descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be open, let \(f:D	o\mathbb{R}\), and at a restart iteration set \(d_k=-g_k\), where \(g_k=
abla f(x_k)\). If \(g_k
eq0\), then \(g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k=-\|g_k\|^2<0\). If \(
abla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on every tested segment contained in \(D\), every tested \(\alpha\) satisfying \[0<\alpha\leq  rac{2(1-c_1)}{L}\] and \([x_k,x_k+\alpha d_k]\subset D\) satisfies the Armijo inequality \(f(x_k+\alpha d_k)\leq f(x_k)+c_1\alpha g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\). Consequently, if sufficiently small tested segments remain in \(D\), geometric backtracking from any finite positive initial step accepts after finitely many reductions in exact arithmetic. Operational responsiveness can fail if gradients or function values are unusable, the tested ray is truncated by the admissible domain, or finite-precision safeguards prevent reaching such a step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A steepest-descent restart restores strict descent and permits finite Armijo backtracking under local smoothness when sufficiently small tested segments remain in the admissible domain; evaluation, domain, or numerical limitations can still prevent operational acceptance.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is open, \(x_k\in D\), and \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient on the tested segments.
Backtracking multiplies the trial step by a fixed factor in \((0,1)\), and sufficiently small tested segments remain in \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restarting with \(d_k=-g_k\) restores descent and finite Armijo acceptance in exact arithmetic under the stated segment and domain hypotheses.

children.title: Persistent-Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cases where restart or safeguarding does not restore productive progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating recoverable nonlinear-CG direction failure from failure persisting after restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear-CG progress failure is persistent at iteration \(k\) if the original direction is rejected or unusable, a restart sets \(d_k=-g_k\), and no admissible representable trial step produces a finite value satisfying Armijo before the prescribed evaluation or step-size limit. For differentiable \(f\) with locally Lipschitz gradient, an interior point \(x_k\), and \(g_k\neq0\), arbitrarily small positive steps along \(-g_k\) satisfy Armijo in exact arithmetic. Hence persistent post-restart failure identifies departure from these conditions—such as domain truncation, nonfinite evaluation, inconsistent derivatives, finite-precision resolution, or an externally imposed minimum step—rather than an inherent nonlinear-CG recurrence obstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure persisting after a steepest-descent restart signals evaluation, domain, derivative, precision, or resource limits rather than the CG recurrence alone.
assumptions_latex: The line search requires Armijo decrease with \(0<c_1<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistent post-restart failure implies that a smooth exact-arithmetic Armijo premise or an operational resource premise has failed.

notation.meaning: computed gradient at the restart point

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Loss of Conjugacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computed loss of the orthogonality or conjugacy relation used by nonlinear-CG recurrences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let computed quantities be denoted by hats. A finite-precision conjugacy-loss indicator is \[\rho_k=\frac{|\widehat g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}\widehat d_k|}{\|\widehat g_{k+1}\|\,\|\widehat d_k\|},\] whenever the denominator is nonzero. Under exact line minimization the corresponding directional derivative is zero, whereas rounding, inexact search, and cancellation can make \(\rho_k\) appreciable. If \(\rho_k>\eta\), with a chosen tolerance \(\eta\), the computed pair no longer satisfies the intended near-orthogonality test. This is a diagnostic boundary, not proof that all conjugacy notions have failed; a restart \(\widehat d_{k+1}=-\widehat g_{k+1}\) removes dependence on the contaminated previous direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A large normalized inner product between the new gradient and previous direction signals loss of intended line-search orthogonality and motivates restart.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k>\eta\) marks failure of the intended computed near-orthogonality relation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p_i,p_j\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\). For linear CG let \(G\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite. For nonlinear CG on the step from \(x_k\) to \(x_{k+1}\), let \(\bar G_k=\int_0^1\nabla^2f(x_k+t\alpha_kp_k)\,dt\) when this average Hessian exists. Let hats denote computed quantities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition measures loss relative to a declared symmetric positive-definite metric. In nonlinear CG it is normally applied locally or consecutively using \(\bar G_k\); global pairwise conjugacy is not generally expected for a nonquadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric positive-definite metric \(M\), define the normalized computed conjugacy defect \[\delta_M(\widehat p_i,\widehat p_j)=\frac{|\widehat p_i^TM\widehat p_j|}{\sqrt{(\widehat p_i^TM\widehat p_i)(\widehat p_j^TM\widehat p_j)}}.\] Exact \(M\)-conjugacy is \(p_i^TMp_j=0\). Given a tolerance \(\tau_c\in(0,1)\), finite-precision loss of conjugacy occurs for the pair \((i,j)\) when the method’s exact-arithmetic recurrence requires \(M\)-conjugacy but \[\delta_M(\widehat p_i,\widehat p_j)>\tau_c.\] For nonlinear Hestenes–Stiefel recurrence, the consecutive local metric is \(M=\bar G_k\), and the intended relation is \(p_{k+1}^T\bar G_kp_k=0\). For a block \(P=[p_{i_1},\ldots,p_{i_q}]\), loss may equivalently be monitored by an off-diagonal normalized Gram defect.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-precision loss of conjugacy occurs when directions that should be conjugate in exact arithmetic have a normalized metric inner product exceeding \(\tau_c\). The defect divides \(|\widehat p_i^TM\widehat p_j|\) by the two metric norms, making it scale-independent. Linear CG uses \(M=G\); a local nonlinear-CG test may use the average Hessian \(\bar G_k\) for consecutive directions.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is symmetric positive definite on the span of the tested directions.
The exact-arithmetic method asserts \(p_i^TMp_j=0\) for the tested pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Loss of conjugacy is the event \(\delta_M(\widehat p_i,\widehat p_j)>\tau_c\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a direction block \(P\), exact conjugacy means \(P^TMP\) is diagonal; loss is detected by a nonzero normalized off-diagonal entry above tolerance.
For consecutive nonlinear-CG directions, \(p_{k+1}^T\bar G_kp_k=0\) is equivalent to the Hestenes–Stiefel coefficient relation when its denominator is nonzero.
special_cases_latex: In exact linear CG on a positive-definite quadratic, all distinct generated directions are \(G\)-conjugate.
Rounding errors can destroy finite termination, so substantially more than \(n\) linear-CG iterations may be required.
immediate_consequences_latex: The diagnostic is invariant under nonzero rescaling of either tested direction.
A restart discards inherited direction information but does not retroactively restore conjugacy among earlier computed directions.
boundary_notes: Nonconjugacy caused by objective nonquadraticity or an inexact line search is not purely a finite-precision loss unless an exact-arithmetic reference recurrence predicts zero defect.
If \(M\) is indefinite, the displayed normalization may be undefined and a different defect measure is required.

notation.meaning: Normalized conjugacy defect in metric M.
Average Hessian along the kth accepted step.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Denominator Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical boundary where a nonlinear-CG coefficient denominator is zero or too small for reliable division.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\), common nonlinear-CG coefficients include \[\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{FR}}=\frac{\|g_{k+1}\|^2}{\|g_k\|^2},\qquad \beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{PR}}=\frac{g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}y_k}{\|g_k\|^2},\qquad \beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{HS}}=\frac{g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}y_k}{d_k^{\mathsf T}y_k}.\] A coefficient is denominator-degenerate when its denominator is zero, or numerically unsafe when its magnitude does not exceed a scale-aware threshold such as \(\tau_{\mathrm{den}}\|d_k\|\|y_k\|\) for the Hestenes–Stiefel denominator. In that regime division can amplify perturbations without bound; the coefficient must be rejected, safeguarded, or replaced by a restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlinear-CG coefficients become undefined or unstable when their gradient-norm or curvature denominator vanishes or is small relative to its natural scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A zero or scale-small denominator makes the corresponding computed \(\beta_{k+1}\) unreliable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scale-Relative Degeneracy of Nonlinear-CG Coefficient Denominators
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\), and \(p_k\neq0\). Several nonlinear-CG coefficients, including Hestenes–Stiefel and Dai–Yuan, divide by \(d_k=y_k^Tp_k\); the Hager–Zhang formula also uses this denominator more than once. Let \(u\) denote the working unit roundoff and \(\tau_d>0\) a chosen safety factor.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition applies to coefficient formulas containing \(y_k^Tp_k\). It does not apply directly to Fletcher–Reeves or Polak–Ribière denominators \(\|g_k\|^2\), except through the analogous norm-squared criterion stated as a special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The denominator \(d_k=y_k^Tp_k\) is exactly degenerate when \(d_k=0\). It is numerically degenerate relative to \(\tau_d\) when \[|d_k|\leq\tau_d\|y_k\|\|p_k\|.\] The ratio \[\kappa_{d,k}=\frac{|y_k^Tp_k|}{\|y_k\|\|p_k\|}\in[0,1]\] is the absolute cosine of the angle between \(y_k\) and \(p_k\); hence degeneracy is equivalently \(\kappa_{d,k}\leq\tau_d\). A nonlinear-CG coefficient-denominator failure occurs when a formula requiring division by \(d_k\) is evaluated in this set without a prescribed fallback, restart, or regularization. A roundoff-scaled choice has \(\tau_d=\gamma u\) for a declared \(\gamma\geq1\), though larger tolerances may be required by the error model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient-denominator degeneracy occurs when \(y_k^Tp_k\) is zero or small relative to \(\|y_k\|\|p_k\|\). The normalized magnitude \(\kappa_{d,k}\) is the absolute cosine between the gradient change and the old direction, so the test is scale-independent. It becomes a coefficient failure when a nonlinear-CG formula divides by the degenerate quantity without using a fallback.
assumptions_latex: The selected nonlinear-CG formula contains the denominator \(y_k^Tp_k\).
The tolerance \(\tau_d\in(0,1)\) is declared before evaluation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The degeneracy set is \(\mathcal D_k=\{|y_k^Tp_k|\leq\tau_d\|y_k\|\|p_k\|\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For nonzero \(y_k,p_k\), \(\mathcal D_k\) is equivalent to \(\kappa_{d,k}\leq\tau_d\).
Exact degeneracy is equivalent to orthogonality \(y_k\perp p_k\).
special_cases_latex: For Hestenes–Stiefel, \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{HS}}=g_{k+1}^Ty_k/(y_k^Tp_k)\).
For Dai–Yuan, \(\beta_{k+1}^{\mathrm{DY}}=\|g_{k+1}\|^2/(y_k^Tp_k)\).
For a denominator \(\|g_k\|^2\), the analogous exact degeneracy is \(g_k=0\), normally a stationarity condition rather than a breakdown.
immediate_consequences_latex: Near degeneracy can magnify perturbations in the numerator or denominator and produce an extremely large computed \(\beta_{k+1}\).
Setting \(\beta_{k+1}=0\) supplies a well-defined steepest-descent restart whenever \(g_{k+1}\neq0\).
boundary_notes: A small numerator may cancel the effect of a small denominator in exact arithmetic, but direct quotient evaluation remains ill-conditioned without a joint rule.
The sign condition supplied by Wolfe line searches does not by itself guarantee a comfortable finite-precision separation from zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compatibility Failure Between an NCG Recurrence and Its Accepted Step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}p_k\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). For a chosen coefficient rule \(B\), let \(\mathcal L_B(x_k,p_k)\) denote the set of step lengths satisfying the line-search conditions used to guarantee the rule’s required descent or convergence property.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition is formula-relative: different nonlinear-CG coefficients require different line-search conditions. It concerns acceptance of an incompatible step, not failure of a compatible line-search routine to terminate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonlinear-CG line-search compatibility failure occurs at iteration \(k\) when the line search accepts \(\alpha_k>0\) but \[\alpha_k\notin\mathcal L_B(x_k,p_k),\] and the missing condition is required for the selected recurrence’s stated descent or convergence regime. For Fletcher–Reeves, the standard compatible set is the strong-Wolfe set with \(0<c_1<c_2<1/2\): \[f(x_k+\alpha p_k)\leq f(x_k)+c_1\alpha g_k^Tp_k,\qquad |g(x_k+\alpha p_k)^Tp_k|\leq-c_2g_k^Tp_k.\] Hence accepting an Armijo-only step, or a step with the curvature inequality violated, is an FR compatibility failure. The realized failure is loss of descent, \[g_{k+1}^Tp_{k+1}=-\|g_{k+1}\|^2+\beta_{k+1}g_{k+1}^Tp_k\geq0.\] Compatibility failure and realized loss of descent are distinct: the former records absence of the guarantee, while the latter records its adverse outcome.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A line search is incompatible with a nonlinear-CG recurrence when it accepts a step outside the step set required by that coefficient formula’s descent or convergence result. For Fletcher–Reeves, compatibility requires strong Wolfe conditions with \(c_2<1/2\); Armijo decrease alone is insufficient. An incompatible step may then yield a new direction with \(g_{k+1}^Tp_{k+1}\geq0\), although incompatibility is recorded even if descent happens accidentally.
assumptions_latex: The chosen coefficient rule \(B\) has an explicitly stated compatible line-search set \(\mathcal L_B\).
The line search returns an accepted positive step \(\alpha_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The compatibility-failure event is \(\mathsf{CF}_k^B=\{\alpha_k>0:\alpha_k\notin\mathcal L_B(x_k,p_k)\}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For Fletcher–Reeves, compatibility is satisfaction of both inequalities (5.43) with \(c_2<1/2\).
Realized descent failure is equivalent to \(\beta_{k+1}g_{k+1}^Tp_k\geq\|g_{k+1}\|^2\).
special_cases_latex: Exact line search gives \(g_{k+1}^Tp_k=0\), so every finite Fletcher–Reeves coefficient yields \(g_{k+1}^Tp_{k+1}=-\|g_{k+1}\|^2<0\) when \(g_{k+1}\neq0\).
Ordinary strong Wolfe does not by itself guarantee descent for unmodified Polak–Ribière; PR+ requires an appropriate modified line-search argument.
Dai–Yuan and Hager–Zhang-type formulas admit descent guarantees under Wolfe conditions stated for those formulas.
immediate_consequences_latex: A steepest-descent restart sets \(p_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}\) and restores descent independently of the inherited coefficient.
Satisfying Armijo decrease alone does not control the cross term \(g_{k+1}^Tp_k\) in the next-direction descent identity.
boundary_notes: A stricter-than-required line search is compatible if it implies every required condition.
The definition does not claim that every incompatible accepted step causes divergence; it identifies loss of the applicable guarantee.

notation.meaning: Step lengths compatible with nonlinear-CG coefficient rule B.

source_refs.locator: Section 5.2, equations (5.42)–(5.45) and surrounding discussion: inexact searches may produce ascent directions; Fletcher–Reeves uses strong Wolfe with c2<1/2; ordinary strong Wolfe does not guarantee descent for unmodified Polak–Ribière

children.title: Acceptance-Rule Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Incompatibility between a nonlinear-CG family and the selected line-search acceptance rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Acceptance-Rule Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mismatch between the implemented line-search acceptance predicate and the predicate required by nonlinear-CG analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k(\alpha)\) be the implemented acceptance predicate and \(R_k(\alpha)\) the predicate required by the selected nonlinear-CG coefficient or convergence result. An acceptance-rule mismatch occurs when there exists a trial step \(\alpha>0\) such that \[A_k(\alpha)=\mathrm{true}\quad\text{and}\quad R_k(\alpha)=\mathrm{false}.\] In particular, Armijo decrease alone may accept a step that fails the curvature or strong-Wolfe inequality required to control \(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}d_k\). The accepted iterate is then valid for the implemented rule, but any descent or convergence claim whose hypotheses include \(R_k\) cannot be invoked for that iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mismatch exists when the implementation accepts a step that fails the stronger line-search condition assumed by the nonlinear-CG update or convergence result.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k\) and \(R_k\) are predicates on positive trial steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_k(\alpha_k)\not\Rightarrow R_k(\alpha_k)\) invalidates application of the result at iteration \(k\).

children.title: Curvature-Control Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Incompatibility between nonlinear-CG direction behavior and line-search curvature control.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Control Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by insufficient control of the post-step directional derivative used in nonlinear-CG descent arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\phi(\alpha)=f(x_k+\alpha d_k)\), the strong-Wolfe curvature condition requires \[|\phi'(\alpha_k)|\leq c_2|\phi'(0)|,\qquad 0<c_1<c_2<1.\] A curvature-control mismatch occurs when the line search enforces only sufficient decrease, or enforces a different curvature bound, while the nonlinear-CG update assumes the displayed inequality or a stricter range of \(c_2\). Then \(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}d_k\) lacks the assumed bound, so the recurrence \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k\) need not inherit the descent estimate used by that analysis. Acceptance remains possible, but the claimed directional control is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the line search provides weaker curvature control than the nonlinear-CG analysis requires, the next recurrence direction need not satisfy its asserted descent bound.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable along the search ray.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of the required curvature inequality removes the associated bound on \(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}d_k\).

notation.meaning: objective restricted to the search ray

children.title: Coefficient Sensitivity to Accepted Steps
children.top_down_role: Dependence of nonlinear-CG coefficients on the quality or placement of accepted steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Sensitivity to Accepted Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of a nonlinear-CG coefficient on the gradient produced by the accepted step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the Polak–Ribière coefficient, define \[B(u;g_k)=\frac{u^{\mathsf T}(u-g_k)}{\|g_k\|^2},\qquad g_k\neq0.\] If two accepted steps produce gradients \(u\) and \(v\), then \[|B(u;g_k)-B(v;g_k)|\leq\frac{(\|u\|+\|v\|+\|g_k\|)\|u-v\|}{\|g_k\|^2}.\] Thus small changes in an accepted step can substantially change the coefficient when the resulting gradients differ appreciably or \(\|g_k\|^2\) is small. Because \(d_{k+1}=-u+B(u;g_k)d_k\), the same acceptance perturbation is transmitted to the next direction and may change its descent status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Polak–Ribière coefficient depends continuously but potentially sharply on the gradient at the accepted step, especially when the previous gradient norm is small.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coefficient sensitivity scales at most as \((\|u\|+\|v\|+\|g_k\|)/\|g_k\|^2\) with the gradient perturbation.

notation.meaning: Polak–Ribière coefficient as a function of the accepted gradient
gradients resulting from two accepted steps

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling Failure Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequences when line-search acceptance and nonlinear-CG coefficient assumptions cease to support each other.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a line search accepts \(\alpha_k\), computes \(g_{k+1}\), and forms \(d_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}d_k\). If the accepted step does not provide the curvature or denominator bounds required by the coefficient formula, then \[g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}d_{k+1}=-\|g_{k+1}\|^2+\beta_{k+1}g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}d_k\] may be nonnegative or numerically indeterminate. In that event the next direction is not certified as a descent direction, ordinary Armijo termination arguments do not apply to it, and convergence results requiring gradient-related directions or Wolfe-compatible coefficients become inapplicable. A descent test followed by coefficient safeguarding or restart is therefore required before continuing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Broken line-search/coefficient coupling can yield a non-descent or undefined next direction, invalidating standard line-search termination and nonlinear-CG convergence arguments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without the required coupling bounds, \(g_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}d_{k+1}<0\) is not guaranteed.

children.title: Robustness Recovery Regimes
children.top_down_role: Chapter-native regimes in which safeguards or recovery mechanisms can restore productive behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Robustness Recovery Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions under which safeguarding and restart restore standard global first-order line-search progress after detected direction failures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a line-search method that replaces every nonfinite, denominator-degenerate, or insufficiently descending candidate direction by \(d_k=-g_k\), and otherwise retains only directions satisfying \[-g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\geq\sigma\|g_k\|\|d_k\|,\qquad \sigma>0.\] Suppose every accepted step satisfies the Armijo and Wolfe conditions, including any step produced by a fallback search. If \(f\) is bounded below on the initial level set and \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz continuous on an open neighborhood of that level set, then the Zoutendijk condition and the displayed uniform angle bound imply \(\|g_k\|\to0\). In particular, \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|g_k\|=0\). This recovery result does not by itself imply convergence of the iterate sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart, coefficient safeguards, a uniform descent-angle test, and Armijo–Wolfe acceptance recover convergence of the gradient norms to zero under smoothness and lower-bounded-level-set assumptions; convergence of the iterates requires additional assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuously differentiable, is bounded below on the initial level set, and has Lipschitz-continuous gradient on an open neighborhood of that level set.
Accepted steps satisfy Armijo sufficient decrease and Wolfe curvature conditions.
Every accepted direction satisfies \(-g_k^{\mathsf T}d_k\geq\sigma\|g_k\|\|d_k\|\) for a fixed \(\sigma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to0\), and hence \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\|\nabla f(x_k)\|=0\).

children.title: Cross-Mechanism Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Failures arising from interactions among direction quality, line-search numerics, and nonlinear-CG behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Mechanism Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of either direction quality or step acceptance destroys the standard line-search globalization guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider iterations \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k p_k\) for a continuously differentiable objective \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), with \(\alpha_k>0\). Global descent guarantees require compatible safeguards on both the direction and the accepted step. Neither safeguard compensates universally for loss of the other. For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\), \(x_0=1\), and \(p_0=1\), the direction is not descent and \(f(x_0+\alpha p_0)>f(x_0)\) for every \(\alpha>0\). Conversely, with the descent direction \(p_k=-x_k\) but an unsafeguarded fixed step \(\alpha_k=3\), one obtains \(x_{k+1}=-2x_k\), so \(f(x_{k+1})=4f(x_k)\) and the iterates diverge whenever \(x_0\ne0\). Thus direction descent alone and positive step length alone are each insufficient for globalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Line-search globalization can fail through either a non-descent direction or an inadequately safeguarded step; a correct mechanism cannot universally compensate for failure of the other.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without joint direction-quality and step-acceptance safeguards, monotone decrease and global convergence are not guaranteed.
